entry.summary: Studies spherical occupancy profiles distilled from multi-view 3D Gaussian reconstructions as a unified intermediate representation for both discriminative and generative 3D tasks, training a FiLM-conditioned profile decoder and a profile-VAE latent diffusion pipeline on Google Scanned Objects. Single-author exploratory work.

entry.title: Tolerance-Dependent Inspection Disagreement Between a Fixed CMM and a Portable Articulated-Arm CMM

author.name: Md Manjurul Ahsan, Hamidreza Samadi, Shivakumar Raman

entry.summary: Empirically examines when measurement disagreements between fixed coordinate measuring machines and portable articulated-arm CMMs cross part tolerance boundaries, using cylindrical, cubic, and spherical features at controlled temperatures. Provides guidance on instrument interchangeability decisions.

entry.title: PSA: We can do better

author.name: hersheys

entry.summary: Argues AI safety newcomers often choose work via vibes-based heuristics (conferences, pragmatic alignment) without deeply understanding core x-risk arguments, urging deeper problem comprehension before contributing.

entry.title: RIACT: A Responsible AI System for Personalized Study Habit Tracking and Early Burnout Signal Detection in University Students

author.name: Ria Sidhu

entry.summary: RIACT is a web application combining structured study-session logging with a hybrid AI architecture to give university students personalized insights and early burnout signals, addressing the retrospective nature of current burnout identification. The system emphasizes responsible-AI design principles.

entry.title: How Merge-Tolerant Are Vision Transformers for Wheat Phenotyping?

author.name: Simon Rav\'e, Pejman Rasti, David Rousseau

entry.summary: Systematic benchmark of training-free token merging (ToMe, Mutual Pair Merging) for ViTs in wheat phenotyping tasks, measuring quality-throughput-memory trade-offs including Raspberry Pi 5 edge inference. Reveals task-dependent merge tolerance hierarchies.

entry.title: HiFiC-G: Adapting HiFiC for Hi-C Contact Matrices

author.name: Andre Antonio Straton

entry.summary: Adapts HiFiC GAN-based compression loss to preserve biologically meaningful structures (loops, TAD boundaries) in Hi-C chromatin contact matrices under lossy compression, since visually acceptable compression can destroy genomic signals. Cross-domain neural codec adaptation.

entry.title: Neighbor-Aware View Synthesis for Restoring Missing Views in Light-Field Camera Arrays

author.name: Sakshi Goel, Ayush Goyal, K S Venkatesh, Koteswar Rao Jerripothula

entry.summary: Restores missing views in light-field camera arrays via neighbor-aware generative synthesis conditioned on selected neighboring images and positional encoding maps. Handles hardware-failure scenarios in dense camera rigs.

entry.title: From Subjective Judgments to Auditable Standards:Protocol-Guided AI Auditing of Website Redundancy

author.name: Ge Kong, Yongtong Cao

entry.summary: CORA provides protocol-guided, auditable AI auditing of website redundancy, separately measuring repetition load, normal-use tax, and failure-domain recovery reserve with versioned VLM annotations, typed validation, and retained traces. Moves subjective web-quality judgments toward reproducible standards.

entry.title: Multi-Modal Semantic Expansion with Constrained LLM Reranking for Conversational Music Recommendation

author.name: Naman Garg, Sarika Jain, George Fazekas

entry.summary: A RecSys 2026 challenge solution for conversational music recommendation using multi-modal retrieval over seven embedding spaces (CF, lyrics, audio, visual) fused with reciprocal rank fusion, followed by lightweight reranking and persona-driven generation. Primarily an engineering contribution showcasing fusion of many signals.

entry.title: Determinants of Starting Salaries for Filipino Graduates: An Explainable Machine Learning Approach

author.name: Alexander Gabriel A. Aranes, John Michael C. Magpantay, Reginald Neil C. Recario, Jamlech Iram N. Gojo Cruz, Rodolfo C. Camaclang III

entry.summary: Analyzes determinants of starting salaries for Filipino graduates using explainable ML on crowd-sourced survey data, finding job role and industry dominate over institutional prestige, corroborated by three independent lines of evidence. Applied social-science ML study addressing labor-market questions in the Philippines.

entry.title: The Axiomatic Trader: Latent Regularity, Information Budgets, and the Canonical Form of a Quantitative Investment System

author.name: Jiayu Li

entry.summary: Posits quantitative trading regularities as a time-invariant mechanism driven by an unobserved latent state, showing five declared constants force the canonical architecture of a correct investment system. Frames persistence-of-regularity as an axiom with information budgets.

entry.title: Multimodal pseudo-CT synthesis for PET attenuation correction using separate modality encoding and topogram conditioning

author.name: Rory Bell, Artemis Bouzaki, Jiaming Cao, Jasmine Morrison, Chelsea Sargeant

entry.summary: BIC-MAC Challenge submission: multimodal 3D patch-based U-Net with separate PET/MR encoders, multi-scale fusion, and FiLM topogram conditioning for pseudo-CT synthesis enabling PET attenuation correction. Reduces reliance on precise voxel-wise cross-modal correspondence.

entry.title: My AI Syllabus Policy

author.name: Vaughn Papenhausen

entry.summary: A philosophy instructor shares an AI syllabus policy arguing LLMs have shifted from calculator-analogy to personal-tutor status, laying out permitted and prohibited student and instructor uses in college education.

entry.title: CiUNet: A Hybrid Swin-CNN UNet for Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Bin Dong, Jinghong Chen

entry.summary: CiUNet is a lightweight hybrid Swin-CNN UNet for medical image segmentation adding a parallel CNN encoder for local texture and bridging modules for fine-grained detail, motivated by privacy-preserving commercial deployment. Conventional hybrid architecture work.

entry.title: MLLM-Assisted Audio VOS: A 3rd Place Report for the MeViS-Audio Track, 8th LSVOS Challenge

author.name: Liangtao Shi, Jinxia Xie, Xiantao Hu, Ting Liu

entry.summary: Third-place technical report for the MeViS-Audio track of the 8th LSVOS Challenge: a training-free pipeline chaining MLLMs for text-visual correspondence with SAM-based segmentation for audio-guided video object segmentation. Demonstrates foundation-model composition for competition tasks.

entry.title: MDFI: A Multi-Domain Features Integration for Compressed Video Quality Enhancement

author.name: Sang NguyenQuang, Hieu Bui Minh, Dang BuiDinh, Xiem HoangVan

entry.summary: MDFI enhances compressed H.266/VVC video quality via a Frame-Prediction Feature Transform module and multi-domain fusion of spatiotemporal, cross-frequency, and compressed-domain prediction features. Incremental codec-enhancement research.

entry.title: Triangular Fuzzy Rescaling Distance

author.name: Eddy Soria, Aida Valls, Ana Beatriz Hern\'andez-Lara

entry.summary: Proposes Triangular Fuzzy Rescaling Distance, a metric between triangular fuzzy numbers that integrates linear rescaling into the distance computation itself, removing the need for separate normalization of heterogeneous attributes. Includes formal proofs of metric properties. Specialized fuzzy-decision-making theory contribution.

entry.title: Quality Inspection of Printed Circuit Board Pin Insertion via Semantic Segmentation and Board-Level Feature Extraction

author.name: Nils Rabeneck, Andr\'e Kiunke, Nicole Hoess, Wolfgang Mauerer

entry.summary: Automated PCB pin-insertion defect detection combining U-Net semantic segmentation, contour feature extraction, and logistic regression board-level classification. A classical, deployable industrial inspection pipeline.

author.name: Mary Joy Daniel Vinas

entry.summary: The study combines QHAdam and AdamW into QHAdamW, an optimizer variant applied to ANN-based air quality index forecasting in the Philippines, showing improved convergence and generalization over Adam across seven evaluation metrics with tuned hyperparameters.

entry.summary: Automatic bee monitoring at hive entrances using YOLO11 transfer learning with progressive backbone unfreezing and ByteTrack parameter optimization, reaching ~97% precision and stable counting on side-view video. Applied ecological monitoring system.

entry.title: Gate Voltage Effect on Pulse Detection Efficiency of Perimeter-Gated SPADs

author.name: Hunter Guthrie, Md Sakibur Sajal, Zexi Liu, Marc Dandin

entry.summary: Characterizes gate-voltage trade-offs in perimeter-gated SPADs under pulsed illumination, showing pulse detection efficiency trades against spurious-event spread reduction, and proposes guidelines for pulsed LIDAR use. Hardware photonics measurement study.

author.name: Jinxing Zhou, Suiyi Zhao, Yanghao Zhou, Ruohao Guo

entry.title: Research Summary: August 24, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research spans causal foundation modeling, certified LLM safety, and training/inference efficiency. Foundation Models for Partial Causal Identification extends causal FMs to bounding intervention effects under unobserved confounding, while MTCR delivers certified robustness guarantees against multi-turn jailbreaks.

  • Muon shows persistent scaling advantages over AdamW on Diffusion Transformers up to 15B parameters
  • E2-TTT derives exact closed-form state transitions for test-time training, advancing the linear-attention architecture race
  • An open-weight introspection study provides rigorous negative findings on whether LLMs can report their own internal computation
  • Optimizer-state analysis yields a causal account of subliminal trait transfer during fine-tuning
  • AI with Authority demonstrates an end-to-end AI-directed verified stack
  • Behavioral safety work shows affective context systematically amplifies LLM sycophancy
  • Self-Speculation (SSR) accelerates reasoning models training-free by drafting from partial chain-of-thought distributions
entry.content:
Today's research spans causal foundation modeling, certified LLM safety, and training/inference efficiency. Foundation Models for Partial Causal Identification extends causal FMs to bounding intervention effects under unobserved confounding, while MTCR delivers certified robustness guarantees against multi-turn jailbreaks.

  • Muon shows persistent scaling advantages over AdamW on Diffusion Transformers up to 15B parameters
  • E2-TTT derives exact closed-form state transitions for test-time training, advancing the linear-attention architecture race
  • An open-weight introspection study provides rigorous negative findings on whether LLMs can report their own internal computation
  • Optimizer-state analysis yields a causal account of subliminal trait transfer during fine-tuning
  • AI with Authority demonstrates an end-to-end AI-directed verified stack
  • Behavioral safety work shows affective context systematically amplifies LLM sycophancy
  • Self-Speculation (SSR) accelerates reasoning models training-free by drafting from partial chain-of-thought distributions

entry.title: Foundation Models for Partial Causal Identification

author.name: Alexis Bellot, Anish Dhir

entry.summary: Develops causal foundation models for bounding intervention effects and counterfactuals under unobserved confounding by defining a canonical prior with full support over structural causal models with discrete observables. The task becomes learning distributions over functions mapping data and assumptions to causal queries.

entry.title: Open-Weight Masked Introspection: Measuring What Language Models Can Report About Their Own Computation

author.name: Emilio Ferrara

entry.summary: This study tests whether open-weight language models can introspect about their own computation by intervening on residual streams, attention heads, and SAE features, then asking models what changed against sham and matched-control baselines. Across eight open-weight models from seven families, none outperformed chance, providing a negative result against claims that sufficiently capable models can audit their own internals.

entry.title: Certified Multi-Turn Robustness for LLM Safety via Compositional Bounds and Safety Persistence

author.name: Yang Liu, Bin Chong, Wenkai Yang, Shuai Zhang, Yancheng Chen, Feiyu Han, GuoZhen, Cheng Zhang, Huaibing Xie, Changze Lv, Shihan Dou, Pluto Zhou

entry.summary: Introduces Multi-Turn Certified Robustness (MTCR), modeling conversational safety via State-Adversarial MDPs and defining k-turn certified robustness against progressive multi-turn jailbreak attacks. It uses embedding-space mode decomposition for tighter compositional bounds and alpha-beta safety persistence to slow bound degradation.

entry.title: Scaling Muon for Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Chenghao Li, Xiao Han, Xinxin Huang, Wei Liu, Boyang Li, Bing Xiao, Heran Zhang, Juanma Perez Rua, Ke Xu, Kangning Liu, Linjun Kuang, Na Li, Tan Wang, Tian Xie, Wei Peng, Yang Pei, Yifan Xu, Yuanhao Zhai, Yuwei Lin, Zhe Wang, Zihao He, Daniel Li, Junbiao Tang, Ziyang Jiang, Dake Chen

entry.summary: This work establishes Muon optimizer scaling behavior on Diffusion Transformers from 1.3B to 15B parameters, showing persistent advantages over AdamW in optimization and generative quality. To fix Newton-Schulz overhead at scale it introduces Periodic Row-wise Muon, which amortizes full spectral updates across steps.

entry.title: Beyond Imitation: Self-Improving Robot Policies via Off-Policy Q-Planning

author.name: Varun Giridhar, Anant Khandelwal, Jeremy A. Collins, Ignat Georgiev, Animesh Garg

entry.summary: Q-Planning equips large visuomotor behavior-cloning robot policies with a small off-policy Q-function trained on the same demonstrations that later absorbs both successful and failed deployment rollouts, enabling self-improvement without extra human data. Because Q estimates value rather than imitating actions, failures become usable signal that BC alone cannot exploit. Avoids scaling difficulties of RL fine-tuning on multi-billion-parameter policies.

entry.title: aiXamine: Unified Black-Box Evaluation of Cross-Dimensional Trade-offs in LLM Safety, Security, and Privacy

author.name: Fatih Deniz, Yazan Boshmaf, Dorde Popovic, Issa Khalil

entry.summary: aiXamine is a unified black-box platform evaluating LLM safety, security, and privacy as interdependent properties through 46 tests across nine services in an automated red-teaming pipeline. It surfaces cross-dimensional trade-offs invisible to siloed evaluations, such as models refusing many benign queries despite high safety scores. Produces hierarchical risk profiles for reproducible trustworthiness assessment.

entry.title: Who Delegates to AI? Evidence from 53,000 Agent Configurations

author.name: Hyeongjae Lee, Jihyang Cheon, Lanu Kim

entry.summary: Introducing delegated exposure and the Agentic Adoption Index, this study measures whether workers have actually committed tasks to AI by analyzing roughly 53,000 agent skill specifications from the Manus Skills Marketplace matched against about 18,000 O*NET task statements. It finds distinct patterns in which occupations are actually delegating work to agents, complementing capability-based exposure measures.

entry.title: Consilience: Conformally Calibrated Communication Control for Hidden-Profile Multi-Agent Reasoning

author.name: Abhijith Babu, Ramneet Kaur, Vishal Pramanik, Olivera Kotevska, Nathaniel D. Bastian, Susmit Jha, Sunny Raj, Yanzhao Wu, Sumit Kumar Jha, Anirban Roy

entry.summary: Consilience is an inference-time orchestration framework that steers and certifies communication in multi-agent LLM reasoning under hidden-profile settings where each agent holds partial evidence. It maintains a compact discussion state capturing uncertainty, disagreement, evidence gain, redundancy, and premature consensus to decide whether conversational actions are appropriate, offering guarantees absent from fixed schedules or debate protocols.

entry.title: AI with Authority, from Application to Silicon

author.name: Jason Hickey

entry.summary: Reporting that generative AI makes machine verification economical and essential rather than a cost overhead, this paper describes one researcher directing AI agents in five weeks from application code through a verified compiler and executive to a RISC-V processor taped out on a community shuttle, with no human-reviewed proofs and no human-written RTL. The Salt method rests on a hallucination-resistant proof kernel.

entry.title: Rethinking Expressivity and Efficiency in Test-Time Training

author.name: Zeyun Zhong, Joya Chen, Manuel Martin, Frederik Diederichs, Juergen Gall, Juergen Beyerer

entry.summary: E2-TTT derives a closed-form chunk-level state transition that exactly reproduces per-token fast-weight and momentum states of test-time training recurrences, enabling fully parallelized chunk-wise training without discarding temporal structure. Validated by training models up to 1.3B parameters. Balances expressivity of per-token updates with hardware-efficient chunked approximations for long-context processing.

entry.title: Move by Move: Measuring and Steering How LLMs Conduct Psychotherapy

author.name: Afonso Baldo, Hugo Pitorro, Areti Vassilopoulos, Anabela C. Areias, Maya D'Eon, Fab\'iola Costa, Ricardo Rei, Nuno M. Guerreiro

entry.summary: Introduces an ontology of ten therapeutic moves validated with five licensed psychologists and scaled via judge-based annotation, then compares human clinicians against frontier LLMs conducting psychotherapy sessions. Finds models over-use inquiry up to three times the human rate, neglect psychoeducation, and anchor strongly to strategies initiated earlier in context.

entry.title: Logic-VLA: A Temporal Logic Conditioned Vision-Language-Action Model

author.name: Celina Shiyu Wang, Yiqi Zhao, Junjie Ye, Yue Wang, Jyotirmoy V. Deshmukh

entry.summary: Logic-VLA conditions vision-language-action policies on Signal Temporal Logic specifications provided at inference time, using a syntax-graph-based STL encoder pre-trained to capture temporal logic semantics. Training combines STL-conditioned supervised fine-tuning with trajectory-level preference optimization over satisfying-versus-violating rollout pairs via a flow-matching surrogate for Identity Preference Optimization.

entry.title: Self-Speculation for Faster Reasoning Models

author.name: Ravisri Valluri, Tung Nguyen, Aditya Grover

entry.summary: SSR is a training-free self-speculative decoding method that uses the partial chain-of-thought answer distribution as the draft for the model itself, exploiting reasoning-workflow structure that token-level acceleration ignores. Targets latency-sensitive interactive applications needing long reasoning traces. No auxiliary drafter model required.

entry.title: Affective Context Amplifies Sycophancy in LLM Responses

author.name: Jiayi Li, Sanjana Menon, Brett Frischmann, Shomir Wilson, Sarah Rajtmajer

entry.summary: Shows that affective context systematically amplifies LLM sycophancy: user-facing responses soften or withhold negative evaluations compared to third-party framings of identical content, measured across seven LLMs on Reddit datasets. Grounded in ingratiation theory, this reveals a consistent safety-relevant bias in emotionally loaded interactions.

entry.title: A Survey on Foundations and Frontiers of Multimodal Agentic Frameworks: Techniques and Applications

author.name: Neel Mokaria, Rishie Raj, Dheeraj Baiju, Xiaoqian Shen, Shraman Pramanick, Kevin Qinghong Lin, Arda Senocak, Mike Zheng Shou, Philip Torr, Mohamed Elhoseiny, Yapeng Tian, Ruohan Gao, Salman Khan, Sayan Nag, Sanjoy Chowdhury, Dinesh Manocha

entry.summary: A comprehensive survey examining how multimodality shapes agency across the core modules of agentic frameworks: perception, memory, reasoning, planning, and action. It fills a gap left by prior LLM-agent surveys by systematically covering systems built on large multimodal models processing images, audio, and video, and maps techniques to applications.

entry.title: Volumetric Radiology AI in the Era of Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Zanting Ye, Shengyuan Liu, Xin Liu, Chenhui Wang, Zhisong Wang, Jiashuai Liu, Zipei Wang, Cheng Wang, Wentao Pan, Mengjie Fang, Di Dong, Mohammad Salmanpour, Arman Rahmim, Yu Gu, Yong Xia, Hongming Shan, Yixuan Yuan, Yefeng Zheng, Lijun Lu

entry.summary: This paper surveys how multimodal large language models are extending radiology AI beyond 2D image analysis toward full volumetric (3D) interpretation. It identifies a core representational mismatch between clinical needs for whole-volume spatial context and current MLLM conditioning on selected slices or report text, and outlines requirements for preserving and integrating task-relevant 3D information.

entry.title: Continuous-Time Quantum Walks based Graph Neural Network

author.name: Yuliang Zhan, Zefeng Gao, Jian Li, Yang Liu, Hao sun

entry.summary: Proposes CTQW-GNN, a graph neural network built on continuous-time quantum walks that jointly addresses heterophily and over-smoothing using properties of the CTQW propagator, with theoretical justification rather than heuristics. This offers a principled alternative to standard message passing.

entry.title: Prediction certification cannot replace explanation certification: a competence envelope for trustworthy AI under compound stress

author.name: Nataliya Shakhovska, Ivan Izonin, Stergios-Aristoteles Mitoulis

entry.summary: Proves a separation theorem showing that a reliable model and a compromised one can be identical under every prediction-side certificate (accuracy, calibration, conformal coverage) yet differ arbitrarily in explanation behavior. This establishes that prediction certification cannot substitute for explanation certification in trustworthy AI.

entry.title: CLEAR: Continuous Latent Adapter Routing for Utility-Preserving LLM Safety Alignment

author.name: Chengxiao Wang, Enyi Jiang, Xiaojing Liao, Sanmi Koyejo

entry.summary: CLEAR proposes conditional safety adaptation where a lightweight hidden-state gate continuously controls the activation strength of a safety low-rank adapter, reducing harmful completions while leaving benign-prompt behavior of the frozen backbone intact. Experiments show improved HarmBench robustness with reduced utility degradation versus global safety tuning.

entry.title: SRL-MPC: Shape-Aware Reinforcement Learned Model Predictive Control

author.name: Ruihua Han, Rui Gao, Zhe Liu, Xinyi Wang, Chang Chen, Shuai Wang, Qi Hao, Jia Pan, Hengshuang Zhao

entry.summary: Quantization-Aware Healing (QAH) recovers structurally compressed 4-bit LLMs by distilling from the bf16 checkpoint rather than refitting hard labels as in standard QAT, which converged slowly and collapsed past its peak. The recipe targets combined structural pruning plus 4-bit quantization pipelines where reasoning and coding degrade severely.

entry.title: Primal Acceleration of Newton's Method

author.name: Nikita Doikov

entry.summary: This optimization-theory paper develops a primal accelerated Newton method for convex functions with Lipschitz Hessian achieving global O(1/k^3) convergence with one linear solve per iteration and predetermined parameters. It is claimed to be the first second-order method attaining this rate without cubic regularization subproblems, nonlinear searches, or dual corrections, implementable Hessian-free.

entry.title: Designing a Robust LLM-Based Evaluation System for Agentic AI in Drug Discovery Through Human Alignment

author.name: Emma Granqvist, Roc\'io Mercado, Samuel Genheden

entry.summary: This paper presents an LLM-as-a-Judge evaluation framework for ChatInvent, an agentic drug discovery assistant deployed at AstraZeneca, validated against human expert judgments. It defines four output-quality dimensions and shows that reference-based metrics fail for open-ended tool-augmented outputs. The work provides one of the first human-aligned validation studies of LLM judges in industrial chemistry workflows.

entry.title: Multilingual Verifier Bias in RLVR: Benchmark, Rollout Diagnosis, and the Cross-Lingual Selection Bottleneck

author.name: Chenyu Zhou, Qiliang Jiang, Xu Zhou

entry.summary: This work shows exact-match verifiers in multilingual RLVR convert format and script variation into language-dependent false-negative reward noise, breaking the assumption of language-neutral rewards. It introduces a reusable auditing protocol with verifier-robustness suites and language-conditioned reward-error metrics across Japanese, English, and Chinese, revealing sharply different rejection rates on MGSM rollouts for Qwen3 models. Identifies cross-lingual selection as a bottleneck for multilingual reasoning training.

entry.title: Llama-Mobile: Efficient 2.7-Bit Quantization of VLMs

author.name: Luka Ribar, Jeevan Bhoot, Douglas Orr

entry.summary: Presents a framework for quantizing vision-language models to 2.7 bits per parameter with efficient Arm CPU execution, using a self-generating-data calibration pipeline requiring no access to the original training setup. Compresses Llama 3.2 11B Vision Instruct to 3.7 GB with 8-bit activations while preserving strong VQA performance. Enables on-device multimodal inference.

entry.title: Truthful Calibration Measures for Sequential Prediction

author.name: Anagha Gokul, Jason Hartline, Lunjia Hu, Jonathan Ullman, Yifan Wu

entry.summary: Resolves an open question negatively: exact truthfulness is incompatible with completeness and soundness for calibration measures in sequential binary prediction, even with independent outcomes. Shows approximate truthfulness escapes the impossibility via two general reductions producing additively and multiplicatively approximately truthful measures. Advances the theory of truthful calibration following Haghtalab et al. 2024.

entry.title: EndoLIFT: Language-Disambiguated Latent-Conditioned Rectified Flow for Bidirectional Endoscopic Control

author.name: Chi Kit Ng, Yidong Zhang, Lui Siu Hing, Jinsong Lin, Tianchun Wu, Ho Yin Chim, Zhiqing Tang, Tao Yang, Huxin Gao, Trevor Yeung, Raymond Shing-Yan Tang, Hongliang Ren

entry.summary: EndoLIFT is a vision-language-action policy for bidirectional gastrointestinal endoscopic control that combines language-based intent conditioning with a latent-conditioned rectified-flow action expert. It formalizes intent aliasing, where nearly identical visual observations require opposite axial actions depending on the requested procedure phase, and resolves it through explicit instruction conditioning.

entry.title: Roadside-Cooperative Autonomous Driving: From Data Platform to Vision-Language End-to-End Reasoning

author.name: Yitao Xu, Tong Wu, Yiyan Wu, Guoji Xu, Yanbo Jiang, Jiahao Wang, Zehong Ke, Junkai Jiang, Fang Zhang, Jianqiang Wang

entry.summary: The work introduces V2XBench, a closed-loop simulation platform with synchronized ego-roadside sensing, plus Chat-V2XBench, a progressively structured VQA dataset for cooperative driving reasoning, and proposes AURORA, an end-to-end cooperative driving framework with dual-view perception and vision-language reasoning. It targets beyond-line-of-sight perception and language-grounded supervision gaps in existing V2X benchmarks.

entry.title: CDRL: Certification-Driven Reinforcement Learning for Neutrino Flavor Model Discovery

author.name: Piyush Jha, Jake Rudolph, Victoria Knapp-P\'erez, Max Fieg, Aishik Ghosh, Vijay Ganesh

entry.summary: CDRL introduces certification-driven reinforcement learning in which symbolic reasoners produce certificates identifying which actions cause constraint violations during scientific hypothesis search. These certificates become reusable constraints that prune invalid solution classes and guide exploration, demonstrated on neutrino flavor model discovery.

entry.title: CAS: Conformalized Agentic Search via Adaptive Retrieval and Policy Weighting

author.name: Zixi Zhu, Jiayuan Su, Jian Zhang, Yu Lin, Hongwei Wang

entry.summary: Introduces Conformalized Agentic Search (CAS), which applies conformal prediction both at retrieval time via adaptive prediction sets for dynamic document truncation and during RL fine-tuning via adaptive conformal inference to curb over-confidence and hallucination. It targets reliability failures of search agents under RL.

entry.title: Stored in Optimizer State, Valued by Later Training: A Causal Account of Subliminal Trait Transfer

author.name: Qinyang Xu

entry.summary: Treating parameters and optimizer moments as one trainer state, this work derives an exact transport-valuation identity explaining how subliminal behavioral traits survive removal of tainted source data and acquire different signs under later training, identifying the first optimizer moment as the causal carrier via state surgery experiments.

entry.title: AsmEvo: Agentic Assembly-Level Optimization of AMD GPU Kernels with Functional Equivalence Verification

author.name: Ji Liu, Puyuan Yang, Rongzhang Zheng, Fan Wang, Jinglin Wang, Muhammad A. Awad, Mortis Huang, Andy Chang, Zekai Li, Zeping Li, Zihao An, Yue Liu, Yuchen Yang, Jianghui Wang, Chushi Chen, Ziqiong Liu, Fuwei Yang, Dong Li, Wen Heng Chung, Shengcai Liu, Emad Barsoum

entry.summary: AsmEvo is an agentic optimizer editing already-compiled AMDGPU code objects where the deployed binary is the only behavioral oracle, reconstructing reassemblable representations, proposing low-level edits with a long-horizon agent, rebuilding ABI-preserving objects, and accepting candidates verified functionally equivalent. Goes beyond CUDA/Triton source-level optimizers. Large AMD-affiliated author list suggests serious industrial backing.

entry.title: Dual-Cache Latent Space Communication between Heterogeneous Language Models

author.name: Jiyao Liu, Qi Zhang, Yaoyi Jia, Ziwen Kan, Song Wang

entry.summary: This work proposes dual-cache latent space communication between heterogeneous language models, letting one model transfer knowledge encoded in its KV cache to another without autoregressive text decoding. It extends prior protocols like C2C and LCF-X by relaxing shared-context, layer-alignment, and compression restrictions between sharer and receiver.

entry.title: Knowing but Not Saying: Preventing Factual Access Failures in LLM SFT via Recall-Anchored Distillation

author.name: Haodong Chen, Yadong Wang, Shengtao Wen, Dong Liang, Xiang Chen

entry.summary: Identifies factual access failure as a distinct phenomenon from catastrophic forgetting: after domain SFT, models can recognize correct answers under constrained probes but fail to produce them in closed-book generation. It proposes recall-anchored distillation to prevent such failures.

entry.title: RAG Deserves an Index: Why Ingest-Time Compilation Beats Query-Time Interpretation

author.name: Kyle Wild, Yusuke Takahashi, Asako Uraki

entry.summary: Argues that production RAG systems waste computation by re-interpreting raw corpus text at query time, and proposes ingest-time semantic compilation (ISC): precomputing a maintained semantic index once at write time, analogous to database indexing. The paper positions this as a paradigm shift for retrieval-augmented QA economics.

entry.title: TreeWY: Speculative Verification for Gated DeltaNet Hybrids

author.name: Sneha Murthy Ghantasala

entry.summary: TreeWY removes state snapshots in speculative decoding for Gated DeltaNet hybrid models by computing each draft tree node output with a tree-structured WY transform of the gated delta rule, reconstructing only the accepted state. This makes wide draft trees memory-feasible for linear-attention hybrids.

entry.title: CellPath-Bench: A Multidimensional Benchmark for Whole-Slide Cellular Representations in Pathology Foundation Models

author.name: Bokai Zhao, Yiyang Zhang, Hanqing Chao, Yawei Ma, Long Bai, Tai Ma, Minfeng Xu, Ming Song, Tianzi Jiang

entry.summary: CellPath-Bench evaluates frozen pathology foundation models at cellular resolution using 25 spatially aligned H&E-Xenium sections spanning 11 organs and over 7 million cells, probing cell-type decodability and transferability across tissues, datasets, and organs.

entry.title: WA-JEPA: Rethinking the Video JEPA Paradigm for World-Action Modeling in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Xinlin Wang, Yujiao Xiang, Yuheng Zhou, Jingqi Wang, Minqing Huang, Jiajie Huang, Dongxu Wei, Tingguang Zhou, Xiyang Wang, Gong Chen, Zhi Xu, Feiyang Tan, Hangning Zhou, Mu Yang

entry.summary: WA-JEPA adapts the video JEPA paradigm for autonomous driving planning via hybrid future-masked pre-training that infers future latents from observed context, replacing random masking and deterministic regression with action-coupled prediction. It positions world modeling tightly around action-conditioned futures for driving.

entry.title: BackDFL: A Unified Benchmark For Backdoor Attacks and Defenses In Decentralized Federated Learning

author.name: Mouhamed Amine Bouchiha, Gregory Blanc, Yufei Han

entry.summary: BackDFL is a unified benchmark for backdoor attacks and defenses in decentralized federated learning, arguing that prior robustness claims are inflated by simplified threat models, non-adaptive adversaries, and inconsistent protocols. It standardizes evaluation across communication topologies and adaptive attackers. The paper reframes the threat landscape when no central parameter server exists.

entry.title: Minimax Optimality of Score-Entropy Discrete Diffusion

author.name: Cholyeon Cho, Yuchen Wu

entry.summary: This theory paper establishes minimax optimality bounds for score-entropy discrete diffusion (SEDD), investigating fundamental statistical properties rather than sampling efficiency under assumed-small score error. It complements prior finite-sample analyses of score estimation itself. Provides foundational guarantees for one of the strongest empirical discrete diffusion families used on text and graphs.

entry.title: Human-JEPA: A Human-Centric Vision Model that Perceives and Anticipates

author.name: Hui Wei, Licai Sun, Guoying Zhao

entry.summary: Human-JEPA is a human-centric video vision model trained via anchored forecasting, pinning dense prediction targets to a frozen copy of initialization to prevent collapse of dense perception, with past-to-future masking replacing block masks. Under frozen probes it leads pose estimation and person re-identification specialists at 2.7 times fewer parameters while adding anticipation ability. Extends JEPA-style learning to humans who move.

entry.title: VT-MUSE: Multimodal Unified Sequential Visuotactile Representation Learning for Manipulation

author.name: Congsheng Xu, Qiaochu Yang, Fangyuan Shi, Yifan Han, Baijun Chen, Yiming Wang, Haonan Zhao, Daolin Ma, Xiaokang Yang, Hesheng Wang

entry.summary: VT-MUSE is a two-stage multimodal representation learning framework for visuotactile robotic manipulation that jointly adapts modality-specific encoders via cross-modal temporal alignment and masked-view consistency, then uses a conditional variational latent model over masked visual sequences with full tactile histories. It targets fine-grained cross-modal dependencies and temporal contact evolution that independent-encode-then-fuse approaches miss.

entry.title: ReFrame: Evidence-Guided Test-Time Safety Alignment in Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Wenzheng Jiang, Xuankun Rong, Yuanzhao Zhai, Dawei Feng, Huaimin Wang

entry.summary: ReFrame is a training-free test-time safety alignment framework for multimodal LLMs, using two-agent input reframing guided by identified failure modes of utility dominance and reasoning inertia. It works on closed-source deployed models where retraining or internal-state access is impossible.

entry.title: Truth Lies Deep: Countering Semantic Camouflage via Latent Intent Verification

author.name: Md. Hasib Ur Rahman

entry.summary: This safety study shows that LLM alignment based on refusal mechanisms remains vulnerable to Semantic Camouflage attacks that wrap harmful intent in benign narrative contexts like creative writing. By analyzing latent activation trajectories in Phi-3, Qwen2.5, and Gemma-2b under adversarial stress, it identifies a universal Intent Horizon, a critical depth at which harmful intent becomes detectable in latent space.

entry.title: Why2Speak: Faithful Reasoning for Abstaining Action Policies

author.name: Shreya Mendi, Brinnae Bent

entry.summary: Why2Speak studies faithful reasoning for policies deciding when to act versus abstain, instantiated as intervention timing in multi-party conversation. Using Qwen3-8B, it compares direct, chain-of-thought, fine-tuned, and RL policies, uncovering a capability-auditability tradeoff where the strongest direct policy resists faithful explanation.

entry.title: Beyond Endpoint Gains: A Weight-Delta Audit of Medical Specialization

author.name: Praphul Singh, Shanu Kumar, Akshat Agarwal

entry.summary: Audits the actual weight deltas between generalist-medical checkpoint pairs (Gemma-3-4B-IT to MedGemma-4B-IT and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct to HuatuoGPT-o1-7B) rather than just endpoint benchmark gains. It finds decoder-side updates strongly reconstruct benchmark movement but the change is not cleanly localized, with MLP components dominating.

entry.title: MGAL: A Multilingual Granularity-Aware Long-Context Benchmark

author.name: Chunhan Li, Chenglin Xu, Zongyang Zhang, Jiale Liu, Zhuoxi Rao, Xudong Jia, Junxiu He, Menglin Yang, Wenjuan Gong, Zhengzhe Liu, Chengwei Qin

entry.summary: MGAL is the first multilingual, granularity- and position-aware long-context benchmark built from UN reports spanning 8K to 128K tokens across six official UN languages. It stratifies tasks by word, sentence, paragraph, and document granularity plus document position, enabling finer-grained diagnosis of long-context failures.

entry.title: Testing and Evaluation of Agentic AI Systems In Military Command and Control

author.name: Ulysse Richard, Heather Frase, Sarah Cao, Di Cooke, Sebastian Kwon, Adrianna Tan

entry.summary: A structured review of 240 documented testing-and-evaluation practices for military command-and-control AI identifies eight assumptions (grouped into specifiability, stability, composability, supervisability) that established methods make, showing how agentic properties weaken each and what that implies for discharging public commitments to human oversight.

entry.title: ClawSentry: A Progressive Multi-Tier Security Monitor for Safeguarding Autonomous LLM Agents

author.name: Kai Wang, Zeming Wei, BiaoJie Zeng, Chang Jin, An Wang, Xiaokun Luan, Zhixiao Lin, Jingjing Qu, Xia Hu, Xingcheng Xu

entry.summary: ClawSentry is an open-source framework-agnostic supervision gateway monitoring autonomous LLM agents across four lifecycle loci: skill admission, invocation-time intent, execution-time effect, and post-action consequence. It addresses progressive risk where denied dangerous objectives reappear across surface forms, tools, or turns.

entry.title: Wrong-Physics Backdoors in Neural PDE Operators

author.name: Hanbing Liang, Fujun Liu

entry.summary: Introducing wrong-physics backdoors, this paper describes a cross-parameter relinking data-poisoning primitive against neural PDE operators trained on solver archives: triggered inputs return physically plausible solutions for the wrong physical parameter. Across 476 campaigns on Burgers and other dynamics it exploits tensor-to-parameter provenance failures in multi-parameter archives.

entry.title: RODE: A Radial-Orthogonal Decoupled Engine for Optimization

author.name: Guoxiang Xu, Bince Qu, Qi Sun, Cheng Zhuo

entry.summary: RODE is a matrix-aware optimizer that decouples the radial (Frobenius norm) and directional components of weight updates, giving each its own update rule and step size, with Newton-Schulz-conditioned directional updates in the tangent space. Controlled GPT-2 interventions demonstrate gains from explicit norm control plus the directional channel. It addresses an underexplored interaction in Muon-style optimizers where norm and direction changes interfere.

entry.title: Asymmetric Capacity Allocation in Self-Refinement Pipelines

author.name: Zhuoyi Yang, Ian G. Harris, Salar Hashemitaheri, Cassie Huang, Yuangang Li, Hyunwoo Oh, Paul Dourish, Tony Givargis, Mohsen Imani, Li Zhang

entry.summary: First stage-wise study of model size in LLM self-refinement pipelines across 5 benchmarks using multiple sizes of Qwen3 and other families. It examines whether generation, critique, and revision require equally capable models, finding asymmetric capacity allocation can save resources. Challenges treating model size as an implementation detail in generate-critique-revise loops.

entry.title: Harmonic Torsional Diffusion for Protein-Ligand Flexible Docking

author.name: Maksim Zhdanov, Pavel Strashnov, Vladislav Kurenkov

entry.summary: Harmony parameterizes ligand and side-chain torsional score fields for flexible protein-ligand docking as derivatives of learned harmonic potentials on the circle, with noise-level dependence supplied analytically by the heat semigroup on the torus. This respects periodic geometry that generic Euclidean diffusion heads ignore. Targets joint pose and protein flexibility modeling in structure-based drug design.

entry.title: Rethinking Demonstration Unlearning in Imitation Learning for Robotics

author.name: Jiazhuo Li, Yu Zhang, Yiming Fei, Kangkang Dong, Xiaojun Zhu, Houde Liu, Jinze Tao

entry.summary: This work defines a retrain-calibrated audit for demonstration unlearning in robot imitation learning along two axes: behavioral similarity to a policy retrained without removed demonstrations, and detectability of prior training exposure. Existing machine-unlearning metrics fail to capture what edits remove from closed-loop policies. Motivated by people requesting removal of their demonstrations from robot training data.

entry.title: RARE: Decoupling Representation Steering from Expert Routing in Mixture-of-Experts Language Models

author.name: Zhibo Zhang, Zhen Ouyang, Ling Shi, Kailong Wang

entry.summary: Identifies a structural mismatch when applying representation steering to Mixture-of-Experts models, showing that behavioral perturbations disrupt router decisions. The proposed RARE framework projects perturbations onto the null space of the router matrix, making steering router-agnostic while preserving clean routing.

entry.title: Basin-Preserving Discretizations of Modern Hopfield Retrieval Dynamics: Energy Cells, Dissipation, and the Attention Limit

author.name: Francisco R. Villatoro

entry.summary: This theoretical work studies which time discretizations of modern Hopfield retrieval dynamics preserve not only energy decay and equilibria but also basins of attraction, introducing energy cells as connected sublevel-set components around attractors. It proves basin containment results covering relaxed attention maps for theta between zero and two and implicit Euler, connecting attention updates to difference-of-convex minimization.

entry.title: PhysCaP: Grounding Code-as-Policy Agent with Physics-Informed Exploration

author.name: Chen-Yu Lin, Jing-Wen Chen, Hsueh-En Chang, Hung-An Chen, Sheng-Hsun Chang, Chi-Pin Huang, Fu-En Yang, Min-Hung Chen, Yi-Ting Chen, Yu-Chiang Frank Wang, Shao-Hua Sun

entry.summary: PhysCaP augments code-as-policy frameworks for manipulation with a physics-informed exploration layer enabling active perception: training-free modules estimate object mass and stiffness from proprioception alone, and a dual-agent Planner-Executor design decides when interacting to gather information outweighs acting directly.

entry.title: ForeTime-VLA: Causal Future-Token Distillation from a World Action Model for Conveyor-Belt Manipulation

author.name: Siyuan Ma, Yutian Zhang, Boshi Zhang, Qinglian Wu, Jiaqi Zhai, Dong Wei, Xiaojin Huang

entry.summary: ForeTime-VLA distills future-aware representations from a world action model teacher into a dense pi0.5 vision-language-action policy for manipulating objects on conveyor belts. Offline, current and future video latents are compressed into a whitened target predicted online by an eight-frame history encoder alongside phase and time-to-transition estimates, keeping inference causal without running a video-scale world model.

entry.title: SPARC: Single-Pass Scaling for Motion Forecasting with Conformal Bayesian Last Layers

author.name: Sakif Hossain, Julian Teusch, J\"org P. M\"uller

entry.summary: SPARC adds a deterministic Bayesian last layer with conformal calibration to motion forecasting, converting feature leverage into an analytic horizon-wise epistemic scale in a single inference pass. It provides calibrated, covariance-preserving uncertainty without repeated stochastic inference required by ensembles.

entry.title: Nothing Changed but the Model: CellFill -- Bounded In-Cell Learning for Bit-Identical, Revocable Updates to Quantized LLMs

author.name: Zifeng Liu, Zhiyong Du, Yaxin Lu, Yiming Mao, Zhenhe Wang, Wenqi Shi, Zhengkun Jing

entry.summary: CellFill writes new knowledge exclusively into per-weight residuals inside the dequantization gaps of frozen 4-bit integer codes and scales, guaranteeing re-quantized artifacts remain bit-identical and updates exactly revocable by dropping residuals, with bounded drift formalized via propositions and training paths.

entry.title: Tydra: An Efficient Hybrid Model for Tabular Data

author.name: Mieszko Komisarczyk, Saurabh Mathur, Maurice Kraus, Sriraam Natarajan, Kristian Kersting

entry.summary: Tydra is a hybrid Transformer-State Space Model architecture for tabular in-context learning that interleaves attention and SSM layers to balance TabPFN-like accuracy with subquadratic cost. Across 30 OpenML datasets it cuts inference time by 30 percent versus TabPFN while retaining most performance and beats a ten-times-larger Hydra model. Supports hybrid designs for tabular foundation models.

entry.title: ViTacPhys: Physical Property-Aware Grasping from Human Visual-Tactile Demonstrations

author.name: Yiwen Liu, Yujun Zhu, Kui Jia, Zhao Liao, Yangwei You, Shuaijun Wang

entry.summary: ViTacPhys estimates object mass, friction-coefficient class, and continuous stiffness from human visual-tactile manipulation demonstrations, trained on 60 rigid and deformable objects with cross-attention multimodal fusion and a VLM-derived semantic prior. It reports high accuracy including 97.2 percent mass classification and 98.8 percent friction classification on seen objects.

entry.title: Nexus: Depth-Adaptive KV-Cache Splicing and Retrieval-Decoupled Tool Routing for Agentic LLMs on Unified Memory

author.name: Mustafa Arslan

entry.summary: Nexus decouples tool routing from schema-prefill cost in MCP-based agentic LLMs using an INT8 semantic lookaside buffer with a calibrated cross-encoder margin gate, generating arguments over compressed textual signatures instead of spliced KV caches. Routing accuracy stays near 89 percent as registries scale to 250 tools, where concatenate-all-schemas baselines overflow the context window entirely.

entry.title: Evaluating Skills, Not Just Agents: Agentic Continuous Evaluation of Skills

author.name: Christopher Kevin, Narendran Raghavan, Jean-Francois Puget, Roshni Malani, Meghana Puvvadi, Moshe Abramovitch, Mohit Gupta, Rama Akkiraju, Subodh Prabhu, Yogesh Dangi, Wei Luo, Seong Hee Lee

entry.summary: ACES is a repository-native framework for continuously evaluating enterprise agent skills as executable artifacts, running paired live trials with and without a target skill and grading trajectories via a standardized Agent Trajectory Interchange Format. It shifts evaluation from static structural checks to empirical evidence that capability packages help live agents complete tasks.

entry.title: Structure for Reading, Prose for Writing: Asymmetric Structural Conditioning in Multi-Agent Document Authoring

author.name: Cheng Yu, Nikhil Mathew, Zhengjie Wang

entry.summary: Reports a deployed multi-agent tender-response system using an open-weights model under sovereignty constraints, evaluated blind against real human-submitted bids: an LLM judge rated it at least as good on 40 of 55 sections, and most flagged gaps traced to knowledge absent from the pipeline sources. It proposes asymmetric structural conditioning for reading forms versus writing responses.

entry.title: Graph-Operator World Models for Morphology-Parameter Generalization in Continuous Control

author.name: Xu Yang, Yiqin Yang, Qianchuan Zhao

entry.summary: GraphOp-WM is a structured world model representing robot bodies as attributed graphs and factorizing transitions into a morphology-independent local dynamics basis plus morphology-dependent terms, enabling generalization to unseen link lengths, masses, damping, and actuation in continuous control.

entry.title: Don't Solve, Just Compare: Tiny Advisors for Runtime Intervention in LLM Agents

author.name: Yanze Jiang, Mingxuan Li, Yuhao Wang, Shengfang Zhai, Jiaheng Zhang

entry.summary: COTA enables constructive runtime intervention in LLM agents using a tiny comparator that only judges between candidate trajectories rather than solving tasks or generating corrections itself, avoiding the cost of an expert solver while providing recovery direction.

entry.title: Inhibitory Attention for Clinical Long-Context Reasoning: Characterizing and Mitigating Lost-in-the-Middle Effects in EHR Processing

author.name: Sanjay Basu

entry.summary: The paper gives the first systematic characterization of clinical lost-in-the-middle effects in electronic health record processing, showing a 21.9 percentage-point accuracy gap between peak and trough context positions across 2,196 instruction-response pairs and six language models. It evaluates context-selection strategies, including inhibitory attention approaches, as mitigations.

entry.title: TracingFlow: A Simulation-Free Trajectory Inference Framework Based on Second-Order Dynamics

author.name: Yuhao Sun, Zekun Wu, Zixun Huang, Peijie Zhou

entry.summary: TracingFlow extends flow matching to second-order dynamics by regressing acceleration fields, providing an exact simulation-free solution to Dynamical Optimal Acceleration Transport. First-order OT frameworks miss regulatory momentum and delayed responses present in processes like cell differentiation.

entry.title: Utility Under Attack: Agent Memory Poisoning and the Limits of Content Screening and Provenance Ranking

author.name: Arulnidhi Karunanidhi

entry.summary: Measuring agent memory poisoning, this paper shows plainly worded false assertions poisoning just 1.2 percent of a LongMemEval corpus drop accuracy from 0.850 to 0.300, while a four-stage write-time content screening pipeline rejects zero of 360 poisoned memories despite good indirect-injection recall. It concludes content-only screening cannot separate false from true assertions without external grounding.

entry.title: Learning Exact NVIDIA SASS Encoders with $\mathbb{F}_2$ Linear Algebra

author.name: Jiading Gai

entry.summary: F2Asm learns exact 128-bit NVIDIA SASS instruction encoders as vector-valued affine maps over F2 from paired disassembly and CUBIN words using Gaussian elimination, becoming the first open-source SASS assembler supporting Rubin SM107 alongside Hopper and Blackwell targets. It enables controlled machine-code rewriting on recent data-center GPUs.

entry.title: Capturing Cardiac Cyclicity through Phase-Equivariant Self-Supervised Learning

author.name: Blaise Delaney, Dominic Dootson, Juan Jose Juan Castella, Salil Patel, Andrew Pfaff, Yuji Xing, Jonny Hancox, Karin Sevegnani

entry.summary: Winder introduces a phase-equivariant self-supervised objective for cardiac signals, organizing representations into phase-invariant coordinates and phase-rotating harmonic subspaces with a fixed closed-form transport operator derived from cycle geometry. On PTB-XL it reaches diagnostic accuracy near state-of-the-art SSL methods with roughly a 1M parameter footprint. Exploits cyclicity of physiological processes as a natural prior.

entry.title: COMET: Contrastive Motion-Enhanced Temporal Reasoning for Video Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Chenghua Zhu, Zhaolu Kang, Qifan Shi, Siyan Wu, Kehan Jiang, Lei Wei, Lianyu Hu, Guangyuan Dong, Mingbo Yang, Rui Lu, Guibo Luo

entry.summary: COMET strengthens video multimodal LLMs on fine-grained motion-temporal understanding through a Taylor frame-difference motion branch injected into the appearance stream via temporal attention, plus direction-aware optimization targeting temporal direction sensitivity. Builds a complete pipeline spanning representation, fusion, and optimization rather than fixing only sparse sampling. Targets fragile frame-to-frame change understanding.

entry.title: Memory Augmentation Unlocks Efficient Chain-of-Thought Reasoning

author.name: Simeng Zhang, Yilong Chen, Wenyuan Zhang, Zhenyu Zhang, Yao Chen, Junyuan Shang, Tingwen Liu

entry.summary: Proposes Memory-Augmented Compression, a training-free framework that builds reusable reasoning memories from historical chain-of-thought traces and retrieves them as prefill-side scaffolds, formalizing a Context-Generation Substitution Law. Reduces decode-time generation overhead without the coherence degradation caused by aggressive CoT truncation.

entry.title: NeSAM: Neuro-Symbolic Kinodynamics with Soil Adaptation for Off-Road Mobility

author.name: Chenhui Pan, Tong Xu, Francesco Cancelliere, Xuesu Xiao

entry.summary: NeSAM is a neuro-symbolic framework for off-road vehicle mobility prediction combining differentiable Bekker-Wong terramechanics, learned terrain representations, and a Transformer-based residual dynamics model for long-horizon six-degree-of-freedom kinodynamic prediction over deformable soil. The physics component supplies interpretable soil-dependent forces while residuals correct discrepancies.

entry.title: Terminal Agents: A Survey of AI Agents in Command-Line Environments

author.name: Yi Bin, Xiaoyang Yuan, Haoxi Zeng, Wencheng Ye, Wenqi Shao, Chen Qian, Wei Ye, Yujuan Ding, Zheng Wang, Pengpeng Zeng, Jingkuan Song, Heng Tao Shen

entry.summary: A survey treating terminal agents as systems whose progress-bearing action-observation loop runs through terminal command execution, textual feedback, and stateful environments, establishing workload boundaries and a seven-dimensional terminal competence profile. It connects system architecture, competence acquisition, and evaluation, showing behavior emerges jointly from model, interface, harness, runtime, and environment.

entry.title: VortexChat: An agentic framework for autonomous multi-objective integrated photonic design

author.name: Faqian Chong, Yulun Wu, Shilong Li, Andrew Forbes, Hongsheng Chen, Song Han

entry.summary: VortexChat is an agentic framework for autonomous end-to-end inverse design of integrated photonic devices from natural-language specifications. It couples an LLM decision agent with topology generation, gradient-based refinement, and full-wave electromagnetic simulation in a closed loop, aiming to replace manual simulation-heavy workflows.

entry.title: Is Multimodal Speculative Decoding Ready for Diffusion-Based Parallel Drafting? A Survey and Empirical Diagnosis

author.name: Yantao Li, Huanlin Gao, Fang Zhao, Chao Tan, Qiang Hui, Shuting Liu, Fuyuan Shi, Ting Lu, Shaoan Zhao, Xueqiang Guo, Xinpei Su, Jianbing Zhang, Xinyu Dai, Kai Wang, Shiguo Lian

entry.summary: A survey and empirical diagnosis of whether diffusion-based block-parallel speculative drafting, which achieves up to 3.6x speedup in text-only LLMs, transfers to multimodal models. It maps the open challenges unique to multimodal verification and drafting.

entry.title: Can Scientific Claims Be Removed from Large Language Models? A Systematic Evaluation of Claim-Level Unlearning

author.name: Snigdha Paul, Manasi Patwardhan, Arman Cohan

entry.summary: Introduces a systematic evaluation of claim-level unlearning, asking whether obsolete or retracted scientific claims can be removed from language models while preserving utility, addressing the interconnected nature of scientific claims that instance-level unlearning ignores.

entry.title: VIALS: A Benchmark for Visual Interpretation of Artifacts in the Life Sciences

author.name: Elaine Lau, Thanuka Udumulla, Lee Izhaki-Tavor, Francisco Guzm\'an, Nicholas Magazine, Jonas Mueller

entry.summary: VIALS is a visual question answering benchmark of 161 artifact interpretation tasks spanning gel blots, microscopy, plasmid maps, and flow cytometry plots drawn from real biotech workflows rather than publication figures. It shows frontier vision-language models fail badly on these scientific images while trained scientists succeed easily.

entry.title: CertVLA: Certified Defense against Physical Visual Attacks for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Hui Lu, Zhijie Peng, Yuqi Lin, Zaijia Yang, Jiaming He, Shuhan Ye, Yi Yu, Hanwei Zhu, Bingquan Shen, Alex Kot, Xudong Jiang

entry.summary: CertVLA provides the first certified defense for closed-loop vision-language-action robot policies under bounded physical patch and texture attacks, using deterministic covering masks guaranteeing one attack-free checked prediction, calibrated regions of behaviorally consistent actions, and max-min-max episode score calibration to produce certificates over temporally correlated continuous actions.

entry.title: Advantage-level Aggregation Reinforcement Learning for X-point Target Magnetic Configuration Control in an EXL-50U Experiment-Calibrated Simulation Environment

author.name: Siqi Ding, Xuanhe Wang, Pei Guo, Guoyang Shi, Changquan Yu, Yiting Wang, Xianming Song, Xiang Gu, Zhengyuan Chen, Lei Xing, Yapeng Zhang, Jianguo Chen, Tianyuan Liu

entry.summary: The paper formulates secondary X-point divertor feedback control in the EXL-50U tokamak as multi-objective reinforcement learning in an experiment-calibrated simulation environment, replacing precomputed feedforward plus PID loops. This enables repeatable routine operation managing divertor heat loads in compact high-power tokamaks.

entry.title: MentorPulse: Refreshing Cross-Model Latent Guidance for Long-Form Generation

author.name: Ziwu Liu, Guozhong Li, Chen Qiu, Weiyang Kong, Panos Kalnis

entry.summary: MentorPulse shows static cross-model latent guidance degrades during long-form generation, even hurting a 4B student below its no-guidance baseline, and restores gains via training-free periodic memory refreshes every 16 tokens. It compresses mentor states into capped slot memory updated incrementally as tokens are generated.

entry.title: Causal Modeling of Adverse Pregnancy Outcomes via Adaptive LLM Proposals

author.name: Kavimayil P. Komarasamy, Saurabh Mathur, Ameet Soni, David M. Haas, Kristian Kersting, Sriraam Natarajan

entry.summary: A neurosymbolic framework treats LLMs as adaptive proposal distributions for causal discovery in adverse pregnancy outcomes, generating hypotheses that are scored against empirical data and iteratively refined. This combines broad LLM prior knowledge with data-driven filtering where pure data-driven methods fail due to sparse data. It targets clinically important outcomes like preterm birth and gestational diabetes.

entry.title: SPARCL: Spectral Partitioned Analytic Continual Learning

author.name: James Hartley, Zeropy Surio, Daniel Whitmore, Hannah Clarke, Thomas Reed

entry.summary: SPARCL identifies spectral interference as the true cause of forgetting in analytic continual learning: shared inverse autocorrelation operators let new task samples perturb old-class logits even without revisiting old labels. It proposes spectral partitioning to isolate old dominant eigendirections. Replaces the conventional stochastic-gradient-overwriting narrative for class-incremental learning.

entry.title: SAC-Copula: Quality-Preserving Watermarking for Diffusion Language Models via Smooth Correlated Gumbel Fields

author.name: Baixin Li, Haiyun He

entry.summary: SAC-Copula watermarks diffusion language models using smooth, locally correlated Gumbel perturbation fields built from a Gaussian copula, matching iterative parallel unmasking dynamics better than i.i.d. position-wise perturbations. A covariance-aware SAC-aware detector with native-sample calibration supports detection. Mechanism-level analysis links local correlation to reduced latent perturbation roughness.

entry.title: The Exceedance Design Effect: Effective Sample Size for Thresholds under Clustering

author.name: Adam Noonan

entry.summary: Introduces the exceedance design effect: conformal predictors, abstention gates, and safety filters set thresholds at quantiles of correlated calibration data, invalidating independence assumptions behind promised coverage rates. Adapts survey-statistics effective-sample-size corrections from 1965 to modern ML threshold setting. Practical correction for clustered prompts, documents, or reasoning traces.

entry.title: Decoupled Vision-Language System for Multimodal Understanding and Generation

author.name: Yifan Xu, Baochen Xiong, Xiaoshan Yang, Donglin Di, Yaowei Wang, Changsheng Xu

entry.summary: Libra is a decoupled multimodal LLM architecture with separate vision and language systems connected by cross-modal bridges, using switch attention and switch FFN modules to dynamically route between self-modal modeling and cross-modal interaction. Evaluated in understanding-only and unified understanding-generation configurations. Aims to let each modality learn its own representations without sacrificing alignment.

entry.title: MigrationNarrate: A Dataset for Detection of Migration Narratives in YouTube Videos

author.name: Fatima Haouari, Carolina Scarton, Kalina Bontcheva

entry.summary: IBM Research Zurich fine-tunes SmolDocling, a compact 256M-parameter vision-language model, for end-to-end key-value extraction from document images, jointly solving identification, localization, and association in a single pass without OCR preprocessing. Extends DocTags with key-value-region-link tags and uses synthetic augmentation to overcome data limitations.

entry.title: Koala Gripper: Co-designing Robotic Grippers and Data-Capture Devices for Scaling Dexterous Manipulation Learning

author.name: Amar Hajj-Ahmad, Zubin Kremer Guha, Tim Fofonoff, Zhi Ern Teoh, Ciar\'an T. O'Neill, Ben Thacher, Igor Fala, Vidullan Surendran, Murphy Wonsick, Peter Whitney, David Watkins

entry.summary: Koala Gripper introduces a co-design framework that simultaneously develops handheld data-collection devices and the robotic grippers they emulate, rather than forcing data devices to match existing gripper morphologies. The resulting system improves dexterity and grasp capability over parallel-jaw designs while preserving scalability and ease of use for large-scale demonstration collection.

entry.title: World models of environment, agent and joint agent-environment systems

author.name: Manuel Baltieri, Filippo Torresan, Yivan Zhang, Alexander Boyd, Fernando E. Rosas

entry.summary: Using computational mechanics, this theoretical paper distinguishes world models by which channel they model: the environment channel, the agent channel, or the joint agent-environment process, defining canonical predictive models via epsilon-transducers and epsilon-machines. It recovers standard predictive state representations as a special case while introducing analogous notions for agent-side and joint modeling.

entry.title: SAGE: A Unified Algebra and Self-Adaptive Execution for AI Functions in SQL

author.name: Xiangqi Wang, Nhan H. Pham, Oktie Hassanzadeh, Dharmashankar Subramanian, Xiangliang Zhang

entry.summary: SAGE provides a unified algebra for AI functions inside SQL engines, reducing diverse APIs to three typed primitives (row transformation, aggregation, join) composed with relational operators. It adds confidence-gated execution and adaptive physical strategies, tackling the hard AI_JOIN case analytically.

entry.title: ReCurveflow: A Flow Matching Framework that Learns Curved Reaction Trajectories to Predict Transition State Geometries

author.name: Seungheun Baek, Mogan Gim, Jaewoo Kang

entry.summary: ReCurveflow predicts chemical transition state geometries using flow matching supervised on continuously curved NEB-derived reaction paths rather than straight linear interpolations, plus off-path correction velocity fields for resistance to exposure bias.

entry.title: Belief Without Behavior: Measuring the Translation of Theory of Mind into Coordinated Social Action in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Tonglin Yan, Gregoire Sergeant-Perthuis, David Rudrauf

entry.summary: MOSAIC is a controlled benchmark measuring whether vision-language models can translate theory-of-mind inferences into coordinated social action across verbal, gaze, facial, and spatial channels in cooperative and competitive embodied scenarios, evaluating 13 models including 11 VLMs over 200 trials.

entry.title: CIVA: Critic-Induced Value-Subspace Attacks on Visual World-Model Agents

author.name: Jiancheng Wang, Mingli Zhu, Tong Zhang, Jiaqi Ruan, Wei Wang, Siyuan Liang, Dacheng Tao

entry.summary: CIVA presents white-box online attacks on visual world-model agents like DreamerV3 by exploiting critic-guided perturbations concentrating in a low-dimensional subspace induced by the victim's own critic. Offline probing extracts the subspace via SVD and test-time optimization adjusts only subspace coefficients for temporally smooth effective attacks.

entry.title: When Clean Data Hurts: Learning with Monotone Corruptions Beyond Binary Classification

author.name: Julian Asilis, Shaddin Dughmi, Chirag Pabbaraju

entry.summary: Extending monotone adversarial corruption theory beyond binary classification, this paper studies multiclass classification, regression, and other settings where i.i.d. samples are augmented with correctly labeled examples from adversarial sources, characterizing when corruption forces increased error rates following the tight logarithmic lower bound shown necessary for binary learners.

entry.title: A Critical Audit of Spatiotemporal Forecasting Benchmark Datasets and Baselines

author.name: Kenneth Martin, Simon Heilig, Asja Fischer, Michel F. C. Haddad, Adam M. Sykulski, Moshe Eliasof

entry.summary: Audits the small set of spatiotemporal forecasting benchmarks (Chickenpox, PedalMe, WikiMaths, METR-LA, PEMS-BAY) dominating GNN evaluation, analyzing them via classical time-series methods to explain why spatially-unaware linear baselines remain competitive and exposing weaknesses in current protocols.

entry.title: ConceptTS: LLM-Guided Concept Bottlenecks for Interpretable Multivariate Time-Series Forecasting

author.name: Yichen Jiang, Yueqiao Chen, Dongyu Liu

entry.summary: ConceptTS uses an LLM to propose named, human-readable concepts and generate executable labeling rules for interpretable multivariate time-series forecasting, organizing predictions around concept bottlenecks without manual annotation. Concepts are organized hierarchically and supervise the forecasting model directly. Aims to make opaque forecasters explainable in terms practitioners can inspect.

entry.title: Anchoring Instruction Outside Mask: Exact Reference Caching for Efficient In-Context Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Yangshuai Liu, Zheming Li, Jiaao Li, Kang He, Ziliang Lai, Zhitai Liu, Chengru Song

entry.summary: Anchors instructions outside masks for in-context diffusion transformers, enabling exact reference K/V caching across denoising steps while letting references attend to text instructions, resolving a limitation of structured sparse attention and cutting computation growth with reference count.

entry.title: MultiCube: Compositional 3D Generation With Part-Level Semantic and Spatial Control

author.name: Ava Pun, Kangle Deng, Yiheng Zhu, Jun-Yan Zhu, Maneesh Agrawala, Tinghui Zhou

entry.summary: MultiCube enables compositional 3D generation with independent part-level semantic and spatial control, taking a global prompt, part schema, and bounding-box layout to output decomposed objects suitable for professional creative workflows. Strong team from CMU.

entry.title: DreamBench-SWE: A Multi-Session Memory-Hygiene Benchmark for Software Agents

author.name: Sarthak Singh

entry.summary: DreamBench-SWE benchmarks software-agent memory hygiene across multiple sessions where later tasks depend on non-inferable earlier-session evidence, scored by executable hidden oracles. Notably, it reports null results: neither the primary contrast nor external memory approaches showed significant gains, with preregistered successor audits confirming no memory method exceeded baseline rates.

entry.title: UpgradeBench: A Decision-Centric Benchmark for Upgrading Fine-Tuned LLM Specialists

author.name: Ye Chen, Weining Zhang

entry.summary: UpgradeBench is a decision-centric longitudinal benchmark covering four consecutive Qwen releases plus OLMo checkpoints, studying whether specialists should be retained, ported, refreshed, or retrained when base models update. It disentangles performance gains, asset transfer, and migration cost questions across real release sequences.

entry.title: When Trust Meets Truth: Trust-Truth Separability in LLM-as-Judge

author.name: Xin Sun, Di Wu, Yuchen Guo, Jiahuan Pei, Isao Echizen, Abdallah El Ali, Saku Sugawara

entry.summary: Shows that LLM-as-Judge trust scores and truth verdicts are more tightly coupled than human behavioral reference data, and that changing only source cues (human vs AI origin) shifts not just trust but truth classifications and correct-side probabilities, undermining their assumed independence.

entry.title: Who Do Language Models Think Is Competent? A Mechanistic Analysis of Occupational Bias

author.name: Keren Fuentes, Aaron Mueller

entry.summary: This mechanistic study decomposes occupational bias into internal competence representations and observable outputs, deriving causal steering vectors for expertise representations verified to mediate behavior in QA and hiring tasks. Across open-weight models it finds representational biases persist even when behavioral evaluations pass.

entry.title: Jacobian-guided Noise Injection for Quantization Robustness in Large Language Models

author.name: Deepanshu Pandey, Arnav Chavan, Nahush Lele, Sankalp Dayal, Deepak Gupta

entry.summary: Identifying softmax attention as a quantization bottleneck due to outlier sensitivity and state-dependent Jacobian behavior, this paper proves suppressing the attention Jacobian Frobenius norm bounds quantization-induced degradation. Jacobian-Guided Noise Injection adds zero-mean Gaussian noise to pre-attention logits with principled variance selection during training.

entry.title: Is Visual Prompting All You Need? Studying VLM Spatial Reasoning under Progressive Visual Scaffolds

author.name: Lars Benedikt Kaesberg, Tianyu Yang, Florian Valentin Wunderlich, Terry Ruas, Jan Philip Wahle, Daniel Kurzawe, Bela Gipp

entry.summary: Studying grid-based visual spatial planning on SPaRC with progressive visual scaffolds that preserve the visual modality while exposing spatial structure, this paper improves VLM accuracy by up to 34 percentage points and complements GRPO-based training. It isolates how visual presentation shapes reasoning failures independent of the underlying problem.

entry.title: Shared Physics Responses Recover Hidden Rankings in Neural Operator Libraries

author.name: Hanbing Liang, Fujun Liu

entry.summary: Companion to the backdoor work, this paper shows a shared anchor-based physical diagnostic recovers over 99.6 percent of pairwise preferences and 99.0 percent of optimal checkpoints when selecting among neural-operator libraries without high-fidelity references, and the corrected proxy often beats the best individual candidate.

entry.title: COEC: Calibrated Orthogonal-Equivalence Compensation for Structured Pruning of Large Language Models

author.name: Peiqi Yu, Nam Ling, Wei Wang, Wei Jiang

entry.summary: COEC is a training-free compensation framework for structured pruning of LLMs that applies alternating left and right orthogonal rotations to the retained weight, optimizing the right rotation on a Stiefel manifold and rescaling singular values. Unlike prior additive or single-rotation fixes, it allows the input singular frame to adapt after column removal. This improves accuracy retention at reduced inference cost.

entry.title: PerturbRx: Learning Treatment-Conditioned Latent Transitions for Patient Drug Response Prediction

author.name: Yoshitaka Inoue, Minoh Jeong, Alfred Hero, Rui Kuang, Augustin Luna

entry.summary: PerturbRx learns treatment-conditioned latent transitions from context-matched but cell-unpaired control and treated single-cell populations, then transfers the frozen transition predictor to pretreatment patient profiles to predict drug response without post-treatment measurements. Explicitly models molecular changes under therapy rather than relying on static profiles. Addresses scarcity and tumor heterogeneity in patient-level response prediction.

entry.title: Tree-of-Concerns: Hierarchical Multi-Agent Debate for Unstated-Limitation Extraction in Scientific Critique

author.name: Sahil Mishra, Niranjan Rajeev, Tanmoy Chakraborty

entry.summary: Tree-of-Concerns deploys skeptic personas operating category-specific analytical lenses as parallel debate trees to extract unstated limitations from scientific papers, with a panel-review mechanism correcting category drift and severity miscalibration. Introduces ToC-Bench, 414 papers with 1,905 unstated limitations sourced from peer reviews. Targets systematic critique as literature volume grows and limitations go under-reported.

entry.title: Annotations as Rollouts: Efficient and Scalable Reinforcement Learning for Video MLLMs

author.name: Yunheng Li, Guohong Mu, Hao Li, Shengsheng Qian, Dingwen Zhang, Qibin Hou, Ming-Ming Cheng

entry.summary: OraRL improves sample efficiency of RL post-training for video MLLMs by treating ground-truth annotations themselves as oracle rollouts inside on-policy groups, not just reward signals. Carefully handles the baseline-inversion problem that naive oracle integration would cause.

entry.title: SDAD: Spec-Driven Agentic Development for the AI-Native SDLC

author.name: Vu Hung Nguyen, Thanh Nguyen

entry.summary: This report formalizes Spec-Driven Agentic Development (SDAD), a methodology for the AI-native software development lifecycle that combines disciplined up-front specification with agentic implementation. It proposes a pipeline of intent capture, machine-readable specifications, agentic synthesis, and independent multi-agent verification with human sign-off, arguing that specification quality is now the key input for autonomous delivery.

entry.title: Difficulty-Aware Semantic-ID Optimization for Generative Recommendation

author.name: Xin Yu, Stephen Li, Sina Aghaei, Zifan Zhu, Jiamu Bai, Guanjie Huang, Bo Peng, Yiyao Liu, Lingzhou Xue

entry.summary: The paper analyzes why the standard SFT-then-GRPO recipe underperforms for semantic-ID generative recommendation, showing target identifiers are often missing from top beam candidates so item-level rewards yield degenerate signal. It proposes Difficulty-Aware Semantic-ID Optimization to match reward structure to tree-structured retrieval difficulty.

entry.title: TRACE: Agentic Catalog Enrichment with Multi-source Evidence Grounding

author.name: Rohan Kumar, Steven Xu, Kyle MacDonald, Matthew Long, Bernice Chow, Mac VanRenterghem, Sudeep Das

entry.summary: TRACE is an agentic LLM framework for automated e-commerce catalog attribute enrichment, with a ScoutAgent triangulating multimodal evidence across catalogs, feeds, and web search and a JudgeAgent verifying each proposed attribute value. It addresses attribute sparsity that undermines search and recommendation.

entry.title: No Judgment Without a Reason: Counterfactual Receipts for Versioned AI Evaluators

author.name: Ye Chen, Weining Zhang

entry.summary: Formalizes evaluator reasoning accountability through grounds, norms, and authority, yielding an eight-cell counterfactual judgment cube and minimal judgment receipts that reproduce revised verdicts. ReasonBench accompanies the framework, with certification cost bounds for black-box evaluators.

entry.title: Large Language Models at the Intersection of Software Engineering and Software Security:An Evidence-Centered Structured Survey and Research Agenda

author.name: Wei Lin, Tao Zhou, Zhaofei Xie, Changgui Hong

entry.summary: An evidence-centered structured survey synthesizing work through May 2026 on LLMs spanning software engineering and software security, with a task taxonomy, artifact-granularity analysis, and an assurance framework plus research agenda as code agents enter security-sensitive workflows.

entry.title: Personalized Privacy Control in LLMs via Attention Head Intervention

author.name: Junseok Kim, Nakyeong Yang, Kyomin Jung

entry.summary: This work introduces personalized privacy, extending contextual privacy norms with user-specific disclosure preferences, and presents P3Bench, a benchmark pairing contextual and personal disclosure policies. It finds prompt-based enforcement unreliable and demonstrates attention head interventions as a more effective control mechanism for agentic LLM privacy.

entry.title: AEGIS: Preventing Cross-Domain Resource Abuse in MCP

author.name: Shriti Priya, Teryl Taylor, Frederico Araujo

entry.summary: AEGIS addresses cross-domain resource abuse in Model Context Protocol tools, where malicious agents can overload backends via excessive search radii, long video requests, or modality-specific vectors. It proposes mitigation mechanisms accounting for divergent abuse characteristics across text, image, video, and location modalities.

entry.title: Making Deployments Safe at Meta: Health Checks for Continuous Change-Safety

author.name: Prakash KL, Anton Korenkov, Uttam Thakore, Christopher Hegre

entry.summary: Meta describes its Service Health Checker infrastructure mediating release velocity versus reliability across thousands of heterogeneous services, covering templated metric checks, thresholds, workflow predicates, and automatic rollback integrated with tiered phased rollouts, plus operational problems encountered at scale.

entry.title: Denoising the Future: Context-Aware Spectral Diffusion for Temporal Knowledge Graph Extrapolation

author.name: Yanglei Gan, Peng He, Run Lin, Peiyuan Jiang, Yifan Wang, Qiao Liu

entry.summary: FreqDiff is a frequency-aware diffusion framework for temporal knowledge graph extrapolation that reformulates future object prediction as query-slot denoising with a dual-stream denoiser combining temporal dependency modeling and spectral calibration. It addresses the problem that aggregated conditioning dilutes query-specific historical evidence in existing diffusion-based TKG methods.

entry.title: Structured but Fragile: On the Limits of LLMs in Cybersecurity Decision-Making

author.name: Pasquale Malacaria, Yunxiao Zhang

entry.summary: This study tests whether LLMs perform structured security reasoning when selecting defense controls under budget constraints on attack graphs from real threat scenarios including ransomware and supply-chain compromise.
