author.name: Xin Yang, Letian Li, Zimo Ji, Terry Jingchen Zhang, Wenyuan Jiang

entry.summary: Reframes many LLM multi-agent system failures as classical concurrency control problems: agents read and write shared state while long inference windows create stale reads, lost updates, and inconsistent outcomes. The authors argue frameworks should adopt explicit conflict detection, isolation guarantees, and structured shared-resource access as first-class design elements.

entry.title: UMER: Unifying Embedding and Ranking via Pair-Aware Discriminative Reasoning for Universal Multimodal Retrieval

author.name: Libiao Chen, Xiyang Liu, Yanheng Wei, Tao Wang, Zhenyu Tang

entry.summary: FM-Bench evaluates long-horizon agent decision-making by having an LLM run a football club for twenty in-game years through 26 tools and hundreds of decision points, with a deterministic engine accumulating consequences into a single score without any LLM judge or human rater. Fifteen frontier models are tested in a solo track and a competing-agents track where choices affect rivals.

entry.title: Preference Reasoning under Indeterminacy in Large Language Models

author.name: Hadi Hosseini, Samarth Khanna, Xiyuan Wang

entry.summary: Studies preference reasoning in LLMs under indeterminacy, distinguishing epistemic indeterminacy from incomplete or partially expressed preferences and structural indeterminacy where no solution exists under standard social choice concepts. Across a task hierarchy, state-of-the-art models are shown to struggle when correctness is not well defined, which matters for agent alignment and multi-agent coordination.

entry.title: A Theory of Post-hoc Debate Judgement

author.name: Xiang Yin, Adam Dejl, Antonio Rago, Lihu Chen, Francesca Toni

entry.summary: Develops a formal theory of post-hoc debate judgement for settings where agents argue with pros and cons and an external judge, often an LLM, determines the outcome. It identifies formal properties around reproducibility, robustness, and groundedness that judgement functions should satisfy, then tests existing judging approaches against them.

entry.title: Robust Risk Under Evolving Uncertainty: A Wasserstein Counterpart of the Entropic Value-at-Risk

author.name: Deep Kumar Ganguly, Jan K\v{r}et\'insk\'y

entry.summary: Introduces a Wasserstein counterpart to the entropic value-at-risk, replacing the relative-entropy ambiguity ball with an optimal-transport ball so that catastrophic outcomes assigned zero probability by the nominal model can still be hedged. The resulting coherent risk measure has a variational dual mirroring the entropic formula and a defined position in the risk measure hierarchy.

entry.title: Self- and Other-Labels Induce Bidirectional Bias in LLM Judges

author.name: Songeun Chae, Min Kim, Donghoon Jung, Seojin Choi, Seohyon Jung

entry.summary: Isolates self-preference in LLM judges from stylistic confounds by having ten models evaluate narrative constraint selections rather than generated prose, since these carry model-specific signatures without stylistic fingerprints. Two experiments show that self-preference behaves differently under blind versus labeled conditions, revealing bias induced by both self-labels and other-labels in either direction.

entry.title: LEDGER: Claim-to-Evidence Trace Graphs for Auditing LLM Agents

author.name: Daehong Kim, Haichao Miao, Shusen Liu

entry.summary: Builds layered trace graphs that link an agent's stated conclusions back to the specific actions, artifacts and validation steps that support them, aimed at human reviewers auditing long tool-use sessions. It argues raw observability events are insufficient because reviewers still must reconstruct relevance.

entry.title: DART-SD: Diamond-topology Aware Retrieval and Tuning for Self-Distillation of Multi-Turn Tool-Calling Agents

author.name: Hangrui Xu, Jiarui Wang, Yang Yang, Chuanbo Zhu, Fangda Chen, Ziqi Wu, Jingming Cai, Yan Song

entry.summary: Argues that training tool-calling agents by imitating full trajectories collapses the combinatorial space of valid orderings for order-independent subgoals, penalizing legitimate alternative solutions. The proposed self-distillation framework retrieves and corrects locally instead of forcing whole trajectories.

entry.title: From Storage to Access: Verifiable Activation of Parametric Knowledge in LLMs via Explicit Priming and Implicit Reasoning

author.name: Zuocheng Ying, Yang Yang, Yumou Wu, Chuanbo Zhu, Jiarui Wang, Ziqi Wu, Jingming Cai, Junqing Yu, Zikai Song

entry.summary: Proposes a two-stage reinforcement learning scheme in which a priming policy first explicitly writes out relevant parametric knowledge when retrieval is insufficient, and that elicitation ability is then internalized into implicit reasoning. This makes it possible to verify whether a correct answer came from model parameters or from the provided context.

entry.title: SkillForge: Self-Distilling Agents for Project-Specific Issue Resolution

author.name: Silin Chen, Han Li, Xiaodong Gu, Yuling Shi, Haibing Guan

entry.summary: SkillForge has a coding agent synthesize its own project-specific practice issues from a repository and distill the resulting solution experience into reusable skills, rather than waiting for real issues or paying heavy per-issue exploration costs. It targets the repository-knowledge gap that limits LLM agents on software issue resolution.

entry.title: Detecting Backdoors in Object Detection via Pre-NMS Prediction Distribution Shift

author.name: Longtian Wang, Zhengyu Zhao, Chenhao Lin, Le Yang, Shiwei Wang, Yuhan Zhi, Xiaofei Xie, Chao Shen

entry.summary: DistScan detects backdoors in object detectors by observing that backdoor injection shifts the pre-NMS predicted class distribution away from training class frequencies even on clean inputs, requiring no trigger inversion. This makes it applicable to scene-level attacks where one trigger corrupts every object in the frame.

entry.title: Uncovering the Limits of Proof Sharing for Neural Networks

author.name: Kanak Das, Shubham Ugare, Bor-Yuh Evan Chang, Sasa Misailovic, Gagandeep Singh, Manu Sridharan

entry.summary: Systematically studies when proof sharing accelerates incomplete neural network robustness verification by reusing intermediate abstract templates across queries, finding that subsumption rates vary widely across architectures, datasets, properties, and training methods. The authors propose a jointly-stable-neuron metric that explains much of this variation.

entry.title: Evidence Before Expansion: Reuse, Spawn, or Defer in Lifelong Expert Pools

author.name: Kentaro Oda

entry.summary: Proposes a decision layer for streaming systems that maintain pools of expert models, framing the choice to reuse an existing expert, spawn a new one, or defer as sequential hypothesis tests on a mechanism-level discrepancy with an indifference zone. Deferral becomes a principled state where neither betting e-process has accumulated enough evidence, with finite-time anytime-validity guarantees.

entry.title: Ask Self, Ask Others: Relation Is All You Need

author.name: Yuting Ge, Pengju Yang, Mingkai Nie

entry.summary: Proposes Relation, a token-mixing primitive that organizes pairwise evidence into explicit self and exchange relations before deriving information flow, yielding several variants including linear, hybrid, and cache-based forms. Small decoder-only models at roughly 10M to 100M parameters reportedly beat multi-head attention on validation loss, with a fast kernel implementation.

entry.title: Causal Inference under Interference with Learned Exposure Mappings

author.name: Cong Cao

entry.summary: Studies how uncertainty in learned pollution transport processes propagates into exposure mappings and spillover estimates in causal inference under interference, comparing mechanistic PDE models with neural operator approaches on simulations and California particulate matter data. It finds that models with nearly identical predictive accuracy imply substantially different spillover effect estimates.

entry.title: Clustering and Token Denoising for Faster and More Robust VLMs

author.name: Baptiste Rossigneux, Inna Kucher, Vincent Lorrain, Emmanuel Casseau

entry.summary: ClustRS is a training-free two-stage visual token pruning method for vision-language models that clusters tokens with attention weighting to pick representatives and then applies a one-pass residual shrinkage denoising step. It targets edge deployment where processing hundreds of visual tokens is prohibitive.

entry.title: Concentrated Liquidity Provision: a Reinforcement Learning Perspective

author.name: Georgios Chionas, Charalampos Kleitsikas, Stefanos Leonardos, Leandro S\'anchez-Betancourt, Carmine Ventre

entry.summary: Formulates concentrated liquidity provision in automated market makers as a stochastic impulse control problem and solves it with reinforcement learning, emphasizing interpretable policies. Learned strategies vary allocation with mispricing, rebalancing cost, uncertainty, and inventory exposure.

entry.title: Learning Hierarchical Skill Policies with Offline Quality-Diversity Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Tanachai Anakewat, Takayuki Osa, Tatsuya Harada

entry.summary: QDOS extracts diverse low-level skills from offline datasets using quality-diversity optimization rather than a plain trajectory autoencoder, so that skill quality is less dependent on dataset quality, then trains a high-level policy over those skills. It targets robust offline-to-online hierarchical reinforcement learning.

entry.title: Learning Deterministic and Stochastic Forced Hamiltonian Systems

author.name: Benedikt Brantner, Tomasz Tyranowski

entry.summary: Develops a geometric framework for learning forced Hamiltonian systems, both deterministic and stochastic, based on the Lagrange-d Alembert principle and variational integrators. It proves convergence for first-order one-step methods and a universal approximation theorem for the proposed structure-preserving network family, including parameter-dependent variants.

entry.title: Learning piecewise-smooth dynamical systems

author.name: Davide Murari, Erik Jansson, Chris Budd OBE, Carola-Bibiane Sch\"onlieb

entry.summary: Tackles data-driven identification of dynamical systems with discontinuous dynamics, which requires recovering both the governing equations and the switching hyperplanes separating regimes. Such piecewise-smooth systems arise in friction mechanics and climate dynamics but are largely ignored by smooth system identification methods.

entry.title: ReCache: Efficient KV Cache Reuse and Compression for Tool-Augmented LLM Agents

author.name: Yichu Fang, Sitong Wei, Haozhe Hu, Xiaoyu Shen

entry.summary: ReCache enables reuse of KV cache states for tool and skill schemas that recur in varying orders across agent requests, by removing cross-resource attention and assigning resource-local positions to produce composition-invariant KV blocks. It further prunes to invocation-critical fields and restricts visibility to selected layer and head-group routes to cut memory. This addresses a real bottleneck where standard prefix caching fails for agentic prompts.

entry.title: When Text and Numbers Disagree: Evidence Arbitration in Large Language Models

author.name: Mattia Carletti, Edward Phillips, Fredrik K. Gustafsson, Patitapaban Palo, Lei Clifton, Danielle Belgrave, Xiao Gu, David A. Clifton

entry.summary: Introduces a controlled synthetic benchmark where latent risk trajectories generate both numerical time series and textual summaries, letting the authors create conflicts in which exactly one evidence source matches ground truth while independently varying modality, recency, stated source reliability and provenance. Across open-weight instruction-tuned models, arbitration behavior is systematic rather than random, revealing consistent biases in which evidence type wins. This matters for tool-using and clinical decision-support deployments.

entry.title: ContractScrub: A benchmark for final review of legal contracts

author.name: Yejin Bang, Kirsty Fielding, Brandan Oliver, Brian Birke, Nabeel Seedat, Andrew M. Bean

entry.summary: ContractScrub is presented as the first benchmark for contract scrubbing, the final review of transactional agreements for internal errors and inconsistencies, a routine but economically valuable legal task that appears well suited to long-context LLMs. The task demands consistency checking, entity tracking and attention to detail across long documents. It supplies missing evaluation for a heavily hyped automation target.

entry.title: When Guidance Goes Off-Scale: Recalibrating Diffusion Transformers under Analog Compute-in-Memory Nonidealities

author.name: Wenshuai Yao, Wenyong Zhou

entry.summary: Characterizes how analog compute-in-memory nonidealities distort diffusion transformer sampling, showing that conditional and unconditional predictions stay near their clean values individually while their difference, the classifier-free guidance residual, is disproportionately attenuated. This suggests recalibrating guidance rather than only improving weight fidelity.

entry.title: V-REX: Efficient Specialist VLM Training for Veterinary X-Rays

author.name: Tim Elsner, Nicole McNally, Andre Dourson, Michael Fitzke

entry.summary: V-REX argues that domain-expert vision-language models need not be fine-tuned giants: by redesigning tokenization, pretraining, grounding, and inference for veterinary radiology, a much smaller model trained from scratch outperforms far larger generalist foundation models. It reports better data utilization and training efficiency across the pipeline.

entry.title: RoMAN-Flow: Taming Autoregressive Normalizing Flows for Offline Reinforcement Learning in Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Shaoxuan Wang, Guangting Zheng, Rui Huang, Zhipeng Tang, Sha Zhang, Jiajun Deng, Yanyong Zhang

entry.summary: RoMAN-Flow makes autoregressive normalizing flow policies practical for offline reinforcement learning in robotic manipulation by attacking their sequential sampling bottleneck during both policy optimization and deployment. Unlike diffusion and flow-matching policies, AR flows provide exact likelihoods needed for likelihood-based offline RL post-training.

entry.title: HiTac-WAM: A Hierarchical Tactile World Action Model for Contact-Rich Robot Manipulation

author.name: Chao Xue, Chaofan Zhang, Wenxuan Ma, Guocai Yao, Shaowei Cui, Shuo Wang

entry.summary: HiTac-WAM forecasts future tactile states for each candidate action chunk before execution, factorizing prediction into contact state, a 3D deformation field, and slip risk arranged as a stop-gradient conditioned hierarchy. Directed attention lets tactile queries read the video-action context of each candidate, extending world-action models to contact-rich manipulation.

entry.title: FinSkillBench: Evaluating AI Agents and Domain Skills for Investment Management

author.name: Jermyn Zhen Yong Bek, Zhuang Qiang Bok, Zhongtian Sun

entry.summary: FinSkillBench is an evaluation suite of 2,603 task episodes across portfolio construction, risk management, and fundamental analysis, each with point-in-time inputs, hidden ground truth, and a task-specific verifier. It compares agents with no skills, curated skill packs, and other conditions to test whether domain skill scaffolding actually improves investment management performance.

entry.title: Safety Alignment Illusion: The Cross-Lingual Safety Gap in LLMs

author.name: Namya Bhatnagar

entry.summary: Shows that English-centric safety alignment leaves LLMs vulnerable in Indian languages, where the same harmful requests can bypass refusal behavior and produce stereotype-reinforcing outputs. Introduces INCLUDE, a multilingual benchmark for quantifying Indian-centric sociocultural bias, with implications for deployed voice and dialogue systems.

entry.title: Global Index on Responsible AI 2026 : Conceptual Framework and Methodology

author.name: Fola Adeleke, Rachel Adams, Ayantola Alayande, Daniela Benavente, Ana Florido, Nicol\'as Grossman, Leah Junck

entry.summary: Documents the methodology for the second edition of a global index scoring countries on responsible AI governance across five dimensions and 38 indicators, distinguishing whether frameworks merely exist from whether they are implemented. It includes an independent statistical pre-audit of the framework.

entry.title: SeisEvo: Evolution of Seismic Data Reconstruction Algorithms by Agents

author.name: Yingjie Xu, Siwei Yu, Jianwei Ma

entry.summary: Uses an LLM-driven multi-agent search to evolve the algorithm itself for seismic data reconstruction, editing only user-permitted components of a classical method and rejecting physically invalid candidates. It contrasts with deep learning approaches that hide the rule inside learned weights.

entry.title: FairGlucose: A CGM Fairness Benchmark Reveals Subgroup Disparities Hidden in Population-Level Validation

author.name: Junjie Luo, Xuzhe Zhi, Rui Han, Abhimanyu Kumbara, Anand K. Iyer, Mansur E. Shomali, Ritu Agarwal, Guodong Gordon Gao

entry.summary: Introduces a continuous glucose monitoring benchmark deliberately balanced across age, gender and diabetes type, and evaluates 33 forecasting models. Aggregate out-of-distribution metrics look stable while subgroup ratios vary widely, showing population-level validation can hide disparities.

entry.title: Low-Power, Neuromorphic, Acoustic Anomaly Detection for Persistent Machine Monitoring

author.name: Steven C. Nesbit (Information Sciences, CAI-3, Los Alamos National Laboratory, Los Alamos, USA), Victor M. Vergara (AeroVironment Inc., Albuquerque, USA), Michael A. Felix (University of New Mexico COSMIAC Research Center, Albuquerque, USA), Evan T. Kain (Air Force Research Laboratory, Kirtland AFB, USA), Luis R. Garc\'ia Carrillo (Air Force Research Laboratory, Kirtland AFB, USA), Gerd J. Kunde (Nuclear and Particle Physics and Applications, P-3, Los Alamos National Laboratory, Los Alamos, USA), Andrew T. Sornborger (Information Sciences, CAI-3, Los Alamos National Laboratory, Los Alamos, USA)

entry.summary: Demonstrates always-on acoustic machine fault detection running an autoencoder on a neuromorphic processor, with normalization, inference and thresholding performed on chip. It reaches very high accuracy on a clean benchmark and exceeds reported baselines on a noisy 2026 challenge task.

entry.title: ERASE: EaRly bAckpropagation SchEdule for Faster Training of Modern Recommendation Systems

author.name: Ergan Shang, Flavio Sales Truzzi

entry.summary: Reinterprets the detachment idea from forward-forward training as a GPU scheduling primitive: detaching a block removes downstream gradient dependencies so its backward pass can launch early on a separate stream and overlap with later forward work. This targets accelerator underutilization when training small proxy recommendation models.

entry.title: Coverage-Driven RTL Assertion Generation with Formal Exploration and Neuro-Symbolic Refinement

author.name: Zhiyuan Yan, Ziyue Zheng, Hongce Zhang

entry.summary: Combines formal trace generation, syntax-guided synthesis and an agent-style refinement loop to generate hardware assertions driven by remaining coverage gaps rather than one-shot prompting. The aim is complete and reliable assertion sets that expose hard-to-reach design behaviors.

entry.title: OmniHandwritingOCR: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Evaluating Multimodal LLMs in Handwritten OCR Scenarios

author.name: Zinuo Guo, Min Zhang, Bo Jiang

entry.summary: Releases a diagnostic benchmark of about 77,600 labeled handwritten images spanning six subtasks, including multilingual handwriting, writer errors and complex mathematical expressions, for evaluating multimodal LLMs as OCR systems. Existing OCR benchmarks skew toward printed or clean single-line text.

entry.title: A Critical Synthesis of Uncertainty Quantification and Foundation Models for Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Steven Landgraf, Joceline Hinz, Markus Ulrich

entry.summary: Provides the first systematic evaluation of uncertainty quantification methods layered on a segmentation foundation model, fine-tuning a lightweight decoder on a frozen large vision encoder. It examines whether standard UQ techniques transfer to foundation-model segmentation under domain shift.

entry.title: AlphaClifford: Efficient Clifford Synthesis and Transpilation with Model-based RL

author.name: Daniele Lizzio Bosco, Jacopo Cossio, Carla Piazza, Giuseppe Serra

entry.summary: AlphaClifford applies model-based reinforcement learning with Monte Carlo tree search to synthesize and transpile Clifford quantum circuits from H, S, and CNOT gates, exploiting symplectic group structure to shape the search space. It targets lower gate counts than standard algorithmic synthesis such as Aaronson-Gottesman.

entry.title: Holtercare-Bench: A Multimodal Benchmark for Evaluating Long-Term Dynamic ECG Analysis

author.name: Yihan Xie, Hanwen Cui, Runze Ye, Juekai Lin, Haoyang Wang, Jinhao Mao, Bo Zhang, Wenqiao Zhang, Xiaogang Guo, Jun Xiao, Lei Zhang

entry.summary: Releases Holtercare-23K, a dataset of nearly 23,000 question-answer pairs from 788 clinical Holter recordings with aligned signal, video, and text, plus Holtercare-Bench for evaluating temporal localization, diagnosis, and summarization on long-term ECG. Zero-shot evaluation shows current multimodal LLMs struggle with long-duration physiological reasoning.

entry.title: Mechanistic Tomography: Designed Measurement for Control-Oriented Interpretability

author.name: Vijay Erramilli

entry.summary: Reframes mechanistic interpretability tools such as activation patching, gradients, Hessian-vector products, and subset interventions as instances of a common linear measurement problem, where an intervention design matrix maps an unknown internal map to noisy observations. This measurement view suggests principled experiment design and error accounting for interpretability studies.

entry.title: Continuous Adversarial MeanFlow Transfer

author.name: Yara Bahram, Zahra Dehghani, M\'elodie Desbos, Eric Granger, Pablo Piantanida, Mohammadhadi Shateri

entry.summary: Addresses two obstacles to adapting fast generators to new domains with little data: acceleration methods being tied to specific source parameterizations, and adversarial refinement being defined only for instantaneous-velocity flows rather than MeanFlow average velocities. The proposed MeanFlow-Transfer maps heterogeneous pretrained outputs into a shared velocity representation and adds an adversarial objective compatible with finite-interval averages.

entry.title: RecPFN: Prior-Fitted Networks for In-Context-Based Recommendations

author.name: En Zhi Tan, Jia Xiang Lim, Bryan Lijie Chew, Tze Minh Ng, Benjamin Yan Han Yap

entry.summary: RecPFN brings prior-fitted network style in-context learning to sequential recommendation by pretraining a small decoder-only transformer entirely on synthetic clickstreams drawn from a broad structural causal prior. At inference it conditions on a handful of domain sequences and predicts next items in one forward pass with no weight updates, reporting state-of-the-art zero-shot results across eight benchmarks.

entry.title: Truncate Bad, Upweight Good: BoN-Style Distillation via Rank-Based Classification

author.name: Yarin Bar, Yaniv Romano

entry.summary: TUP distills best-of-N sampling into a single policy by truncating low-ranked completions out of the target distribution entirely while upweighting good ones, instead of using smooth full-support rank reweighting. The design trades reduced lower-tail mass against reliance on a single reward model at the top of the ranking.

entry.title: PETA:Parameter-Efficient Test-Time Adaptation for Virtual Screening

author.name: Jia-Qi Lin, Yinghua Yao, Chang-Dong Wang, Yew-Soon Ong, Yuangang Pan

entry.summary: Recasts pocket-specific specialization of pretrained virtual screening models such as DrugCLIP as a test-time adaptation problem, and proposes PETA to adapt only a small set of parameters per protein target. This avoids full retraining while enabling target-specific customization for ligand ranking.

entry.title: Deep-MKV-TS: Path-Dependent McKean--Vlasov Control for Financial Time Series Generation

author.name: Samer El Boustany, Th\'eo Basseras, Samy Mekkaoui, Alexandre Alouadi, Yadh Hafsi, Huy\^en Pham

entry.summary: Deep-MKV-TS generates financial scenarios using a path-dependent McKean-Vlasov control formulation that keeps an interpretable reference drift while adjusting volatility to match path and volatility features of real data. It is solved with a neural sample-based stochastic maximum principle and validated against exactly computable oracles.

entry.title: Question-Guided Evidence Acquisition for Multimodal Visual Question Answering

author.name: Alin-Ionut Popa

entry.summary: Argues that document visual question answering fails because models encode a page once and answer from that single fast pass, missing small text, tables, and layout cues. Q-Guide is a lightweight agent that reads the question, decides what evidence to look at next, and spends extra inference-time compute acquiring it before answering.

entry.title: Task-CoEvolve: Efficient Harness Optimization via Adaptive Validation Task Selection

author.name: Atsuyuki Miyai, Kiyoharu Aizawa, Toshihiko Yamasaki

entry.summary: Task-CoEvolve makes LLM agent harness optimization cheaper by co-evolving the validation task set with the harness: it adaptively selects informative tasks and estimates full-set performance from partial evaluations. This targets the large evaluation bill incurred when iteratively rewriting agent scaffolding code. It matters as scaffold-level optimization becomes a mainstream way to gain performance without touching model weights.

entry.title: LoRA-GA$^2$: Low Rank Adaptation with Multi-step Gradient Adaptive Alignment

author.name: Haonan He, Xinyue Fan

entry.summary: LoRA-GA squared initializes and aligns low-rank adapters using multi-step gradient information gathered by a lightweight probe, rather than the one-step gradient approximations used by prior alignment methods. The goal is to close the residual gap between LoRA and full fine-tuning by better matching the true update dynamics. It is a drop-in improvement for parameter-efficient tuning.

entry.title: Outcome Monitors: Recovery Affordances for Silent Tool Failures

author.name: Sugam Panthi, Rabab Abdelfattah

entry.summary: Outcome Monitors detect silent tool failures, such as cached error pages or negative prices arriving in valid format, by checking outcome contracts mined from task-disjoint traces or public schemas, then issuing a nonbinding receipt naming the violated property and public recovery tools. In prespecified evaluations with injected failures, ToolMaze completion rises from about 11 percent to 28 percent across four models in two provider families, with double-digit gains on tau-bench retail tiers. Silent bad data is a major unaddressed agent failure mode.

entry.title: TempJail: Temporal Jailbreak Attack against Large Vision-Language Models via Subtitle Scheduling

author.name: Ling Zhou, Yihao Huang, Jingling Sun, Zhiwen Tian, Yi Zeng, Qihe Liu, Shijie Zhou

entry.summary: TempJail shows that jailbreak success against large vision-language models depends not only on the semantics of text embedded in video but also on its temporal presentation, and exploits subtitles to schedule harmful content across precise durations and timing slots without visible manipulation. This opens a video-specific attack surface that text- and image-level defenses do not cover. It highlights a gap in multimodal safety evaluation.

entry.title: Break It Down, Pass It On: Cross-Task Skill Transfer in LLM Agents

author.name: Yiyang Feng, Biddut Sarker Bijoy, Niranjan Balasubramanian, Jiawei Zhou

entry.summary: A controlled study of when skills induced from completed tasks actually transfer across tasks for LLM agents, varying task-level versus subtask-level induction and text versus code skill formats. Task-level skills mostly push agents below their no-memory baseline while subtask-level skills raise performance on average, with text and code formats transferring differently. It gives concrete design guidance for agent skill libraries.

entry.title: Block3D: Efficient Text-to-3D Generation via Block-Wise Diffusion

author.name: Bowen Cui, Weijie Wang, Zeyu Zhang, Yefei He, Mingda Lin, Haoyu Zhao, Yuanyu He, Donny Y. Chen, Feng Chen, Bohan Zhuang

entry.summary: Block3D partitions discrete 3D shape-token sequences into contiguous blocks generated autoregressively while all tokens inside a block are denoised jointly, blending autoregressive and diffusion decoding. The goal is high geometric fidelity in text-to-3D at substantially lower inference cost.

entry.title: Coupled Optimal Transport with Landmark Constraints

author.name: Xiang Gu, Jian Sun, Zongben Xu

entry.summary: Introduces a coupled optimal transport framework in which a handful of annotated landmarks guides recovery of an underlying deformation field, jointly optimized with the transport plan through mutual coupling. The aim is geometrically meaningful correspondences that pure cost minimization misses.

entry.title: Artificial Intelligence for Workflow Analysis in Colorectal Surgery: A Multicentric, Cross-Procedural Development and Generalization Study

author.name: Pietro Mascagni, Julia Alekseenko, Pooja P Jain, Marta Goglia, Andrea Balla, Ludovica Baldari, Gianfranco Silecchia, Claudio Fiorillo, Vincenzo Tondolo, Salvador Morales-Conde, Luigi Boni, Sergio Alfieri, Nicolas Padoy

entry.summary: AI-ColoWorkflow automates surgical phase and step recognition in minimally invasive colorectal surgery using a fine-tuned DINOv3 vision transformer with a hierarchical multi-stage temporal convolutional network, trained on annotated videos from four centers plus a public dataset. It tests cross-procedural generalization for a previously validated manual assessment tool.

entry.title: OrthoSkillVLA: Continual Skill Learning via Gradient-Informed Skill Subspace Adaptation

author.name: Jiaqi Wang, Zhou Fang, Qiongfeng Shi, Yi Zhou

entry.summary: OrthoSkillVLA tackles catastrophic forgetting when sequentially adapting pretrained vision-language-action models to new skills, arguing that the language backbone and the action expert have different failure modes and so should not share one orthogonal-subspace constraint. It allocates gradient-informed skill subspaces per component without inflating inference cost.

entry.title: Multi-Tool Robotics Enables In-Situ Sample Manipulation for Time-Resolved Synchrotron Measurements

author.name: Aditya Bondada, Elizabeth M. Wall, Eric Yuan Xiao, Quinn C. Burlingame, Yueh-Lin Loo, Esther H. R. Tsai, Ruipeng Li

entry.summary: A modular multi-tool robotic platform installed inside a synchrotron X-ray scattering hutch performs sample handling and processing during live measurements, which safety rules otherwise forbid humans from doing. The system revealed previously inaccessible transient dynamics in perovskite thin films.

entry.title: Causal Generalization of Continuous Treatment Effects under Covariate Shift

author.name: Jay Jojo Cheng, Guanhua Chen

entry.summary: A statistical method for estimating average dose-response curves for continuous treatments when the analysis sample differs from the target population and only covariates are observed in the target. The approach uses two-sample local polynomial regression on pseudo-outcomes plus a source-to-target extension of distance-covariance optimal weighting to handle confounding and distribution shift jointly.

entry.title: Ablating 1 of a chess transformer's 128 attention heads makes the model stop finding Paul Morphy's queen sacrifice

author.name: dl27

entry.summary: An interpretability experiment reporting that removing a single attention head from a 128-head chess transformer causes the model to lose the ability to find a famous queen-sacrifice combination. It is a compact case study of highly localized capability within a game-playing transformer.

entry.title: AI #182: Pause For Reflection

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi's weekly roundup synthesizing recent AI developments, including OpenAI's response to a security incident involving HuggingFace and pauses to development while safeguards are added, Anthropic's revenue trajectory and IPO preparation alongside its August 2026 risk report, and a discussion of a podcast on recursive self-improvement. It functions as a curated digest with commentary on alignment, infrastructure, and governance.

entry.title: Can a Lightweight Multimodal Model Estimate LLM Reasoning Performance? A Study for Compute-Optimal Document Inference

author.name: Zishan Ahmad, Vishal Vaddina

entry.summary: Introduces BudgetDoc, a multimodal benchmark with explicit supervision over model, reasoning budget, and performance trade-offs on document tasks, and DRB, an approximately 1B parameter pre-flight estimator that predicts ordinal performance across budget levels before inference. Dynamic budget allocation with DRB matches or beats always-maximum-budget baselines in most of the tested model and dataset combinations.

entry.title: Competence, Not Accuracy: A Diagnostic for Reference-Free Judge Gates in Skill Optimization

author.name: Chenle Chen, Yangbo Wei, Chao Yao, Shaoqiang Lu, Junhong Qian, Chen Wu, Lei He

entry.summary: Asks whether an LLM judge can be used as a validation gate for text-space skill optimization on tasks lacking automatic verifiers, formalizing a reference-free judge as a latent solver whose evaluation capacity is bounded by its own ability to solve the task. It derives a closed-form diagnostic to predict, before deployment in the loop, whether the judge's scores separate correct from incorrect answers.

entry.title: Evaluating and Explaining Prompt Sensitivity of LLMs Using Interactions

author.name: Ruiyang Qin, Qingzhuo Wang, Tian Wang, Zhihua Wei, Wen Shen

entry.summary: Explains prompt sensitivity by decomposing an LLM output score into interaction terms over sets of input variables, rather than only comparing final outputs across paraphrases. This yields a finer-grained account of why semantically irrelevant prompt edits change behavior.

entry.title: MR-IQA-2: Faithful Image Quality Reflection via Fine-Grained Credit Assignment

author.name: Yuan li, Youyuan Lin, Chenhui Chu, Shin'ya Nishida

entry.summary: Improves multimodal image quality assessment by separating credit for the quality rating from credit for the reasoning that justifies it, using an actor, editor and judge arrangement with verifiable supervision. The goal is to prevent models from being rewarded for unfaithful explanations that happen to yield correct scores.

entry.title: Beyond Predictive Fairness: Quantifying Attribution Consistency Across Demographic Groups in Diabetic Retinopathy Screening

author.name: Kerol Djoumessi, Philipp Berens

entry.summary: Introduces a divergence-based score measuring whether a medical imaging model relies on similar visual evidence across demographic subgroups, complementing standard subgroup performance metrics. In diabetic retinopathy screening, explanation consistency stays high even where predictive performance differs, suggesting the two fairness notions are distinct.

entry.title: DA-WAM: Decision-Aligned Future Latents for Driving World Models

author.name: Ruiguo Zhong, Benshan Ma, Xiaolong Chen, Lang Zhang, Mingyue Feng, Yaonong Wang, Pei Liu, Jun Ma

entry.summary: DA-WAM unifies predictive representation learning, action-conditioned future prediction, and trajectory scoring so that a driving world model's imagined futures actually differentiate candidate trajectories. The argument is that existing models decouple future prediction from planning, diluting action-specific consequences.

entry.title: PGFS++: Molecular Property Improvement under Synthesis and Diversity Constraints

author.name: Boqiao Zhang, Godbless James, Sai Krishna Gottipati, Andrew Fitzgibbon

entry.summary: PGFS++ improves synthesis-aware reinforcement learning for molecular optimization by replacing indirect reactant-embedding prediction with trainable lookup tables for reaction templates and reactants, plus better scoring and RL algorithms, and then adds diversity constraints. The result is property improvement that stays within synthesizable chemical space.

entry.title: G-MARK: Grounded Multi-Agent Reasoning for Cooperative Driving via Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Bhavya Gupta, Onat Gungor, Tajana Rosing

entry.summary: G-MARK converts vehicle-to-vehicle cooperative perception into explicit provenance-aware knowledge graphs rather than latent fused features, so it stays clear which agent observed each object and how conflicting evidence is resolved. The aim is interpretable and auditable cooperative driving under occlusion and partial observability.

entry.title: Active Spiking Perception: The Membrane Potential as a Belief State for Anytime 3D Point Cloud Recognition

author.name: Akarsh Jain, Arya Pawa, Ayush Debnath, Smera Rawal, Sayeed Shafayet Chowdhury

entry.summary: Reframes spiking 3D point cloud recognition as an active perception loop in which the leaky integrate-and-fire membrane potential is read as a running belief over classes, driving both which spatial chunk to observe next and when to exit early. A lightweight selection policy is trained end to end with straight-through Gumbel-Softmax.

entry.title: Heteroscedastic Neural Surrogate Modeling for Robust and Rapid Bayesian Inference in Fusion Plasma Diagnostics

author.name: Liyun Zhang, Naoya Mamada, Kentaro Sakai, Takeo Hoshi, Toru Aonishi

entry.summary: Builds a dual-head neural surrogate that predicts both the expected emission spectrum and channel-wise measurement noise variance for fusion plasma Thomson scattering diagnostics, trained with a Gaussian negative log-likelihood objective. The learned aleatoric uncertainty makes downstream MCMC parameter inference faster and more robust to noise.

entry.title: Composition-Driven Phase Evolution in Sm-Doped BiFeO3 via Latent-Field Reconstruction of Atomically Resolved STEM Data

author.name: Newsha Javanmardi, Christopher T. Nelson, Anna N. Morozovska, Eugene A. Eliseev, Ichiro Takeuchi, Sergei V. Kalinin

entry.summary: Replaces the usual atom-column fitting pipeline for atomic-resolution electron microscopy with a latent Bragg field representation that yields continuous maps of crystalline order, displacement, strain, and rotation. The method is applied to composition-driven phase evolution in samarium-doped bismuth ferrite.

entry.title: RIPE++: Reinforced Keypoint Learning from Positive Pairs Only

author.name: Johannes K\"unzel, Peter Eisert, Anna Hilsmann

entry.summary: RIPE++ revisits reinforcement learning for local keypoint detection and description, which needs only weak supervision about whether two images depict the same scene rather than poses or depth. It replaces coarse binary rewards and hand-built negative pairs with a formulation intended to improve training stability and descriptor discriminability.

entry.title: Where Does the Union Bound Go? Best-Arm Identification and Strong FWER Control

author.name: Rianne de Heide

entry.summary: Clarifies an apparent paradox in fixed-confidence best-arm identification, where union bounds introduce a Bonferroni-like factor even though only one arm can truly be best. It shows two valid hypothesis orientations, one giving a strong familywise error rate problem with many true nulls and the other allowing a single true null to be falsely rejected through many pairwise comparisons.

entry.title: Flow Matching Meets 3D Curvilinear Structure Segmentation in Medical Imaging

author.name: Sidi Mohamed Sid'El Moctar, Nicolas Vitry, H\'el\`ene Bouvrais

entry.summary: Presents a flow-matching model for segmenting curvilinear anatomical structures such as vessels in 3D medical volumes, keeping the iterative refinement benefits of generative segmentation while avoiding the expensive sampling of diffusion models. It targets generalization across anatomies and imaging modalities.

entry.title: Represented but Ignored: A Causal Account of Prosodic Underuse in Audio-Language Models

author.name: Linkai Peng, Baorian Nuchged

entry.summary: Introduces a stage-specific probe ladder to localize why audio-language models fail on prosodic input, distinguishing loss of acoustic information, wrong internal interpretation, and failure to use available representations. Across four understanding-only audio-LLMs, prosody is usually preserved in the audio path yet underused downstream. It offers a causal diagnosis rather than just behavioral scores.

entry.title: Mitigating Identity Essentialism in LLM Agents with Longitudinal Life Trajectories

author.name: Hexi Wang, Yujia Zhou, Bangde Du, Weihang Su, Xinyuan Cao, Qingyi Pan, Qingyao Ai, Yueyue Wu, Min Zhang, Yiqun Liu

entry.summary: Shows that static demographic-profile LLM agents exhibit stronger between-group separation and within-group compression than real humans, a pattern the authors attribute to identity essentialism, and proposes conditioning agents on longitudinal life trajectories instead of sparse static labels. The aim is more human-like heterogeneity in social simulation. It bears directly on the credibility of LLM-based social science.

entry.title: ArmorOCR: Grounded Adversarial Visual Perception via Observation-Transferred Self-Distillation

author.name: Linhan Cao, Siyuan Li, Jun Lan, Liangbo He, Guannan Li, Xiaolei Huang, Jun Jia, Shuheng Zhou, Huijia Zhu, Weiqiang Wang, Wei Sun

entry.summary: Formulates adversarial OCR as a grounded perception task and releases AdvSpot, a region-annotated benchmark of 390 images spanning 13 fine-grained adversarial text types that humans read but models mislocalize. ArmorOCR uses observation-transferred self-distillation to harden large multimodal models on these cases.

entry.title: When Automata Meet Streams: Temporal Logic Compilation for Stream-Based Robotics Task and Motion Planning

author.name: Sayem Nazmuz Zaman, Cyrus Neary

entry.summary: Enables temporal logic specifications such as safe ordering, invariance, and liveness in stream-based task and motion planning, where the geometric object set expands during iterative stream refinement and breaks existing automaton compilation techniques. The proposed synchronous action monitoring approach makes automata compatible with growing continuous parameter streams.

entry.title: Accurate Decoding of Natural Sentences from Non-Invasive Brain Recordings

author.name: Mingfang Zhang, Jarod L\'evy, Cedric Rommel, J\'er\'emy Rapin, Corentin Bel, Julie Bonnaire, Daniel Nieto, Pierre Bourdillon, Svetlana Pinet, St\'ephane d'Ascoli, Thomas Moreau, Jean-R\'emi King

entry.summary: Covered in yesterday's Research roundup, Describes the second-generation non-invasive brain-to-text model that decodes typed natural sentences from magnetoencephalography, trained on 22,000 sentences from nine subjects with ten hours each. It reaches an average word error rate near 39 percent, with the best participant decoded to within one word error on half of sentences.

entry.title: Position: AI Leaderboards Are Underserving the Global South: A Case Study from India

author.name: Sourav Banerjee, Saikat Saha

entry.summary: Argues that global AI leaderboards structurally fail Global South users not because regional benchmarks are missing, since suites for Indic, African, and Arabic languages already exist, but because leaderboards lack independent governance, conflict-of-interest policies, and metric evolution mechanisms. It uses India as a case study of persistent, uncorrected evaluation failures.

entry.title: Adversarial Review: Structured Disagreement for Grounded Agentic Code Review

author.name: Eric S. Qiu, Joyce Gill

entry.summary: Adversarial Review is a minimal three-role code review protocol where a main coding agent works with a reviewer and a critic that audits the review through structured disagreement before edits are made. It aims for a middle ground between passive subagent tool use and large multi-agent teams that show diminishing returns, and reports the highest pass rate among compared scaffolds on LiveCodeBench.

entry.title: CTIFoundry: An Agent-Native Corpus Scaffold for Cyber Threat Intelligence

author.name: Yutong Cheng, Changze Li, Qian Cui, Wei Ding, Lingzhi Wang, Yan Chen, Peng Gao

entry.summary: CTIFoundry argues that the bottleneck in agentic cyber threat intelligence is the corpus substrate rather than model capability, since threat reports are still packaged as opaque chunks behind an embedding index. It builds an agent-native scaffold that materializes a deterministic ontology graph over CVE, CWE, CAPEC, and ATT and CK knowledge bases at build time so agents can traverse structure instead of guessing from retrieval.

entry.title: Metrics That Write Themselves: Evolving an Evaluator from Its Own Blind Spots

author.name: Xing Zhang, Yanwei Cui, Guanghui Wang, Zhihao Lin, Peiyang He

entry.summary: Attempts to evolve an automatic evaluation metric for hard-to-score tasks like report generation by maintaining a pool of small Python operators that each flag one named defect or abstain, then vote. Directly asking a model for operators yields little diversity, so the authors adapt counterexample-guided abstraction refinement from program verification to search for cases the current operator pool cannot distinguish.

entry.title: Nine Emotion Centroids: A Label-Free Valence Axis That Transfers Across Four Modalities

author.name: Yousef Radwan

entry.summary: Finds a single internal valence direction in frozen encoders using only nine emotion category names and about fifty short narratives each, taking the top principal direction of the averaged emotion embeddings. The same axis appears in text, vision, audio, and human brain encoders that were never jointly trained, recovering most supervised sentiment performance and correlating with human valence ratings on a large image set.

entry.title: Same Facts, Different Updates: Inference Setup Shapes LLM Behavior in Medical Allocation

author.name: Spencer Gibson, Tyler Crosse, Magnus Saebo, Achyutha Menon, Eyon Jang, Diogo Cruz

entry.summary: Examines how accumulated conversational context changes LLM decisions in a medical resource-allocation vignette, comparing runs where the model does or does not see its own prior answer. Three of four models update differently under paired context versus independent inference, indicating anchoring on prior outputs.

entry.title: Decomposing Wrong-Consensus Agreement in LLM Self-Consistency: A GPT-4.1 Case Study

author.name: Lizhuo Zhang, Mengmeng Tang, Chenfeng Long, Xiaoyong Tang, Xiang Luo

entry.summary: Quantifies why majority voting over sampled answers sometimes backfires by defining an agreement index and splitting it into a mechanical part predicted by per-question answer preferences and an unexplained residual. The null model is difficulty matched and leak free, estimated from other runs of the same question.

entry.title: Bernstein-Vazirani Networks: Quantum Machine Learning by Interference

author.name: Natacha Kuete Meli, Tolga Birdal, Prayag Tiwari, Vladislav Golyanik, Michael Moeller

entry.summary: Bernstein-Vazirani Networks are a non-variational quantum machine learning framework that encodes labeled data in superposition and uses interference in Fourier or problem-adapted bases to extract features, with gradient-free training. The authors argue for universal approximation via overcomplete interference bases and test on vision and representation tasks.

entry.title: Towards On-Board Implementation of ML-Based Helicopter Weight Estimator

author.name: Nicolas Valot, Ammar Mechouche, Benjamin Lesage, Claire Pagetti, Louis Fabre

entry.summary: Describes an LSTM-based supervised model that estimates helicopter takeoff weight from Airbus in-service fleet data, developed under an explicit learning-assurance process aligned with EASA guidance and the emerging Eurocae ED-324 standard. The model is implemented and verified on legacy avionics computers for airborne deployment.

entry.title: Systematic Evaluation of TabPFN-TS for Zero-Shot Probabilistic Heat Load Forecasting in District Heating Networks

author.name: Ben Spoek, Karim K. Ben Hicham, Kai Derzsi, Philipp Althaus, Alexander Mitsos, Dirk M\"uller

entry.summary: Systematically benchmarks TabPFN-TS zero-shot probabilistic forecasting against other time-series foundation models and trained baselines for district heating load prediction. The study tests whether in-context forecasting can replace repeated system-specific retraining as networks evolve.

entry.title: End-to-end Early Classification of Time Series in Non-Stationary Environments

author.name: Aur\'elien Renault, Alexis Bondu, Antoine Cornu\'ejols, Vincent Lemaire

entry.summary: Studies early classification of time series under distribution drift, where most existing methods assume stationarity and optimize classification and trigger decisions separately. It introduces DQeND, a reinforcement-learning architecture that jointly learns representation, classification, and when to commit to a decision.

entry.title: Compliance, Capability, and Conflict: Benchmarking Multimodal LLMs under System Messages

author.name: Juan Yeo, Geewook Kim

entry.summary: VSysBench, built on MMVet-v2, measures whether multimodal LLMs follow system-message constraints in visual settings and whether such compliance degrades core vision-language ability. It organizes 5 main and 22 sub-categories of constraints, each paired with a misaligned counterpart that stress-tests the instruction hierarchy. This fills a gap since production MLLM deployments govern behavior through system prompts.

entry.title: Hear2Act: Benchmarking When Prosody Should Change What an Assistant Does

author.name: Xinyi Liu, Hooshang Nayyeri, Dilek Hakkani-Tur, Emine Yilmaz, JK Kim, Yifei Zhang, Charith Peris, Hari Thadakamalla

entry.summary: Hear2Act provides 480 persona-grounded scenarios in which the same hidden user concern is conveyed either explicitly in words or mainly through prosody, with objectively verifiable task outcomes. This lets evaluators test whether prosodic evidence actually changes an assistant's downstream decisions rather than just its perception scores. It unifies prosody perception, response appropriateness and task success in one protocol.

entry.title: PEA-DPO: Perception-Enhanced Alignment Direct Preference Optimization for MLLMs Alignment

author.name: Jiawei Feng, Jiancan Wu, Xingyu Zhu, Junkang Wu, Xiang Wang, Xiangnan He

entry.summary: Identifies visual insensitivity in multimodal preference optimization, where DPO-trained models fail to distinguish original images from ones with critical visual context removed, and decomposes it into across-image and within-image insensitivity with theoretical analysis. PEA-DPO explicitly injects visual perception signals into the preference objective to fix this. It addresses a structural flaw in transplanting DPO to multimodal settings.

entry.title: A Plug-in Interpretation of Conditioning in Score-Based Diffusion Models

author.name: Libo Chen, Souvik Ghosh, Teo Deveney, Chris Budd, Vinay P. Namboodiri

entry.summary: Proposes conditioning diffusion models by learning an unconditional joint score over target and condition, then injecting conditioning at inference as an explicit plug-in correction term. This yields interpretable conditional reverse-time SDEs and probability-flow ODEs, with a Fokker-Planck residual regularizer to reduce ODE-SDE sampling discrepancy.

entry.title: Towards Surgical World-Action Modeling: A Preliminary Joint Visual-Trajectory Forecasting for Surgical Motion Planning

author.name: Weiliang Huang, Huanrong Liu, Bob Zhang, Qi Dou, Zhen Chen, Yun Gu, Guy Rosman, Qingbiao Li

entry.summary: Proposes joint forecasting of future surgical scene appearance and instrument trajectories as a step toward surgical world-action models, arguing that scene-only and trajectory-only models each miss half the picture. Joint prediction permits trajectory-level accuracy evaluation while capturing the visual consequences of instrument motion.

entry.title: LF-GICP: Parameter-Free Degeneracy-Aware LiDAR Odometry via a Voxel-Normal Localizability Field

author.name: Eunsoo Im

entry.summary: LF-GICP shows that in voxelized GICP the Gauss-Newton Hessian masks translational degeneracy because covariance regularization keeps the translation block artificially well-conditioned, then bypasses this with a regularization-free voxel-normal localizability field. Two derived statistics distinguish directional anisotropy and true information absence, yielding parameter-free degeneracy handling in tunnels and corridors.

entry.title: Learning the Right Abstraction: Neural Reduced Dynamics for Complex Robot Control

author.name: Harry Zhang, Dan Negrut

entry.summary: Argues that the practical value of neural dynamics models for complex robot control lies in learning the right abstraction, a reduced state that preserves control-relevant physics while allowing high-throughput policy learning. The neural reduced dynamics framework separates what the model must propagate from what can be supplied externally as input.

entry.title: One Gate Is Not Enough: Composing Stateful Pre-Action Controls for Agentic AI

author.name: Gaston Besanson

entry.summary: Formalizes the problem that when one pre-action safety control remediates an agent action, it can invalidate the judgment of another control, and gives a re-gating protocol to restore soundness. It also shows two implemented remediation operators do not commute, so ordering matters.

entry.title: TTSD-FAR: Test-Time Self-Distillation with Fisher-Anchored Restoration for Missing-Modality Emotion Recognition in LVLMs

author.name: Muhammad Haseeb Aslam, Alessandro Koerich, Marco Pedersoli, Ali Etemad, Eric Granger

entry.summary: Handles missing or noisy modalities at test time for emotion recognition with large video-language models by combining self-distillation with a Fisher-anchored restoration step that limits drift from the original weights. It targets the failure of entropy-based test-time adaptation on autoregressive multimodal models.

entry.title: A Few Cases Are All You Need: An Empirical Study of Annotation-Efficient LoRA Fine-Tuning of MedSAM3

author.name: Sachin Dudda Nagaraju, Bendik Skarre Abrahamsen, Ashkan Moradi, Mattijs Elschot

entry.summary: Empirically measures how many expert-annotated cases are needed to adapt a medical segmentation foundation model with low-rank fine-tuning to reach clinically useful accuracy on abdominal structures. The answer bears directly on annotation budgets for new clinical tasks.

entry.title: Graphical Design of Interpretable Architectures

author.name: Pietro Barbiero

entry.summary: Introduces a graphical notation adapted from Penrose tensor diagrams for specifying interpretable neural architectures, designed to map one-to-one onto einsum code so diagrams stay faithful to actual tensor operations. It is applied to describe concept-based and other interpretable-by-construction models.

entry.title: ReWEIGH the Evidence: Calibrating Token-Level Ordinal Visual Evidence to Mitigate Hallucinations in Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Jihae Jeong, Junha Choi, Hwanjo Yu

entry.summary: ReWEIGH is a training-free decoding method that pools rank-based, scale-invariant readouts from visual token states to measure how strongly the image supports each candidate token, then calibrates for token-specific rank biases. It is applied to reduce hallucinations in large vision-language models.

entry.title: Interpretable AI predicts a 2026 summer dry anomaly in central China

author.name: Anran Wang, Wen Shi, Yong Luo, Jianbin Huang, Lijuan Chen, Junhu Zhao, Weixin Jin, Huihui Yuan

entry.summary: Uses a deep learning model to translate dynamical-model circulation forecasts into seasonal precipitation estimates, producing a consistent prediction of a dry summer 2026 anomaly over central China from March-to-May initializations. Interpretation ties skill to central equatorial Pacific warming and an anomalous western North Pacific cyclonic circulation.

entry.title: Unregularized Convergence of Single-Loop, Entropy-Regularized Natural Actor-Critic

author.name: Zhiqiang Tan

entry.summary: Analyzes a single-loop entropy-regularized natural actor-critic with compatible linear function approximation and shows convergence rates for the unregularized objective, using an uncentered critic to keep tracking stable as the policy nears determinism and the Fisher matrix degenerates. Results are given for stochastic and deterministic-style optimization regimes.

entry.title: MileGPO: Milestone Inference with Local Evidence for Graph-Based Policy Optimization of Long-Horizon LLM Agents

author.name: Bo Qian, Yuting Wu, Shuang Zeng, Huaiyu Wan, Dalin Zhang, Jiqiang Liu

entry.summary: MileGPO derives process-level credit for long-horizon agent training by mining candidate milestones from successful rollouts and recurring traps from failed ones within grouped on-policy samples, then weighting them by outcome-based confidence. This targets the sparse final-reward problem without requiring external step annotations.

entry.title: FAR-DPO: Feasibility-Aware and Robust Direct Preference Optimization for Cyclic Peptide Design

author.name: Guofeng Zhang, Rong Han, Xiaoyu Wang, Zhiyun Li, Zongbo Han, Xiaohong Liu, Guangyu Wang

entry.summary: FAR-DPO adapts direct preference optimization to cyclic peptide design so generative models are steered toward geometrically and biophysically feasible cyclized structures rather than relying on zero-shot generation plus post hoc filtering. The framework is architecture-agnostic and addresses multi-objective trade-offs under scarce training data.

entry.title: Reliable Neural Collapse Approximation for Open-World Test-Time Adaptation

author.name: Jia-Qi Lin, Yuangang Pan, Chang-Dong Wang, Haizhang Zhang, Ivor W. Tsang, Joey Tianyi Zhou

entry.summary: Introduces ReNC, a test-time adaptation method for open-world settings where label distributions shift and out-of-distribution samples appear. It uses neural collapse geometry as a structural prior, treating pretrained classifier weights as source-domain prototypes to filter unreliable samples before adaptation.

entry.title: Demons on a Budget: Adaptive Measurement Placement at the Entanglement Phase Transition

author.name: Rohan Pandey

entry.summary: Fixes the measurement budget in monitored random Clifford circuits and varies where measurements are placed, comparing random placement with hand-designed and learned policies near the entanglement phase transition. It finds that placement geometry matters more than placement information, with a contiguous sweep sharply reducing entanglement entropy.

entry.title: Data-Driven Time-Varying Control Barrier Functions for Adaptive Safe-Set Learning with Online Decremental Support Vector Machines

author.name: Shawon Dey, Michael Budihartono, Hever Moncayo

entry.summary: Learns a safe operating envelope from data with a kernel support vector machine, uses its decision function as a control barrier function, and updates the certificate online with decremental SVM learning as system capability degrades. This keeps safety filters valid when actuator authority changes during a mission.

entry.title: Microlensify: a Transformer Based Machine Learning Classifier for Microlensing Events Trained on TESS Light Curves

author.name: Atousa Kalantari, Somayeh Khakpash, Sedighe Sajadian, Hosein Haghi, Willow Fox Fortino, Rosanne Di Stefano

entry.summary: Microlensify is a physics-informed transformer-based variational autoencoder trained on simulated microlensing light curves plus real satellite photometry to find microlensing events and characterize false positives in high-cadence all-sky survey data. It targets detection of otherwise invisible compact objects.

entry.title: Far from the Crowd: Scalable Self-Supervised Learning via Geographic Isolation

author.name: Daniele Rege Cambrin, Francesco Rossi, Mattia Varile

entry.summary: Proposes ranking self-supervised pretraining samples for Earth observation by geographic isolation, a label-free curriculum signal computed from geolocation metadata alone with near-linear cost and no image decoding or model feedback. It is integrated into contrastive and masked autoencoder pretraining and evaluated on multiple downstream benchmarks.

entry.title: Feature Evolution and Migration during Vision Transformer Training

author.name: Joonas J\"arve, Halil Ibrahim Aysel, Tarun Khajuria, Meelis Kull

entry.summary: Uses sparse autoencoders on CLS-token representations to track how individual features in Vision Transformers appear and shift across both layers and training epochs, introducing the notion of feature migration. Findings suggest migration concentrates early in training and differs by feature type. It offers an interpretability lens on training dynamics that representation-similarity metrics cannot see.

entry.title: Keeping the Franka Emika Panda alive: a ROS 2 stack with a reliable position interface

author.name: Antonio Langella, Davide Risi, Vincenzo Petrone, Enrico Ferrentino, Pasquale Chiacchio

entry.summary: An open-source ROS 2 software stack that restores and stabilizes external position control on the discontinued Franka Emika Panda arm. The authors trace the classic vibration and protective-stop problems to control-loop timing and sampling jitter, and fix them with an asynchronous hardware interface, rate matching, and position-domain reference generation.

entry.title: SESSE: Sketch, Expand, Sort, Summarize, Evaluate -- LLM-as-Judge Evaluation via Structured Decomposition

author.name: Dae Lee, Mihai Delgeanu, Adel Youssef

entry.summary: SESSE is a training-free framework that breaks holistic A/B preference judgments into structured sub-questions mined from the judge model's own error cases, requiring no oracle answers, hand-written rubrics, or fine-tuning. On a 1,000-item RewardBench slice it matches chain-of-thought baselines and approaches a fine-tuned 32B specialist judge while providing per-criterion vote evidence.

entry.title: SuTRA : Structurally-Unified Tokenization with Root Awareness

author.name: Vaibhav Rathore, Siddhant Gole, Dadhichi Telwadkar, Rooshil Bhatia, Maulik Ruparel, Siddharth Surekha, Neha Bhargava

entry.summary: SuTRA is a morphology-aware tokenizer for Indic languages that preserves the indivisibility of orthographic syllables and penalizes merges that cross root and affix boundaries, countering what the authors call morphological shattering by frequency-based subword methods. The work also releases a new morphological segmentation dataset for Hindi, Marathi, and Gujarati.

entry.title: Counterfactual Contrastive Analysis

author.name: Yunlong He, Pietro Gori

entry.summary: Proposes generating visual counterfactual explanations without a classifier by using contrastive analysis to disentangle factors shared across two datasets from those salient to each class, then swapping the salient factors. This avoids inheriting classifier shortcuts and calibration errors that plague classifier-guided counterfactuals.

entry.title: Complementary, Not Cumulative: Interaction Effects in Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Navier-Stokes Vortex Shedding

author.name: Devesh Shah

entry.summary: Tests whether the many proposed physics-informed neural network training tricks actually compose, using the standard unsteady cylinder wake benchmark. Nearly every technique alone matches an untreated baseline, but combining periodic activations with causal weighting unlocks accurate velocity and pressure reconstruction to about four percent relative error against a CFD reference.

entry.title: A Locally Tokenized Generative Model for Robust Time-Series Watermarking

author.name: Dongbin Kim, Geonwoo Shin, Yujin Choi, Soyeon Park, Jaewook Lee

entry.summary: Shows that existing multivariate time-series watermark detectors fail because globally coupled re-encoding lets post-editing attacks shift the non-watermarked z-score distribution in either direction, invalidating thresholds calibrated on clean data. The proposed L-VQVAE produces each discrete token from a bounded local temporal window so detection statistics remain stable.

entry.title: Separating Covariate Shift from Mechanism Change with Two Discriminators: CJSD, a Conditional Discrepancy with an Exact Covariate-Concept Decomposition

author.name: Kentaro Oda

entry.summary: Introduces a conditional discrepancy measure with an exact decomposition into covariate shift and mechanism change using two discriminators, and builds a sequential decision layer that lets a streaming system reuse an expert model, spawn a new one, or defer. Anytime validity is proved via betting e-processes with an explicit indifference zone for deferral.

entry.title: ConceptGuard: Benchmarking Context-Sensitive Unlearning in Large Language Models

author.name: Sahil Kale, Ian Harris

entry.summary: ConceptGuard argues that unlearning benchmarks built on disjoint sets of independent facts and simple recall tests miss the real requirement, which is removing unsafe applications of a concept while preserving its legitimate uses. It proposes concept-level, context-sensitive evaluation of unlearning completeness and utility preservation. This reframes a core problem in machine unlearning research.

entry.title: Does Marginal Coverage Guarantee Class-Conditional Safety for Zero-Shot VLMs Under Shift?

author.name: Jai Kumar Sharma, Amartya Dutta

entry.summary: Audits split-conformal prediction as an abstention layer for zero-shot vision-language models under deployment shift across CLIP, OpenCLIP and SigLIP, finding that marginal coverage can stay near 0.86 while worst-class coverage collapses toward zero on ImageNet-Sketch. The failure tracks target-domain per-class accuracy and is not predicted by the source-domain diagnostics tested, and source-side Mondrian calibration does not transfer. It warns that marginal guarantees do not imply class-conditional safety.

entry.title: MUST-PET: MUltimodal Self-supervised learning across Tracers for whole-body PET/CT-based lesion segmentation

author.name: Bashirul Azam Biswas, Amartya Bhattacharya, Biratal Raj Wagle, Matthew E. Maeder, James B. Yu, Indrani Bhattacharya

entry.summary: MUST-PET applies multimodal self-supervised pretraining with context-aware masked reconstruction across FDG and PSMA tracers for whole-body PET/CT lesion segmentation, trained on multi-institutional pan-cancer scans. It aims to overcome annotation scarcity and cross-tracer domain shift.

entry.title: Ultra-High-Definition Restoration Transformers with Correlation Matching Transformation

author.name: Cong Wang, Liyan Wang, Jinshan Pan, Wei Wang, Wenqi Ren, Jun Liu, Xiaochun Cao

entry.summary: UHDformer++ restores ultra-high-definition images through four coordinated learning spaces spanning high-resolution extraction, compact low-resolution representation, super-resolution upsampling, and fusion-based reconstruction, connected by correlation matching transformation. It is a general framework tested across multiple UHD restoration tasks.

entry.title: MOSAIC: Modality-agnostic Spectral Alignment for Federated Image-level Weakly Supervised Tumor Segmentation under Client-specific Missing Modalities

author.name: Tarun Kumar Garg, Vaanathi Sundaresan

entry.summary: MOSAIC is a federated framework for weakly supervised tumor segmentation using only image-level labels when different institutions hold different, incomplete sets of imaging modalities. It uses modality-agnostic spectral alignment to keep fusion quality from collapsing under client-specific missing modalities.

entry.title: The Forward-Backward Disconnect: State Dynamics, Credit Assignment, and Biological Grounding in Neural Computation

author.name: Hadi Al Mubasher, Mariette Awad

entry.summary: A position and survey paper observing that forward computation has diversified enormously, spanning recurrence, attention, state-space dynamics, continuous time, implicit equilibria, and spikes, while training remains concentrated on backpropagation and its variants. It examines the resulting mismatch between state dynamics and credit assignment, including biological plausibility considerations.

entry.title: Temporal Multi-Signal Fusion for Token-Level Hallucination Detection

author.name: Igor Itkin

entry.summary: Treats hallucination as a temporally extended span and labels tokens with a bidirectional recurrent model over a 33-dimensional feature stream fusing text statistics, entailment signals and surprisal, without touching model internals. It reports an 11-point AUC gain over an independent per-token baseline on a retrieval-grounded benchmark.

entry.title: FedCoRe: Target-Adaptive Completion for Missing Modalities in Healthcare Federated Learning

author.name: Holger R. Roth, Ziyue Xu, Peter Cnudde

entry.summary: Tackles federated multimodal learning when hospitals lack some modalities by learning corrections in representation or logit space rather than synthesizing missing images or signals. Only clients that can produce paired with-and-without examples update the completion module, and the base predictor stays frozen.

entry.title: Physics-Unrolled Neural Operator for Wireless Field Modeling

author.name: Rafid Umayer Murshed, Saif Ur Rahman, Mingyue Tang, Elahe Soltanaghai

entry.summary: Predicts high-fidelity indoor radio propagation maps from cheap low-fidelity inputs using a three-stage physics-unrolled neural operator, explicitly handling the Monte Carlo noise present in affordable simulated training labels. This reduces the cost of coverage planning and localization studies.

entry.title: GCNO: Gramian Chebyshev Neural Operator for Physics-Based Compression of Wireless Channels

author.name: Rafid Umayer Murshed, Shahab Hamidi-Rad, Elahe Soltanaghai, Akshay Malhotra

entry.summary: Compresses wireless channel feedback by reporting a variable number of dominant propagation paths rather than a fixed-length neural code, using a Chebyshev-based neural operator formulation. The scheme adapts to channel complexity and avoids retraining when antenna counts change.

entry.title: Orienteering Problem with Uncertain Time-Varying Rewards: Framework and Benchmark for Everyday Service Robotics

author.name: Masafumi Endo, Kohei Honda, Yuu Jinnai, Ryo Yonetani

entry.summary: Defines a routing problem in which rewards at locations are both uncertain and time-varying, so agents must forecast reward dynamics from observations, and provides planners plus theoretical performance bounds. A benchmark is released for everyday service robotics scenarios such as shifting delivery demand.

entry.title: The Impact of CutMix on Reliability and Robustness in Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Steven Landgraf, Markus Ulrich

entry.summary: Isolates the effect of a popular mixing augmentation on segmentation calibration, uncertainty quality and robustness rather than accuracy alone, across a convolutional and a transformer architecture. It is motivated by evidence that semi-supervised methods built on this augmentation can damage reliability.

entry.title: Identifying Implicit Premises for Logical Reconstruction of Argument Graphs

author.name: Xuyao Feng, Anthony Hunter

entry.summary: Proposes a neuro-symbolic pipeline where an LLM proposes implicit premises for incomplete arguments (enthymemes), which are then translated into logical formulae and checked with a theorem prover to establish entailment or contradiction between statements. It targets automated logical reconstruction of argument graphs from natural language.

entry.title: Pre-Compiled Pipeline Shards for Distributed LLM Inference on Intel AI PC Fleets

author.name: Tate Berenbaum, Muthaiah Venkatachalam

entry.summary: Shows that several ordinary Intel AI PCs on a normal network can jointly serve models too large for any one of them, by splitting layers into pre-compiled OpenVINO pipeline shards and streaming activations. The paper identifies a compilation pitfall that made naive per-stage export far slower than monolithic inference and describes fixes.

entry.title: Finite-Horizon Input-Output Dynamics of Minibatch Perturbations in AdamW

author.name: Kang Liu, Suyan Li

entry.summary: Models AdamW as a finite-horizon input-state-output system whose state includes parameters and both moment estimates, then linearizes to derive a signed response operator mapping a single perturbed gradient update to its future loss effects. This quantifies how optimizer memory carries the influence of one minibatch forward in magnitude, timing, and sign.

entry.title: Multi-Source Wasserstein Distributionally Robust Graph Learning

author.name: Chuansen Peng, Yifan Xia, Jinshan Zhong, Xiaojing Shen

entry.summary: Presents MS-WDRO, a framework for inferring graph topology from signals when target-domain data are scarce but heterogeneous source domains are abundant. It fuses sources via weighted Wasserstein barycenters rather than Euclidean averaging, preserving each source geometry under distributional robustness.

entry.title: A Standardized Framework for Machine Learning in Power System Protection

author.name: Julian Oelhaf, Georg Kordowich, Paula Andrea P\'erez-Toro, Christian Bergler, Johann J\"ager, Andreas Maier, Siming Bayer

entry.summary: Argues that near-perfect reported accuracies in machine learning for power system protection are often uninterpretable because evaluation design varies jointly along many unspecified dimensions. It proposes a seven-dimension standardization framework and instantiates it in a bounded case study on a public electromagnetic-transient dataset.

entry.title: Time-Series Retrieval for Grounding Multimodal Language Models in Remaining Useful Life

author.name: Valeriu Dimidov, Rapha\"el Frank

entry.summary: Grounds multimodal language models for remaining useful life estimation by retrieving historically similar degradation segments and rendering them as a visual comparison artifact inside a structured prompt. It is evaluated on a standard turbofan degradation benchmark under repeated trials.

entry.title: Quantum Gaussian processes for prediction of channel observations

author.name: Jonas J\"ager, Yaroslav Khmelnitskiy, Paolo Braccia, Artur Miroszewski, Diego Garc\'ia-Mart\'in, M. Cerezo, Piotr Czarnik

entry.summary: Extends quantum Gaussian process regression from unitary evolutions to general quantum channels, proving convergence of channel outputs to a quantum Gaussian process and deriving a closed-form kernel under a uniform prior over channels. It also shows the kernel dimensional factor imposes exponentially demanding measurement precision for large subsystems.

entry.title: skchange: Fast and Flexible Algorithms for Changepoint Detection

author.name: Martin Tveten, Johannes Voll Kolst{\o}, Per August Jarval Moen

entry.summary: Describes skchange, an open-source Python library implementing modern changepoint and anomalous-segment detection algorithms in a modular and composable framework. It includes fast approximate search methods, high-dimensional algorithms, and data-driven penalty calibration utilities.

entry.title: Spike-based Belief Propagation in Nonlinear Dynamical Systems

author.name: Sepideh Adamiat, Hongye Wang, Wouter M. Kouw, Bert de Vries

entry.summary: Combines a spiking neural model with Bayesian inference to produce a brain-inspired adaptive controller that updates beliefs and generates goal-directed plans through spike-driven message passing. It is demonstrated on the nonlinear mountain car parking benchmark.

entry.title: What You Can't See Is What You Learn: Restricted Evidence Visibility Favors Compositional Generalization in Shared-Genome Language-Model Societies

author.name: Narcis Marincat

entry.summary: Tests whether restricting which evidence each module can see changes the solutions gradient training discovers, using four-cell societies that share one frozen pretrained model and one adapter and communicate through narrow continuous vectors. Across ten tightly matched pairs differing only in the attention mask, restricted societies generalize compositionally far better than globally visible twins.

entry.title: Information on trajectories: martingales and random times

author.name: Akshay Balsubramani

entry.summary: Derives exact variational identities for nonnegative martingales on path space, valid at arbitrary random stopping times, and shows how classical concentration inequalities from Ville to PAC-Bayes arise as lossy special cases. The slack each bound discards is given an exact form in three geometric regimes, decomposed per step into conditional divergences or Bregman terms. It unifies and sharpens the toolkit underlying anytime-valid inference and generalization bounds.

entry.title: When Irrelevant Text Matters: Affine Margin Shifts in Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Yinfeng Wang, Zhiyuan Yao, Zheren Fu, Lei Zhang, Zhendong Mao

entry.summary: Shows that appending task-irrelevant text systematically biases multimodal LLM predictions in binary visual judgment tasks, and characterizes the effect through the log-probability decision margin. The authors report a geometric regularity in which context-conditioned margins shift in an approximately affine manner. This gives a quantitative handle on context sensitivity beyond accuracy drops.

entry.title: TextRefine: Improving Textual Fidelity, Spatial Placement, and Glyph Rendering for Text Editing in Product Posters

author.name: Honglie Wang, Jia Sun, Zijun Li, Junlong Wu, Pengcheng Wei, Jiyuan Wang, Yongrui Heng, Boheng Zhang, Huaiqing Wang, Dewen Fan, Qianqian Gan, Fan Yang, Tingting Gao, Yan-Ming Zhang

entry.summary: TextRefine post-trains an image editing model for inserting and replacing text in product posters, combining supervised fine-tuning with operation-specific reward optimization that scores text-span semantic fidelity, placement, and glyph quality. It targets known failure modes of general-purpose editors in commercial design workflows.

entry.title: Wave-Based Bilateral Teleoperation between Nonlinear Manipulators with Direct Contact Force Feedback

author.name: G. Q. Bao Tran, Takanori Miyoshi, Ho Duc Tho

entry.summary: This work develops a stability theory for bilateral teleoperation of nonlinear multi-DOF manipulators under communication delay when the true environmental contact force is fed back to the operator, which normally risks instability. The authors characterize the passivity shortage of the Euler-Lagrange remote system via linear matrix inequalities and compensate it with a strictly passive communication law.

entry.title: Emergence of cooperation: A reputation-modulated reinforcement learning

author.name: Chenyang Zhao, Jiqiang Zhang, Li Chen, Yong Zou

entry.summary: A spatial prisoner's dilemma in which Q-learning agents fold a locally computed reputation signal into how they interpret their own and neighbors' behavior, treating reputation as information rather than as an external payoff modifier. Simulations show reputation-modulated learning substantially strengthens the emergence of cooperation.

entry.title: Breaking the weakest link to evade vision language models
