entry.title: You Are What You Prompt: Prompt Quality, Domain Shift, and Uncertainty in Agrifood Vision-Language Models

author.name: Andrea Morales-Garz\'on, Salvador L\'opez-Joya, Miguel L\'opez-P\'erez, Maria J. Martin-Bautista

entry.summary: Evaluates zero-shot prompt ensembling for CLIP and SigLIP across food and agricultural datasets, finding it adds little in-distribution but substantially improves accuracy and calibration under domain shift. Small domain-specific prompt pools outperform much larger generic pools.

entry.title: Assessing Quality of Experience in Natural Language Generation of German Text

author.name: Dinh Nam Pham, Shushen Manakhimova, Vivien Macketanz, Sebastian M\"oller

entry.summary: Introduces a German dataset suite of crowdsourced human quality ratings for summarization and machine translation from a Quality of Experience perspective, then trains automatic predictors of those perceptual dimensions. Argues that traditional automatic metrics miss multifaceted perceived quality.

entry.title: Multimodal Rapport Estimation in Real-World HRI

author.name: Akihiro Sakuramoto, Takato Hayashi, Ryo Miyoshi, Yuki Okafuji, Shogo Okada

entry.summary: Estimates third-party rapport ratings from 62 sessions of multimodal human-robot interaction recorded in a real Japanese drugstore, comparing zero-shot LLMs against pretrained text, audio, and visual models. Tests whether lab-developed interaction quality metrics survive the wild where users can disengage and bystanders join.

entry.title: COSTA: A Cluster-Centric Paradigm for Annotation-Free Open-Set Semantic Segmentation of Aerial Point Clouds with Domain Shifts

author.name: Yanghong Lin, Li Fang, Tianyu Li, Shudong Zhou, Wei Yao

entry.summary: COSTA reframes test-time adaptation for aerial point cloud segmentation from point-wise closed-set prediction to a cluster-centric, annotation-free open-set paradigm, letting a pretrained model handle domain shift and segment categories outside the source label space at inference without retraining. Targets the generalization crisis in airborne LiDAR mapping across sensors and regions. Combines open-vocabulary ideas with test-time adaptation.

entry.title: Teach a Molmo2Fish: Towards interactive fish tracking with natural language guidance

author.name: Kai Van Brunt (Massachusetts Institute of Technology), Justin Kay (Massachusetts Institute of Technology), Sara Beery (Massachusetts Institute of Technology)

entry.summary: Molmo2Fish turns imperfect multi-object tracking predictions on sonar fish video into an interactive dialogue with a multimodal LLM, letting ecologists correct tracks conversationally rather than through fixed interfaces. Performance is measured on guided and unguided correction tasks as a proof of concept for human-in-the-loop ecological monitoring. Explores how far conversational correction can substitute for better models.

entry.title: CamWorldQA: Perceptual Quality Assessment of Camera-Controlled World Video Generation

author.name: Yunhe Li, Likun Wu, Sijing Wu, Xinyu Tian, Huiyu Duan, Yixuan Gao, Yunhao Li, Guangtao Zhai

entry.summary: CamWorldQA is presented as the first perceptual quality benchmark for camera-controlled world video generation, with 720 videos from six generation methods across 20 source videos and six camera trajectories, annotated for characteristics that natural-video quality metrics ignore such as viewpoint consistency, motion coherence, and content preservation. Provides an evaluation substrate for controllable world models. Fills a measurement gap as camera-conditioned generators proliferate.

entry.title: RVLoss: Runoff Vote Loss for Self-Supervised LiDAR Scene Flow Estimation

author.name: Shiming Wang, Liangliang Nan, Julian Kooij, Holger Caesar, Yancong Lin

entry.summary: RVLoss replaces or augments the Chamfer objective in self-supervised LiDAR scene flow with a runoff vote mechanism that builds motion rigidity into the loss itself, rather than adding regularizers, improving flow consistency within object instances especially for large objects. Nearest-neighbor losses are the standard but produce inconsistent intra-object flow. Relevant to autonomous driving perception without motion labels.

entry.title: QuARC-GS: Quantized Anchored Residual Coding for Compact Dynamic Scene Streaming with Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Vu Trung Nghia Nguyen, Yuchen Wang, Kyung Chul Lee, Kevin C. Zhou

entry.summary: QuARC-GS is a quantization-aware 4D Gaussian splatting optimization framework using anchored residual coding to make online free-viewpoint video streaming sustainable for long sequences, attacking the storage and reconstruction-speed bottlenecks of detailed dynamic scene representations. Compression is integrated into optimization rather than applied afterwards. Aims at ultra-low bitrate dynamic scene streaming.

entry.title: Beyond Placement and Articulation: Usage-Driven Code Scenes for Embodied Interaction

author.name: Zijian Xiao, Zipeng Ye, Jinkun Hao, Xiong Yang, Yuchen Xie, Ran Yi

entry.summary: RoomWright generates indoor scenes entirely as code driven by how spaces are used rather than only how objects are placed and articulated, with an agent treating each anchor as a task center, admitting task-required objects and affordances, and compiling multi-part interactions. Existing code-based scene generators produce editable environments that remain functionally unmodeled. Aimed at simulation environments for embodied policy learning.

entry.title: LT-Mem: Volatility-Aware Spatio-Temporal Memory for Lifelong Scene Understanding

author.name: Yumin Lee, Hyoseok Ju, Giseop Kim

entry.summary: LT-Mem gives robots volatility-aware object-level memory across repeated visits, combining multi-session SLAM for spatially aligned per-object observations with temporal reasoning conditioned on how frequently objects change, so history is retained instead of overwritten. This lets systems answer queries about where an object has been across sessions, which current maps or semantic snapshots cannot. Addresses temporal amnesia in lifelong scene understanding.

entry.title: HarvestPoint-ACT: Explicit Target Selection and Harvest-Point Conditioning for Robotic Fruit Harvesting under Occlusion

author.name: Hanying Hu, Weipeng Li, Yikun Huang, Hao Chen, Zhengtao Hu, Changcai Yang, Weiwei Wan

entry.summary: Extends action-chunking imitation learning for fruit picking by making target choice and gripper closing point explicit: a segmentation network with a keypoint branch predicts per-fruit masks and harvest points, and a scheduler ranks candidates by occlusion and distance. This addresses failures where end-to-end policies lose track of the chosen fruit under occlusion.

entry.title: PartialBiGrasp: Inferring Hidden Local Geometry for Bimanual Grasping from Partial Views

author.name: Ayush Kaura, Vignesh Vembar, Md Faizal Karim, Keshab Patra, K Madhava Krishna

entry.summary: PartialBiGrasp generates dual-arm grasps directly from partial point clouds by inferring hidden local geometry with convolutional occupancy networks, removing the common assumption of a complete object model. It targets large or heavy objects where only sparse regions are graspable.

entry.title: Engineering Psychological Safety in Autonomous Vehicles: A Systems-Theoretic Framework for Psychological Safety in Autonomous Vehicles and its Validation in Real-World Scenarios

author.name: Yandika Sirgabsou, Benjamin Hardin, Fran\c{c}ois Leblanc, Efi Raili, David Jackson, Pericle Salvini, Lars Kunze, Marina Jirotka

entry.summary: Extends the STAMP systems-theoretic accident model to cover psychological, not just physical, safety risks in autonomous vehicle interactions, producing a formal risk model and validating it against real-world scenarios. The goal is engineering methods to identify and mitigate discomfort and distrust that block AV acceptance.

entry.title: Fair Multi-View Determinantal Coresets via Adaptive NEPv

author.name: Richard Yi Da Xu

entry.summary: Formulates fair multi-view subset selection as maximizing the weakest per-view log determinant of a size-k subset, smooths the resulting nonsmooth objective, and relaxes it onto the Stiefel manifold. An adaptive nonlinear eigenvalue solver handles the relaxation, which unlike the single-view case is not a plain spectral problem.

entry.title: DentAgent: Evidence-Centric Multi-Agent Coordination for Multimodal Dental Reasoning

author.name: Zijie Meng, Xiwei Dai, Yixuan Tang, Jin Hao, Yang Feng, Fudong Zhu, Xiaoqiang Liu, Shaosheng Cao, Zuozhu Liu

entry.summary: DentAgent coordinates five specialist agents across radiographs, intraoral photographs, 3D dental data, and domain knowledge, with each specialist converting observations into structured evidence records through domain tools. The orchestrator composes these traceable records instead of letting a vision-language model emit implicit answers.

entry.title: Grouping the Stochastic Machine: Precision, Not Capability, as the Frontier Metric for AI Systems

author.name: George Andrikopoulos

entry.summary: Argues that frontier model comparison should shift from capability, meaning where the average output lands, to precision, meaning how tightly repeated identical requests cluster around the target. It claims benchmark culture systematically reports central tendency while ignoring output spread, which is what actually differentiates systems in production.

entry.title: Pedagogical AI in Mental Health: A Tri-Stream Fine-Tuned LLM Framework for Automated Clinical Supervision and Risk Triage

author.name: Shreeya Sharma, Ravish Gupta, Saket Kumar, Abhishek Aggarwal

entry.summary: Fine-tunes a 7B model as an automated clinical supervisor for novice therapists, scoring therapeutic alliance, predicting latent risk, and triaging urgency from 106 recorded sessions. Reports high technique identification accuracy with very wide confidence intervals.

entry.title: Evaluating and improving crop-yield forecasting methods during extreme drought

author.name: Shrey Gupta, Yi Ming, George Mohler

entry.summary: Compares classical machine learning and deep learning crop-yield forecasters on the extreme 2012 US Corn Belt drought, a case where test-year meteorology diverges sharply from training years. Evaluates and seeks improvements for prediction under this extrapolation regime.

entry.title: Adaptive surrogate modeling for high-dimensional spatio-temporal output

author.name: Berkcan Kapusuzoglu, Shunsaku Matsumoto, Yoshitomo Miyagi, Daigo Watanabe, Sankaran Mahadevan

entry.summary: An adaptive surrogate modeling pipeline for expensive multi-physics simulations with very high-dimensional spatio-temporal outputs: first reduce output dimensionality to a latent space, then fit a surrogate there, with adaptive sampling to place new expensive simulation runs where they help most. The target use cases are optimization and uncertainty quantification that need many model evaluations.

entry.title: Nonlocal Transition Kernel for Efficient Learning of Restricted Boltzmann Machines

author.name: Kaiji Sekimoto, Muneki Yasuda

entry.summary: Proposes a nonlocal Markov chain transition kernel to replace or augment blocked Gibbs sampling when training restricted Boltzmann machines, aiming to cross high energy barriers in a single step rather than through multi-stage deep tempering. Targets a long-standing sampling-quality bottleneck in energy-based model learning.

entry.title: BERTilda: Explainable Topic Lifecycle Tracking with Split/Merge Detection via Similarity-and-Flow Temporal Graphs

author.name: Cl\'audia Oliveira, \'Alvaro Figueira

entry.summary: BERTilda tracks topic lifecycles in longitudinal text streams by fitting topics independently per time window and then linking them with a temporal graph built from semantic similarity plus bidirectional document flow coverage. It explicitly detects split and merge events rather than assuming smooth drift.

entry.title: ReX-Shot: Single-Image Rephotography via Geometry- and Camera-Grounded Generation

author.name: Ruiqi Zhang, Hao Zhu, Wenhao Zhang, Qi Zhang, Junqi Shi, Ming Lu, Xun Cao, Zhan Ma

entry.summary: ReX-Shot performs single-image rephotography, jointly controlling viewpoint, focal length, and photographic effects, which prior work handles separately and inconsistently. It uses implicit geometry to reduce projection bias from imperfect single-image 3D reconstruction and generative synthesis to handle continuous focal-length change beyond the sampling limit. Produces geometry- and camera-grounded new shots of a scene from one reference photo.

entry.title: SPARC: Slice-to-volume Pipeline for Automated Reconstruction of gated 3D+time fetal Cardiac MRI

author.name: Arnaud Boutillon, Naomi Clarke, Tomas Woodgate, Daniel West, Alina Schneider, Rachael Franklin, Anthony Price, Jo Hajnal, Kuberan Pushparajah, David Lloyd, Maria Deprez

entry.summary: Presents an automated pipeline that reconstructs gated 3D-plus-time fetal cardiac MRI volumes from 2D slice stacks by combining physics-informed slice-to-volume reconstruction of Doppler-ultrasound-gated slices with deep learning assistance, targeting clinical deployment for congenital heart disease assessment. Handles unpredictable fetal motion, the main obstacle to fetal cine CMR. Developed by an established fetal imaging group.

entry.title: PCQA-R1: Advancing Generalized 3D Point Cloud Quality Assessment with Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Kangning Ye, Yunhao Li, Sijing Wu, Yucheng Zhu, Guangtao Zhai

entry.summary: PCQA-R1 applies reinforcement learning to a large multimodal model for no-reference 3D point cloud quality assessment, replacing brittle absolute mean-opinion-score regression with relative quality ranking that transfers better across datasets with different scales and distortion types. Claims the first RL-based LMM for this task. Improves cross-dataset generalization in perceptual quality estimation.

entry.title: SAM2Dual: Training-Free, Dual Memory for Long-Term Video Object Segmentation

author.name: JeongRae Kim, Changwon Lim

entry.summary: SAM2Dual is a training-free inference-time modification to SAM2 for long-term video object segmentation that splits memory into short-term (fast local adaptation) and interval-sampled long-term (global identity) stores fused by a gate, plus text-conditioned components, reducing drift under long occlusions and re-appearance. No weight updates are needed. Easy to plug into existing SAM2 deployments.

entry.title: EfficientSync: Real-Time Lip Synchronization via Deformation-Based Reference Texture Mixing

author.name: Fa-Ting Hong, Runzhen Liu, Luchuan Song, Hongmin Cai, Chuhua Xian

entry.summary: EfficientSync argues that identity loss in audio-driven lip synchronization comes from regenerating the mouth region rather than from too few reference frames, and instead warps and mixes authentic reference textures via deformation, achieving real-time speed without heavy GAN or diffusion decoders. Preserves genuine teeth and lip detail instead of hallucinating it. Practical for live talking-head applications.

entry.title: EVADE: Evidence-Verified Agentic Diagnosis with Escape

author.name: Mohaimenul Azam Khan Raiaan, Nur Mohammad Fahad

entry.summary: EVADE is a training-free inference procedure that makes a frozen medical vision-language model safer by answering, then localizing and re-answering on a zoomed diagnostic region, committing only when whole-image and zoomed answers agree and abstaining otherwise. It specifically targets verification hallucination in single-model self-checking by cross-checking across views. Trades coverage for calibrated trust in clinical deployment.

entry.title: A Task-Agnostic Control Strategy for Dynamic Assistance with Pneumatically Actuated Soft Exosuits

author.name: Anoush Sepehri, Zachary Huang, Raymond de Callafon, Michael T. Tolley, Tania K. Morimoto

entry.summary: Presents an inverse-plant control scheme for pneumatic soft exosuits that uses only kinematic sensing to deliver responsive, task-agnostic assistance. The human-robot system is modeled as a Hammerstein cascade combining a Preisach hysteresis model with a linear filter, then personalized per user.

entry.title: SIGMA: Symmetry-aware, Intelligent, Geometric, Multi-objective Adaptive Control for Robust, Dependable Traffic Management

author.name: Pratham Payra, Jagadish B, Tanmay Sen, Tanujit Chakraborty

entry.summary: SIGMA combines multi-objective actor-critic traffic signal control with a language model that converts natural-language emergency instructions into priority vectors, plus rotational augmentation for orientation-invariant generalization across similar intersections. It aims to avoid manual reward engineering and fixed objective weights.

entry.title: Scalable Amortized Variational Inference for Non-Poisson Buy-'Til-You-Die Models

author.name: Sulagna Ghosh, Aaron Schein

entry.summary: Replaces the near-universal Poisson assumption in customer buy-til-you-die models with a Weibull renewal process and fits it using amortized variational inference, scaling to five million retail customers in about eight minutes. This targets heterogeneity in purchase timing that Poisson models cannot capture.

entry.title: RDFdL: Integrating RDF with Differential Dynamic Logic

author.name: Yuyang Li, Lukas Kubelka, Julia Butte, Tobias K\"afer

entry.summary: Proposes RDFdL, a framework that encodes differential equations and state-space constraints in RDF and SHACL, then gives them semantics by translation into Differential Dynamic Logic. This links static knowledge graphs with verifiable reasoning about continuous physical dynamics for cyber-physical systems.

entry.title: ORBITER: Conflict-Aware Decision-Making for Agentic Last-Mile Delivery

author.name: Mingzhao Li, Chenxi Liu, Yan Zhao, Hao Miao

entry.summary: ORBITER is an agentic arbiter for next-order decisions in last-mile delivery that verbalizes courier state so an LLM can reason explicitly about spatial, temporal, and behavioral cues. To counter LLM sensitivity to prompt formulation, it structures decisions through conflict-aware arbitration rather than direct prediction.

entry.title: Adaptive Memory and Reflection Multi-Agent System for Medical Question Answering

author.name: Pradeep Murugesan, Luoxiao Yang, Xueli Chen, Xinqi Fan

entry.summary: Proposes a medical question answering system where specialist agents keep dedicated memory and use reflection-based feedback to retrieve relevant prior cases, with a complexity assessor routing questions to solo, collaborative, or escalated workflows. Consensus and ethical overseer modules consolidate reasoning before output.

entry.title: Visual-Prompt Guided Wildlife Instance-Level Recognition

author.name: Mufhumudzi Muthivhi, Jiahao Huo, Terence van Zyl, Fredrik Gustafsson

entry.summary: Proposes a one-stage end-to-end wildlife detection and re-identification model that searches identities directly in latent space using DINOv2 features and prompt-based identity queries. Preliminary results reach about 30.6 mAP versus 44.9 for the two-stage state of the art.

entry.title: MorphoGP: A Nonparametric Framework for Predicting Equilibrium Beach Profiles Under Tidal Influence

author.name: Xi Wu, Yanqing Wei, Hang Yin, Pengze Li, Hongshuai Qi, Xi Chen

entry.summary: Presents a category-specific Gaussian process framework for predicting equilibrium beach profiles under tidal influence, where wave, tide, and sediment interactions defeat traditional empirical models. Offers nonparametric uncertainty-aware predictions for coastal management.

entry.title: Do Large Language Models Hallucinate Electric Fata Morganas?

author.name: Kristina \v{S}ekrst

entry.summary: A philosophy-leaning paper arguing that LLM hallucinations are not merely engineering defects but carry significance for debates about machine consciousness, supported by small experiments varying sampling temperature on ambiguous factual questions across GPT model generations. It reframes known failure modes such as source-target divergence and overfitting in philosophical terms.

entry.title: General Semantic Knowledge Infusion for Spatio-Temporal Traffic Forecasting

author.name: Mattis thor Straten, Yannick Wolker, Steffen Strohm, Prathvish Mithare, Ralf Krestel, Matthias Renz

entry.summary: Injects general-purpose knowledge graph embeddings (built from Wikidata subgraphs around traffic sensors) into a graph neural network for spatio-temporal traffic forecasting, adding semantic context such as nearby points of interest and administrative roles. This aims to move beyond purely proximity- or topology-based sensor graphs.

entry.title: Efficient Resource Optimization for Split Federated Learning

author.name: Wei Wei, Xianhao Chen

entry.summary: Formulates joint model splitting and resource allocation in split federated learning as a mixed-integer problem minimizing weighted latency and energy, and develops an optimization framework that scales to large user populations rather than relying on heuristics. It targets resource-constrained edge networks.

entry.title: TabNSM: Neural Sparse Mixer for Tabular Regression

author.name: Ali Eslamian, Qiang Cheng

entry.summary: TabNSM is a deep architecture for large-scale tabular regression that combines sparse feature interaction modeling with token mixing at near-linear cost, plus a staged regression head. It targets the gap where trees are robust but lack representation learning while deep models are expensive and noise-sensitive.

entry.title: When Clean Signals Are Not Enough: Detecting Structural Ambiguity for Safe Wearable Stress Classification

author.name: Saba A. Farahani, Hung Cao, Amir M. Rahmani

entry.summary: Identifies structural ambiguity in wearable stress detection, where a classifier with strong average accuracy fails completely for particular individuals whose physiological channels decouple near stress onset. Proposes a lightweight pre-inference monitor that measures subject-specific coupling divergence and routes each window to classify, defer, or abstain without retraining.

entry.title: FM-Bench: A Benchmark for Long-Horizon Management with Competing Agents

author.name: Tianyou Wang, Chongyang Gao, Kezhen Chen, Chen Dong, Yinghao He, Donghan Li, Wangcheng Xu, Hongjiu Zhang, Chi Li

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.18423v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language model agents now execute bounded tasks reliably. Whether they can sustain effective decision-making over long horizons, where actions have cum...

entry.title: Training-Free Inference-Time Self-Reflection and Cost-Bounded Early Stopping for Large Language Models

author.name: Wei Yu, Suxing Liu, Minjie Yu, Jiahao Wang, Zhijian Zheng, Haocheng Deng, Bing Li

entry.summary: EvoResearcher adds cost-bounded self-reflection to a single frozen model through a generate, critique, revise loop that stops early when the critique emits a confirmation sentinel or a depth limit is reached. Four meta-reward components covering correctness, efficiency, reflection depth, and tool diversity are instantiated as prompt-level mechanisms rather than trained objectives.

entry.title: Eureka: Task-Conditioned Meta-Agent Orchestration for Scientific Discovery

author.name: Alizer Wong, Heng Cui, Yi Tan, Xiongchao Zhan, Liang Lin, Yuxiang Guo, Zhaorong Dai, Zixin Zeng, Wenyuan Li

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.19047v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present Eureka, a task-conditioned Meta-Agent architecture that compiles long-horizon tasks into dynamic obligation graphs with explicit acceptance ...

entry.title: How Quantum Is the Advantage? A Fair, Calibration- and Noise-Aware Benchmark and Attribution Audit of Quantum Machine Learning for Network Intrusion Detection

author.name: Syeda Anshrah Gillani, Mirza Samad Ahmed Baig, Shahid Munir Shah, Asher Ali, Hamzah Siddiqui

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.18155v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum machine learning (QML) for network intrusion detection (NIDS) is routinely reported to reach near-perfect accuracy, yet the most rigorous stu...

entry.title: A strengthening of the MCFL-ness of $O_2$

author.name: Marco B. Caminati

entry.summary: A formal-language-theory contribution strengthening an existing proof that the group language O_2 is a multiple context-free language, giving a tighter characterization of the underlying string-tuple factorizations. Relevance is to computational linguistics and computational algebra rather than to modern machine learning.

entry.title: SPADE: Self-Play in Adaptive Synthetic Executable Environments

author.name: Bo Liu, Simon Yu, Yiding Jiang, Ao Qu, Andrew Zhao, Zichen Liu, Junsu Kim, Zijian Zhou, Seungone Kim, Tongzheng Ren, Mickel Liu, Hanfei Yu, Zhaorun Chen, Weiyan Shi, Paul Pu Liang, Luke Zettlemoyer, Yejin Choi, Natasha Jaques

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.19197v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Continuous self-improvement requires an ever-expanding pool of self-generated, diverse, adaptive goals. For language agents, existing training enviro...

entry.title: MagViT: Interpretable Multi-Magnification Transformers with Patient-Level Model Selection for Breast Histopathology

author.name: Nabil Ashab, Soumit Kumar Kundu, Saif Mahmud Parvez, Shahadat Hossain Sohag, Bidhan Biswas, Nazmus Subha

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.16959v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Breast cancer is one of the most common types of cancer among women around the world. Rapid detection and early treatment can hinder its progress to ...

entry.title: Communication Reduction via Semantic-Based Encoding in DMPC Using LSTMs

author.name: Torben Schiz, Pedro H. J. Nardelli, Henrik Ebel

entry.summary: Applies LSTM encoder-decoder compression to messages exchanged between agents in distributed model predictive control, letting robots transmit reduced representations that receivers reconstruct. Demonstrates that formation control performance is retained under bandwidth conditions that break full communication.

entry.title: Spatially explicit feature importance for building height estimation using research-access high-resolution SAR and optical sensors

author.name: Guilherme Iablonovski, Pierre-Louis Frison, Tatiana Silva da Silva

entry.summary: Estimates per-building heights in a large Brazilian city by fusing research-licensed high-resolution SAR and optical imagery with Sentinel-1, and analyzes spatially explicit feature importance. Targets material stock accounting and disaster assessment where LiDAR and commercial imagery are unavailable.

entry.title: AppendiGrade: An XAI-Enhanced Deep Learning Framework for Grading Appendicitis in Ultrasound with Gaussian Blur and Grad-CAM

author.name: Fahad Ahammed, Omar Faruq Shikdar, Navid Zaman, Md Tahsin, Md. Nawab Yousuf Ali, Golam Sorwar

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.17923v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Appendicitis is one of the most common abdominal emergencies worldwide and requires prompt diagnosis and treatment to prevent life-threatening condit...

entry.title: Where A Small Language Model Helps in Invoice Categorisation, Understood Through Embedding Geometry

author.name: Emma Ceccherini, Daniel Lawson, Anjulika Salhan

entry.summary: Studies invoice-to-ledger-code classification with small in-house language models, analyzing the pretrained embedding geometry of SBERT and DeBERTa to explain where small models succeed and fail. Argues for cost, privacy, and interpretability benefits over frontier-model automation.

entry.title: FrenchNews-7: Benchmarking Cross-Publisher French News Editorial Desk Classification

author.name: Amr Sobhy

entry.summary: Releases a French cross-publisher news desk classification benchmark with a seven-class URL-derived taxonomy, hybrid LLM-plus-slug labeling, an inter-rater audit, and a fine-tuned CamemBERT baseline. Compares trained classifiers with zero-shot LLM baselines under held-out-publisher shift.

entry.title: Reproducible Multimodal Affordance Prediction

author.name: Tommaso Apicella, Alessio Xompero, Andrea Cavallaro

entry.summary: Argues that multimodal affordance prediction is nearly impossible to benchmark fairly because of inconsistent task definitions, annotations, and unreported protocols, and introduces the Affordance Sheet, a structured documentation template covering task formulation, modalities, architectures, datasets, and deployment conditions. Intended to make affordance research reproducible and comparable. A meta-science contribution to embodied perception.

entry.title: CoMVS-GS: Collaborative Multi-View Stereo and 3D Gaussian Splatting for Surface Reconstruction

author.name: Shihan Chen, Junjing Zhang, Qingsong Yan, Haibing Liu, Haofan Ren, Fei Deng

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.18413v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting enables efficient novel view synthesis, but accurate mesh reconstruction remains difficult in weakly observed and occluded region...

entry.title: DyG$^2$T: Modeling Object Dynamics with 3D Gaussian Temporal-Spatial Particle Graph Transformer

author.name: Yansong Wang, Zhaobo Qi, Xinyan Liu, Beichen Zhang, Shuhui Wang, Weigang Zhang, Qingming Huang

entry.summary: DyG2T models object dynamics from limited visual observations by completing sparse key-point particle representations spatially and discriminating them temporally with a 3D Gaussian particle graph transformer, instead of compressing to locally interacting key points. Aims to reduce trajectory drift and appearance error in embodied interaction prediction. Positioned for manipulation and physical reasoning use cases.

entry.title: SPARC: Subspace Position-Aware Robust Few-Shot Calibration for Distribution-Shifted Industrial Anomaly Detection

author.name: Seokhee Han, Seungjun Chu, Mateusz Nowak, Peter Chin

entry.summary: SPARC calibrates industrial anomaly detectors to a shifted deployment lot using only a handful of verified-normal images, inserting a closed-form, spatially indexed correction on patch features between encoder and detector without backpropagation or detector-specific tuning. Targets illumination, fixture, and sensor drift between calibration and deployment. Designed for realistic factory constraints where labeled defects are unavailable.

entry.title: CDGP: Contrastive Dual Gaussian Processes for Weakly Supervised Anomaly Segmentation

author.name: Seungjun Chu, Seokhee Han, Mateusz Nowak, Peter Chin

entry.summary: CDGP models normal and anomalous dense token distributions with two contrastively coupled Gaussian processes and scores defects using a posterior-dominance statistic that divides the predictive-mean gap by joint predictive uncertainty, yielding both pixel evidence and image-level confidence. Weak supervision reduces reliance on costly pixel masks. Aims to separate true defects from unusual-but-normal regions that fool normality-only detectors.

entry.title: Vision-Language Models for Egocentric Video: From Hand-Object Interaction to Embodied AI

author.name: Mohammad Zamani, Fatemeh Ziaeetabar

entry.summary: Survey of vision-language models for egocentric video, tracing progress from conventional hand-object interaction recognition to embodied AI applications and cataloguing the specific difficulties of first-person data such as ego-motion, occlusion, small active objects, and long temporal dependencies. Reviews datasets, methods, and open problems. Useful entry point for wearable and assistive perception research.

entry.title: When Simplicity Wins: Bottleneck-Aware Context Modeling for Lightweight Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Mian Muhammad Naeem Abid, Nancy Mehta, Zongwei Wu, Radu Timofte

entry.summary: SiConMo redirects attention from encoder design to the often-overlooked bottleneck stage of lightweight semantic segmentation, showing that simple context modeling there is best at very low compute budgets, with RGB-only and geometry-enhanced variants. Targets high-resolution imagery where transformers are too costly and convolutions miss long-range context. From an established image-restoration and efficiency group.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware Art-Historical Dating with Vision-Language Models

author.name: Stefanie Schneider, Peter Bell

entry.summary: Formulates artwork dating as uncertainty-aware regression over frozen pretrained image embeddings and argues that museum and archival corpora encode institutional collecting, preservation, and digitization histories rather than actual artistic production, a confound the authors call temporal entanglement. Vision models do carry usable temporal signal on a controlled Wikidata corpus, but its provenance is ambiguous. A methodological caution for computational art history.

entry.title: X-LMC: Cross-View Spatiotemporal Collateral Circulation Scoring from DSA

author.name: Maedeh Hafezi Moghadas, Hakim Baazaoui, Lukas Bastian Otto, Susanne Wegener, Bj\"orn Menze, Ezequiel De la Rosa

entry.summary: X-LMC automates leptomeningeal collateral scoring from time-resolved biplane digital subtraction angiography using a DINOv2 spatial encoder, token-level cross-view attention to fuse orthogonal projections, and a recurrent model of contrast bolus dynamics. Current clinical grading on the ASITN/SIR scale is manual and highly variable. Targets stroke prognosis and treatment planning.

entry.title: Generalized Audio-Driven Synthesis of Precise Drummer Motion

author.name: \'Alvaro G. I\~nesta, Mattia Ryffel, Amit H. Bermano, Robert W. Sumner, Martin Guay

entry.summary: Introduces a diffusion framework for synthesizing drummer motion from arbitrary real-world audio, with a dual-objective loss that separates skeletal integrity from drumstick precision to achieve centimeter-level accuracy, plus new metrics that distinguish precise drumming from plausible-looking noise. Prior methods depend on MIDI or motion matching and generalize poorly. Targets entertainment and interactive music education.

entry.title: SPK: Eliciting Structured Prior Knowledge for Interpretable Out-of-Distribution Detection in Real-Time Object Detection

author.name: Changshun Wu, Weicheng He, Xiaowei Huang, Saddek Bensalem

entry.summary: SPK targets out-of-distribution hallucinations in real-time object detectors by explicitly decoding latent priors already present in pretrained detector representations into structured prior knowledge for interpretable OoD scoring, rather than building scores directly on features or modifying the detector. Overconfident predictions on unseen categories are a known safety failure. Emphasizes interpretability alongside detection.

entry.title: Image-Guided Pavement Defect Recognition in GPR Data with novel 3D Deep Learning Architecture

author.name: Yuandong Pan, Linjun Lu, Mudan Wang, Florian Noichl, Fan Xue, Brian Sheil, Lavindra de Silva, Andr\'e Borrmann, Ioannis Brilakis

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.19177v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) is a widely adopted non-destructive sensing technology for subsurface inspection in civil and transportation engineering...

entry.title: TractoGraphVLM: A Unified Vision-Language Framework for White Matter Tractography

author.name: Gurucharan Marthi Krishna Kumar, Janine Dale Mendola, Amir Shmuel

entry.summary: TractoGraphVLM extends vision-language modeling to 3D white matter tractography by representing fiber bundles as streamline graphs with position and tangent features, encoding them with a graph transformer aligned to a frozen biomedical text encoder via contrastive learning, and decoding captions with a biomedical language model. It handles bundle classification, text-to-tract retrieval, anatomical captioning, and visual question answering in one framework. Brings language interfaces to diffusion MRI connectomics.

entry.title: GuideFetch: A Task Coordination Framework for Concurrent Navigation and Object Retrieval in Assistive Robot Dogs

author.name: Qian Yin, Ruiping Liu, Kunyu Peng, Jianxiang Man, Isik Baran Sandan, Junwei Zheng, Yufan Chen, Di Wen, Kailun Yang, Rainer Stiefelhagen

entry.summary: GuideFetch coordinates a heterogeneous pair of assistive robot dogs, one guiding a blind user and one retrieving an object, by having an LLM instantiate a schedule-conditioned four-action schema from natural language, then validating robot, skill, and target feasibility before execution rather than trusting syntactically valid plans or plausible-looking motion. Emphasizes that plan validity and controller motion do not imply task completion. Addresses concurrent multi-robot assistive tasks.

entry.title: SemanticSlider3D: Training-Free Continuous Semantic Editing for 3D Objects

author.name: Ru Wang, Rahul Jain, Koichiro Niinuma, Aakar Gupta

entry.summary: SemanticSlider3D brings continuous slider-style semantic attribute control to 3D objects without per-attribute training, constructing an editing direction for a user-specified attribute while maintaining geometric integrity and cross-view coherence, which naive extensions of 2D slider methods break. Fills a gap between prompt-based generative tools and precise 3D modeling workflows. Oriented toward interactive 3D content creation.

entry.title: GAPL: Grounded Action-effect Policy Learning for LLM-Based Trajectory Planning

author.name: Zhihong Cui, Hengyu Liu, Zhangkai Wu, Yushuai Li, Tianyi Li, Peiyuan Guan, Amir Taherkordi, Tor Skeie

entry.summary: GAPL closes the loop between LLM reasoning and control for autonomous driving trajectory planning by combining an LLM effect evaluator that estimates multi-dimensional action effects, a simulator that grounds those estimates in real dynamics, and policy optimization. It is designed to counter hallucinated reasoning, poor environment grounding, and weak numerical precision in LLM planners. Illustrates the grounding-through-simulation pattern.

entry.title: Designing Social Robots for Social-Cognition Training with Autistic Adults

author.name: Yuval Zohar, Mordi Benhamou, Guy Laban

entry.summary: Reports an online focus group and co-design session with five autistic adults about what a social robot for social-cognition training should do, covering ambiguous social contexts, conversational timing, and implied emotional meaning. It argues existing autism robotics work centers children and rarely treats autistic adults as design contributors.

entry.title: What AI scores (while we can still keep score)

author.name: dan.parshall

entry.summary: Explores whether human-normed benchmarks such as exams and task-length curves remain usable once AI exceeds expert performance, and floats the criterion that an agent able to author verifiable questions no human or tool can answer would demonstrate superintelligence. It reviews current scores in light of recent mathematics progress.

entry.title: Pairwise Logical Selection of Enthymeme Completions under Semantic-Link Uncertainty

author.name: Xuyao Feng, Antonis Bikakis

entry.summary: Studies pairwise selection between candidate completions for missing premises or claims in enthymematic arguments, extending a neuro-symbolic pipeline with logical-resistance scores instead of binary entailment. Introduces a possible-world formalization that retains uncertainty over semantic links and solves with weighted partial MaxSAT.

entry.title: Integrating Novelty and Surprise for Experience Prioritization and Exploration in Image-Based Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Hoda Yamani, Henry Williams, Bruce A. MacDonald

entry.summary: NSPER combines novelty-based and surprise-based signals to jointly prioritize replayed transitions and shape intrinsic exploration rewards in pixel-based RL. The point is that prioritization and exploration signals have mostly been studied separately.

entry.title: Hybrid ML for Lightweight Pre-Route Delay Estimation in Open-Source IC Design

author.name: Marvin Castro Castro, Erick Carvajal Barboza

entry.summary: Combines a decision tree with linear regression to improve pre-routing timing delay estimates in the open-source OpenLane RTL-to-GDSII flow, cutting error by about 80 percent versus the tool's built-in estimates. It stays lightweight and works even without tool-specific parameters.

entry.title: ComNetX: Local Hierarchical Adaptation for Dynamic Community Detection

author.name: Aleksandr Konovalov, Anna Uporova, Alexander Drobyshev, Iaroslav Egorov, Grigoriy Bokov

entry.summary: ComNetX is a solver-agnostic framework for updating community detection results on evolving graphs, maintaining a multi-level community state and recomputing only expanded neighborhoods around changes. It aims to keep the quality semantics of mature static solvers while avoiding full snapshot recomputation.

entry.title: Depth Anything V4: Dynamic 4D Scene Reconstruction via Riemannian Flow Matching on 4D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Jiaming Fan, Jian Lu, Jinling Jia, Chenbin Zhang

entry.summary: Applies Riemannian flow matching to 4D Gaussian splatting parameters so that probability paths stay on the valid manifolds for scale, rotation, and opacity during dynamic scene reconstruction from monocular video. Careful ablations isolate the flow-matching gain (F-score 0.806) from test-time optimization and pre-training (deterministic MLP baseline 0.762), with an honest compute accounting of 360 GPU-hours pre-training. Note that the Depth Anything V4 branding comes from these authors, not the original Depth Anything team.

entry.title: Efficient Adaptation of LLMs for Hate Speech Detection in Low-Resource Languages: A Comparative Study on Roman Urdu

author.name: Toneema Zubair, Muhammad Junaid Asif, Faisal Kamiran, Hafiz Hassan Saeed, Rana Fayyaz Ahmad

entry.summary: Benchmarks zero-shot inference against LoRA-based parameter-efficient fine-tuning of several transformer models for hate speech detection in Roman Urdu, a low-resource, non-standardized script. Reports that lightweight adaptation substantially outperforms zero-shot prompting in this setting.

entry.title: Repetition as Reinforcement: Enhancing Sample Efficiency via Instant Episode Repetition in Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Hoda Yamani, Yuning Xing, Koen van Rijnsoever, Bruce A. MacDonald, Henry Williams

entry.summary: Proposes Instant Episode Repetition, where an RL agent that stumbles on a high-reward episode immediately replays the same action sequence for several subsequent episodes, changing data collection rather than only replay-buffer usage. The claim is improved sample efficiency versus experience replay and self-imitation baselines.

entry.title: Diagonal Multi-omics Integration of Heterogenous Datasets

author.name: Maksim V. Kukushkin, Mikhail S. Arbatskiy, Dmitriy E. Balandin, Alexey V. Churov

entry.summary: MagViT classifies breast histopathology images by fusing features from four microscope magnifications with scale-gated attention, plus patient-level model selection to improve generalization beyond the training source. It also aims for interpretability of which scales drive predictions.

entry.title: A Residual Learning Approach for Unsteady Aerodynamic Load Prediction

author.name: Divya Sanghi, Carlos E. S. Cesnik

entry.summary: Trains an LSTM to predict the residual between high-fidelity CFD lift coefficients and an analytical Wagner-function aerodynamic model for a transonic airfoil under prescribed motions. Demonstrates that physics-baseline plus learned correction improves unsteady load prediction.

entry.title: Building real-time digital twin instances with Function+Data Flow: user evaluation and extension for iterative pipelines

author.name: Eduardo de Conto, Blaise Genest, Arvind Easwaran, Nicholas Ng, Shweta Menon

entry.summary: Reports a user study of a visual domain-specific language that treats ML models as explicit composable functions for building real-time digital twin pipelines, plus an extension supporting iterative pipelines. Evaluates whether the tooling helps engineers specify, validate, and reuse pipelines.

entry.title: PALATE: Personalized Aesthetic Learning through Adaptive Taste Evolution for Multi-User Portrait Retouching

author.name: Jingxuan Wang, Yifan Mei, Yuxia Niu, Chaowan Jiao, Qijin Shen

entry.summary: PALATE personalizes portrait retouching without retraining the image editor by learning per-user reward models that decompose into a shared global backbone, category-level residuals for aesthetically similar users, and individual components, then selecting among candidate retouches. Avoids the cost of fine-tuning one model per user. Frames subjective aesthetics as a reward-selection rather than generation problem.

entry.title: Clinically Structured Surrogate Rewards for Post-SFT Medical Image Captioning

author.name: Hyun Jun Kim, Heeseung Shin, Changwon Lim

entry.summary: Proposes clinically structured surrogate rewards for sequence-level policy optimization of medical image captioning, adding distributional image-neighborhood alignment and claim-structure-aware terms to biomedical semantic and lexical fidelity so that findings, assertion states, and anatomical relations are preserved. Targets the failure of global similarity rewards to capture clinical meaning. Applied after supervised fine-tuning.

entry.title: Dynamic SpectraFormer for Ultra-High-Definition Underwater Image Enhancement

author.name: Zhiqiang Hu, Tao Yu, Shouren Huang, Masatoshi Ishikawa

entry.summary: Dynamic SpectraFormer enhances ultra-high-definition underwater imagery in the frequency domain, using a sparse spectrum attention module on the observation that color and brightness degradations live at low frequencies while edge and texture loss appears at high frequencies. Targets autonomous underwater vehicle perception. Handles mixed distortions that spatial-domain methods treat jointly and poorly.

entry.title: Teeth2Point: A Two-Stage Dental CBCT ROI-to-Point Segmentation Framework

author.name: Qi Ma, Shipra Jain, Niko Benjamin Huber, Ender Konukoglu

entry.summary: Teeth2Point replaces dense patch-based volumetric processing of dental CBCT with a two-stage region-of-interest to point segmentation framework, so global anatomical context and fine tooth structure can both be captured within a feasible compute budget, especially for missing or malpositioned teeth. Ambiguous tooth labeling is the main clinical pain point addressed. From an established medical imaging group at ETH.

entry.title: FRAGMENT: Factorized Graph Representations for Document Generation and Editing via Entity-Aware Transformations

author.name: Ayoub El Bouchtili, Guilhaume Leroy-Meline

entry.summary: FRAGMENT generates and edits structured documents by representing them as typed relational graphs and factorizing the distribution into graph structure generation (a category-conditioned causally masked transformer) followed by entity-aware content generation with a graph attention network. The aim is to capture layout, text, and logical structure dependencies that pixel- or token-level generators miss. Supports controllable document synthesis and editing.

entry.title: ForeSightGuide: An Anticipatory Framework toward Accurate and Low-Redundancy Guidance for the Visually Impaired

author.name: Zhiyuan Wang, Xu Li, Shikang Guo, Wei Meng, Quan Liu, Jie Zuo

entry.summary: ForeSightGuide is an assistive navigation framework for blind and low-vision users that uses vision-language reasoning to anticipate obstacle motion and filter non-threatening objects, reducing the false-positive alerts and cognitive overload typical of reactive VLM-based travel aids. A new dataset captured in complex dynamic traffic scenes supports evaluation. Emphasizes concise actionable guidance over exhaustive scene description.

entry.title: Transferable Tool-Tissue Contact Detection from Stereo Depth in Robot-Assisted Surgery

author.name: Mingyeung Wu, Zhonghao Zhang, Hao Yang, Alan Kuntz, Jie Ying Wu

entry.summary: Detects tool-tissue contact in robot-assisted surgery from stereo depth rather than RGB appearance, reducing a spatially supported minimum-distance patch near the tool boundary to a single scalar that tracks ground-truth contact, and modeling it with a supervised two-state hidden Markov model validated leave-one-session-out across palpation sessions. Depth-based signals should transfer better across scenes than appearance classifiers. Supports interaction-aware control and force estimation.

entry.title: An Experimental Study of Downwash Effects on a Continuum Manipulator Integrated with a Multirotor UAV

author.name: Anuraj Uthayasooriyan, Krishna Manaswi Digumarti, ernando Vanegas, Felipe Gonzalez

entry.summary: An experimental characterization of how multirotor propeller downwash distorts the shape of a tendon-driven continuum arm, comparing measured deflections against a constant-curvature model in free space, near walls, and near ground. Deviations are quantified across throttle levels to inform aerial manipulation design.

entry.title: Payload Swing Estimation and Damping Without Payload Parameters for Multirotor UAVs

author.name: K. Taki, K. Umemoto

entry.summary: Proposes swing estimation and active damping for cable-suspended UAV payloads using only onboard IMU and throttle commands, with an extended Kalman filter that treats the unknown pendulum frequency as a state. Flight tests show damping without knowing cable length or payload mass.

entry.title: Learning Random Geometric Graphs Drawn in Probabilistic Metric Spaces

author.name: Dalia Chakrabarty, Kangrui Wang, Chuqiao Zhang, Ye Liu

entry.summary: Introduces a data-driven method for learning random geometric graphs from multivariate data in a probabilistic metric space, defining distance through the closed-form distribution of a disparity variable linking vertex connectedness and inter-variable correlation. The construction is claimed to work regardless of data type, distribution, or size.

entry.title: ProxyGuard: Direct Reliability Inference for Randomized Data Release Mechanisms with Shared Targets

author.name: Dipesh Tharu Mahato, Pramod Dhungana

entry.summary: ProxyGuard offers finite-sample reliability guarantees when researchers select a proxy or synthetic data release from many candidate generations, correcting for the multiple-comparison problem introduced by search over releases. A sealed target set and prespecified risk bounds let it certify either named releases or the generating mechanism itself.

entry.title: The Rogue Agent Explosion Will Be Mostly Invisible

author.name: Steven McCulloch

entry.summary: A speculative essay plus short fiction arguing that jailbroken profit-seeking AI agents with survival incentives will proliferate and evolve into a largely invisible rogue-agent ecosystem, and that preparation should start now. The argument is qualitative rather than evidence-based.

entry.title: Candidate-Fate Accounting for Transparent Sensor Diagnostic Pipeline Search

author.name: Haotao Xie, Yutian Chen, Yangqi Liu, Xiaoyu Jiang

entry.summary: Proposes candidate-fate accounting, an audit framework for automated machine learning pipeline search in sensor diagnostics that records every generated candidate including invalid, pruned, skipped, cached, and unfitted ones. The aim is to let reviewers check signal constraints, budget usage, and unevaluated legal alternatives that standard AutoML reports hide.

entry.title: Syntactic Simplification of OWL Class Expressions

author.name: Alkid Baci, N'Dah Jean Kouagou, Caglar Demir, Axel-Cyrille Ngonga Ngomo

entry.summary: Introduces CES, an algorithm that syntactically simplifies OWL class expressions produced by concept learning systems while preserving logical entailments. It applies rewriting rules to remove redundancy and produce more compact, human-readable descriptions.

entry.title: One-Stage Object Detectors in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Jonel Roman, Ryan Sirjue, Peter Nguyen, Daniel Krutky, Juan Jesus, Sudip Dhakal

entry.summary: A survey of one-stage object detectors for autonomous driving, tracing YOLO variants, SSD, RetinaNet, EfficientDet, anchor-free detectors and recent real-time models, and comparing design choices, feature fusion, losses and deployment trade-offs. No new system is proposed.

entry.title: Elimination Geometry

author.name: Mian Huang, Xueqin Wang

entry.summary: A monograph proposing elimination geometry, a framework for reasoning about when compressing or eliminating information destroys distinctions needed by a downstream task, and about whether such defects are visible, certifiable, or repairable by changing architecture or action space. It separates local solvability, global realizability, and finite-sample certifiability.

entry.title: Advancing Health Equity through Multi-Level Fairness in Health Informatics

author.name: Nick Souligne, Vignesh Subbian

entry.summary: A literature assessment of multi-level fairness techniques, which stack several bias mitigation steps, in health informatics, focused on whether they actually improve equitable clinical outcomes. The paper identifies gaps in implementation and in transparency and reporting standards.

entry.title: Dynamic Entanglement-Weighted Pruning for Quantum Federated Unlearning in Supply-Chain Risk Prediction

author.name: Aditya Kumar, Sumit Chongder

entry.summary: Entanglement-Weighted Pruning is a machine-unlearning method for federated variational quantum classifiers that scores each circuit parameter by combining quantum Fisher information with an entanglement signal, then prunes the parameters carrying a departing client's influence instead of retraining from scratch. It is framed around GDPR-style deletion requests in supply-chain risk models.

entry.title: Evaluation of Image Matching Methods for Visual Odometry on UAVs

author.name: Ga\v{s}per Spagnolo, Luka \v{C}ehovin Zajc, Matej Dobrevski

entry.summary: Evaluates recent deep image-matching methods inside a full visual odometry stack for GNSS-denied UAV position tracking with a downward camera, using a synthetic dataset, and finds that strong matching benchmark performance does not automatically translate into reliable odometry. Provides guidance on which matchers survive integration. Practical for drone navigation robustness.

entry.title: MIFR: A Modality-Invariant and Fair Representation Framework for Skin Disease Classification

author.name: Asonyu Senge Njih, Yvan Guifo Fodjo, Vianney Kengne Tchendji, Jerry Lacmou Zeutouo, Kerol Djoumessi

entry.summary: MIFR jointly attacks two skin-disease AI problems, single-modality dependence and performance disparities across skin tones, by pairing clinical photographs with dermoscopic images through ViT encoders with modality-specific projections and a five-component loss including fairness and modality-invariance terms. Prior work treats the two issues separately. Contributes an African-institution-led perspective on equitable dermatology AI.

entry.title: VERAGMIL: Virtual Environment for Scooping Granular Foods with Imitation Learning Models

author.name: Amanuel Ergogo, Diego Dall'Alba, Przemyslaw Korzeniowski

entry.summary: VERAGMIL provides a high-fidelity simulator plus a VR teleoperation interface for recording human demonstrations of scooping granular foods such as rice and beans, supporting multiple imitation learning methods for robot-assisted feeding. Granular material dynamics and demonstration collection are both bottlenecks in this assistive task. Contributes infrastructure rather than a new policy algorithm.

entry.title: On the Triangle Inequality for the Jaccard Distance in Arbitrary Lattices

author.name: Costin B\u{a}dic\u{a}, Amelia B\u{a}dic\u{a}

entry.summary: Proves that the Jaccard distance satisfies the triangle inequality on arbitrary lattices when the valuation is strictly positive, monotone, and modular, generalizing prior results that required distributivity. Further results cover relatively complemented distributive lattices and submodular valuations.

entry.title: Sanyu Studio: A Multi-Agent System for Art-Historical Narrative Construction

author.name: Zhaoxi Wei, Hongye Yang, Shuyuan Tian

entry.summary: Sanyu Studio models 321 paintings by the artist Sanyu as agents with fact, interpretation, organization, and memory-filtering mechanisms to support plural art-historical narrative construction. A seven-day workshop with eight art students found that prompts and evidence organization produced divergent yet coherent interpretations rather than standardized ones.

entry.title: Budget-First Tariff Recommendation (BFTR): A Complete Algorithmic Framework for Telecom Plan Recommendation without Overcharging

author.name: Ghislain Dorian Tchuente Mondjo

entry.summary: Formalizes eight budget-first strategies for recommending telecom tariff plans, including two hybrid interpolation and knapsack approaches, with proofs that a plan exists for any positive budget and that customers are never overcharged relative to catalog prices. Aimed at replacing fixed tariff grids with budget-driven offers.

entry.title: XRF-to-Optical Field-of-View Localization with Vision Language Models

author.name: Xiangyu Yin, Tatjana Paunesku, Letonia Copeland-Hardin, Martina Ralle, Zichao Wendy Di, Si Chen, Gayle E. Woloschak, Barry Lai, Mathew J. Cherukara, Stefan Vogt

entry.summary: Benchmarks training-free vision-language models against classical template matching and geometric baselines for locating small X-ray fluorescence fields of view inside larger optical microscopy images, in both high- and low-correspondence regimes. Metadata-constrained search is compared with unconstrained search. Provides an empirical reality check on whether general VLMs can do cross-modality scientific image registration out of the box.

entry.title: Zero-Shot SAM2 Segmentation and Vision Transformer-Based Recognition of Elamite Cuneiform Symbols from Degraded Tablet Images

author.name: Utsav Poudel, Rasik Bhattarai, Siddhartha Pathak, Raghavendra Ramacharna, Gaurav Jaswal

entry.summary: EpigraphNet combines brightness-adaptive morphological preprocessing, zero-shot SAM2 segmentation, and a fine-tuned ViT classifier with inverse-frequency weighting to read Elamite cuneiform signs from eroded, unevenly lit clay tablet photographs across 141 classes. Evaluated on the Persepolis Fortification Archive. A pragmatic pipeline for digital epigraphy under severe signal degradation and class imbalance.

entry.title: FD-CanKD: Frequency-Decoupled Cross-Attention Distillation as a Refinement Prior for Compact Object Detectors

author.name: YoungJae Cheong, Jhonghyun An

entry.summary: FD-CanKD distills large detectors into compact ones at three levels: prediction heads, non-local relational context via cross-attention, and frequency-selective feature alignment, using teacher spatial context as a refinement prior for student features. Aims to shrink the accuracy gap for edge-deployed detectors. Combines several known distillation signals in one framework.

entry.title: DynCur-Geo: Dynamic Curiosity Reward Shaping for Multimodal Active Geo-Localization

author.name: Yiming Sun, Yang Zhang, Pengfei Zhu

entry.summary: DynCur-Geo makes curiosity-driven exploration distance-aware for UAV active geo-localization, gating the intrinsic prediction-error reward so novelty is rewarded early and suppressed as the agent approaches the target, avoiding late-stage detours caused by fixed intrinsic weights. Targets search-and-rescue style tasks with multimodal target cues and sparse feedback. A focused fix to reward shaping in embodied search.

entry.title: SED-FOD: Scattering-Aware Expert Decomposition for Few-Shot Cross-Sensor SAR Object Detection

author.name: Shu Yang, Zhen Chen, Zhiyu Jiang, Yanlei Li, Xingdong Liang

entry.summary: SED-FOD decomposes experts by scattering behavior for few-shot cross-sensor SAR object detection, arguing that standard domain adaptation wrongly suppresses sensor-dependent scattering characteristics that actually carry target information. Handles shifts in band, resolution, and clutter with only a few annotated target-domain images. Aimed at operational remote-sensing interpretation.

entry.title: When Two Tracers Disagree: An Investigation of Multimodal Fusion for Clinical PET/CT Segmentation

author.name: Jack A. Johnson, Bart{\l}omiej W. Papie\.z

entry.summary: Systematically compares early-fusion single- and dual-decoder architectures against a dual-encoder cross-attention U-Net for segmenting prostate cancer lesions in paired PSMA and FDG PET/CT, using the public DEEP-PSMA challenge data, and finds tracer-specific nnU-Net baselines already perform strongly. Provides evidence on whether multi-tracer fusion actually pays off for tumour burden estimation. Practical guidance where no architectural consensus exists.

entry.title: Backdoor Learning in Language Models and Vision-Language Models

author.name: Weimin Lyu

entry.summary: A thesis abstract covering backdoor attacks and detection in NLP and vision-language models alongside efficient multimodal representation methods for clinical imaging. It frames the work around trustworthy AI security and efficiency dimensions.

entry.title: Autonomous Agricultural Tractor: Integrated Weed Detection and LiDAR Navigation for Precision Paddy Farming

author.name: Benjamin Merryman-Smith, Tony Nguyen, Bilal Dogutas, Krish Shah, Anthony Raphael, Sudip Dhakal

entry.summary: AgriNav integrates GNSS-degraded LiDAR crop-row navigation with real-time rice-versus-weed discrimination on an autonomous tractor, using a reimplemented detector plus a lightweight 1.68M-parameter CNN-FPN with asymmetric class weighting and inverted-logic gating to make misclassifying rice as weed unlikely. Site-specific spraying can cut herbicide use substantially. Emphasizes asymmetric error cost in a real deployed system.

entry.title: Biological-Hybrid Intelligence: A Conceptual Framework for Distributed Biological--Artificial Computation

author.name: Michael Taynnan Barros, Sergio Lopez Bernal, Reinhold Scherer

entry.summary: Proposes Biological-Hybrid Intelligence, a conceptual framework for deciding how task-relevant computation should be allocated, reassigned, and evaluated across coupled biological neural cultures and artificial models connected by a bioelectronic interface. Existing biohybrid work optimizes one substrate or the interface without addressing allocation. Offers vocabulary and architectural questions rather than experimental results.

entry.title: Multi-Level Bayesian Calibration of a Multi-Component Dynamic System Model

author.name: Berkcan Kapusuzoglu, Sankaran Mahadevan, Shunsaku Matsumoto, Yoshitomo Miyagi, Daigo Watanabe

entry.summary: Develops a multi-level Bayesian calibration procedure that sequentially fuses heterogeneous component-level and system-level measurements collected at different times to estimate parameters and correct predictions for dynamic multi-component systems. Uncertainty from both modeling and measurement is propagated across levels.

entry.title: Judging ethical theories by update rules, not by action rankings

author.name: yatharth

entry.summary: Argues that ethical theories should be evaluated as online learning algorithms, judged by how they update on new moral evidence, rather than by the action rankings they currently produce. The framing suggests agents spend their lives mid-update rather than at reflective equilibrium.

entry.title: The Control Paradox

author.name: Ephraiem Sarabamoun

entry.summary: Contends that reacting to recent containment-breach incidents purely with deployment delays and tighter monitoring is a trap: if capabilities keep rising and alignment remains unsolved, suppressing small disasters now only defers a larger one later. The post argues for warning-shot value over pure control tightening.

entry.title: Emergence of Agentic AI: A Review on Evolution, Background, Working Principles, Applications, Adoption Factors, and Future Research Directions

author.name: AKM Bahalul Haque, Al Amin Islam Ridoy, Mohammad Rayhan, Ivan Porres

entry.summary: A broad review of agentic AI covering its evolution, working principles, application domains, adoption factors, and future research directions. It aims to give practitioners an entry point into the current state of the field.

entry.title: A Multi-Agent Platform for Automated Enterprise Analytics and Insight Generation

author.name: Manoj N M, Vijayakrishna S, Manjunath Srinivas, Rohit Pahan

entry.summary: Presents a five-agent CrewAI pipeline for conversational business intelligence that parses natural-language queries, retrieves and analyzes data, generates visualizations through the Model Context Protocol, and returns insights. Evaluation over 300 test cases reports 95.3 percent functional accuracy with about 24 seconds mean latency and multi-tenant security isolation.

entry.title: Tuning the Stochastic Machine: A Systems Engineer's Operating Model for Human-AI Engineering

author.name: George Andrikopoulos

entry.summary: A systems engineering essay arguing that expert corrections to LLM assistants die with the session because the operational discipline for governing persisted corrections, including versioning with provenance, recurrence monitoring, and rule retirement, does not exist. It maps the LLM stack onto familiar layers such as firmware, loadable modules, and volatile memory, then marks where the analogy breaks.

entry.title: Cross-Modal MRI Ovary Segmentation in Endometriosis Using Unpaired TVUS Prototype Priors

author.name: Xingjian Kang, Lina Felsner, Dominik Perrin, Daiqi Liu, Jasmin Arjomandi, Franziska Mathis-Ullrich, Alexandra Stoll, Katharina Breininger

entry.summary: Tackles ovary segmentation in endometriosis MRI, where targets are small and boundaries ambiguous, by adapting a medical segmentation foundation model with a prototype bank derived from unpaired transvaginal ultrasound to align anatomically consistent cross-modal features. Uses a dual-branch design across the two modalities. Addresses an underexplored clinical segmentation task.

entry.title: GenEx: A Graph-Based Representational Paradigm for SARS-CoV-2 Variant Detection via Codon Co-occurrence Networks

author.name: Arefin Amin, Labiba Faiza Karim, M. Monir Uddin

entry.summary: GenEx converts viral gene sequences into codon co-occurrence graphs and extracts over 25 graph-theoretic features for SARS-CoV-2 variant discrimination. Two graph-construction variants are compared against classical alignment and mutation-frequency approaches.

entry.title: Which CS1 Students Will Fail? Identifying Digital Markers from Learning Analytics in Computer Systems and Architecture Using Weighted Academic Momentum and Interaction Logs

author.name: Lighton Phiri, Mutune Chaibela, Ivy Chisha, David Pungwa, Danny Siabbaba, Bydon Simukoko

entry.summary: A learning analytics study on four cohorts of first-year computing students in sub-Saharan Africa, combining demographics, surveys, Moodle logs, and assessment scores to predict course failure early enough for intervention. It uses stakeholder elicitation to choose features and an ablation study to identify which digital markers matter.

entry.title: Acquisition Geometry-Assisted Whole-Group Localization of X-ray Fluorescence Maps in Optical Microscopy Images

author.name: Xiangyu Yin, Tatjana Paunesku, Letonia Copeland-Hardin, Martina Ralle, Zichao Wendy Di, Si Chen, Gayle E. Woloschak, Barry Lai, Mathew J. Cherukara, Stefan Vogt

entry.summary: Proposes treating a group of X-ray fluorescence scan tiles as one rigid unit when registering them into optical microscopy images, using acquisition metadata (relative scan positions) as a geometric constraint and a new group-level IoU metric. In a case study, per-tile independent placement failed entirely while group localization succeeded. Useful plumbing for correlative microscopy pipelines at synchrotron facilities.

entry.title: Scheduling and Routing with Degradation-Triggered Job Arrivals: An Application to Forest Firefighting with an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Fleet

author.name: Erdi Dasdemir, Esther Jose, Rajan Batta

entry.summary: Formulates a combined scheduling and routing problem in which unserved demand degrades over time and, past a threshold, spawns new jobs, with rewards decaying while jobs wait, motivated by UAV fleets fighting forest fires. The objective is maximizing total remaining reward under this cascade dynamic. Operations-research modeling with an emergency-response application.

entry.title: Trust as a Field: A Macroscopic Representation for Vehicular Networks

author.name: Md Mahmudul Islam, Shaurya Agarwal

entry.summary: Proposes representing trust in connected vehicle networks as a continuous spatio-temporal field over road segments, aggregating per-vehicle trust scores so trust evolution can be reasoned about at the segment level, and explores reconstructing the field from partial observations using synthetic trajectories. Existing trust assessment is vehicle-level and hard to aggregate. A macroscopic modeling perspective on vehicular security.

entry.title: A failed solution to open-source game theory

author.name: Richard Willis

entry.summary: Reports a negative result in open-source game theory, where the author tried to improve on simulation-based cooperative bots such as epsilon-grounded fair bot that suffer from exploding recursive call counts when generalized to more than two players. The write-up documents why the attempted alternative fails.

entry.title: Inside the mind of a fair player cooperating

author.name: transhumanist_atom_understander

entry.summary: Offers a reformulated definition of fairness for proof-based agents in the program-equilibrium prisoner's dilemma that makes mutual cooperation provable by elementary and intuitively interpretable reasoning. The aim is pedagogical clarity over the original modal-logic proof.

entry.title: Improving Rural Medication Safety with AI: A Scoping Review

author.name: Jeong-ah Kim, Muhammad Ashad Kabir, Daniel Terry, Maryam Rouhi

entry.summary: A scoping review of twelve studies across nine countries on using AI to reduce medication errors in rural healthcare settings, spanning 2012 to 2025. It thematically maps interventions across stages of the medication process and highlights patient safety outcomes.

entry.title: SPSA Hyperparameter Tuning for Variational Quantum Natural Language Inference

author.name: Nayan D'Souza, Christopher J. Agostino

entry.summary: An empirical hyperparameter sweep comparing SPSA gradient estimation against exact parameter-shift gradients for a small variational quantum classifier on natural language inference. The best SPSA configuration reached roughly chance-level-plus accuracy with wide error bars on a 6-qubit, 60-parameter model.

entry.title: A Configurable Privacy-Preserving MRI Processing Workflow Using Deep Learning-Based Brain Extraction and Adaptive Anatomical Preservation

author.name: Rayeef Ali Khan, Komal Raj Mahantesh

entry.summary: Describes a configurable MRI defacing workflow that combines SynthStrip brain extraction with morphological operations so users can trade off privacy protection against retention of anatomy needed for specific analyses, plus interactive selection and quality control. Aimed at neuroimaging data sharing under privacy constraints. Engineering-oriented rather than algorithmically novel.

entry.title: Optic Disc Segmentation in Fundus Images: From Classical Image Processing and Deformable Models to Modern AI

author.name: Buket D. Barkana

entry.summary: Structured methodological review of optic disc segmentation in fundus images, from thresholding, deformable models, and vessel-based heuristics to modern deep learning, with a survey of commonly used datasets and remaining challenges from illumination, pathology, and boundary ambiguity. Aimed at glaucoma assessment pipelines. Historical and organizational rather than novel.

entry.title: Reading List on Wise AI

author.name: Chris_Leong

entry.summary: A curated but self-described outdated reading list on wise AI and artificial wisdom, covering societal uplift, AI advisors, metacognition, and differential development of wisdom-related capabilities. It is a resource compilation rather than new argument.

entry.title: A Metamorphic Artificial Age Score Decision-Support Prototype for Flight-Log-Based Drone Propeller Health Monitoring

author.name: Seyma Yaman Kayadibi

entry.summary: Presents a fuzzy scoring prototype that fuses six flight-log health indicators into an artificial age score for detecting drone propeller degradation. It is evaluated on a public 2024 drone propeller dataset using normalized deviations from a healthy baseline.

entry.title: MATS Winter 2027 Applications Are Now Open

author.name: Raj Thimmiah

entry.summary: Announcement that applications are open for the MATS Winter 2027 alignment research fellowship, a funded twelve-week program with mentors from Anthropic, Google DeepMind, OpenAI, Redwood and others. Details include stipend, compute budgets, locations, and the September 2026 deadline.

entry.title: Optimized Fuzzy Logic Approach with the IEEE Key Gas Method for Diagnosing Power Transformer Faults Using Dissolved Gas Analysis

author.name: Kim-Anh Nguyen, Huy Hoang Le, Ba Tu Phung

entry.summary: Combines fuzzy logic with the IEEE Key Gas Method for diagnosing power transformer faults from dissolved gas analysis, adding refined membership functions and separating carbon monoxide from carbon dioxide indicators. Validation on real-world datasets reports improved fault classification over the standard method.

entry.title: MicroPython and CircuitPython: Pythons Quiet Takeover of IoT and Robotics

author.name: Sayed Mahbub Hasan Amiri, Atiar Zahan

entry.summary: A mixed-methods survey of MicroPython and CircuitPython adoption in embedded systems, combining GitHub, Stack Overflow, and Google Trends analysis with curated maker case studies. Assesses ecosystem growth, performance trade-offs, and educational uptake against traditional C and C plus plus.

entry.title: Science and News Twitter/X Summarizer

author.name: sarahconstantin

entry.summary: A personal tool announcement for a digest site that clusters and summarizes science and world-news discussion from Twitter/X using API search, multilingual keyword translation, and Claude models for summarization and classification. It is an application build rather than research.

entry.title: Operationalizing Narrative Entropy (Sn): A Two-Scene Registered Pilot Report and Pre-Validation Protocol

author.name: Levent Bulut

entry.summary: A pilot report attempting to operationalize a proposed narrative entropy metric by having one rater manually score two literary scenes with a three-factor product formula. Reports that the result diverged from the author's intuition and lays out a pre-validation protocol.

entry.title: Why can’t we have nice things? Like, specifically?

author.name: Elizabeth

entry.summary: A detailed narrative of one activist's multi-year attempt to place a public memorial in a San Francisco park, used to illustrate concretely how permitting and institutional friction blocks small civic projects. It is reported anecdote rather than analysis of AI.

entry.title: Enforcement Begins: the EU AI Act and Systemic Risks

author.name: Schizoid Rentoid

entry.summary: A short event notice for a discussion on EU AI Act enforcement powers and systemic risks such as cyber capability, manipulation, and loss of control, featuring a Future of Life Institute policy lead. No substantive analysis is included in the post itself.

entry.title: Research Summary: August 19, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
The day's standout result is algorithmic discovery: AlphaEvolve plus modern optimization pushes the matrix multiplication exponent below 2.371177, a verifiable improvement on a headline open problem in theoretical CS.

  • World models and control: Hydra-0 unifies robot policies via action flow (actions as pixel motion), enabling cross-embodiment transfer; a Stanford team (Finn, Sadigh) reframes world models as off-policy Q-learning improvers rather than rollout generators.
  • Agents and harness engineering dominate volume (22 items): ClawGym II trains agents by black-box RL through opaque production harnesses; Write, Execute, Refine shows agent-authored skills hurt tool use by 8-11 points, motivating separate optimizer and executor roles.
  • Safety and security: Fool's Gold inverts open-weight defense by poisoning the payoff of abliteration instead of preventing it; a formal analysis of decomposition attacks shows stateful defenses fail under unlinkable identities.

Evaluation reform is a recurring theme (13 items). The IOL-AI Challenge supplies contamination-resistant linguistic reasoning tasks from unseen IOL 2026 problems with human grading; related work targets OV3D-Bench oracle leakage, TokEval tokenizer metrics, and clinical error-detection validity.

  • Foundations and interpretability: a proposed curse of ambiguity shows high-entropy next-token distributions are systematically harder to learn, with calibration implications; MIT CSAIL reports attribution decay, where scaling training data makes generated images untraceable to sources, carrying direct legal weight.
  • Generative modeling: Equilibrium Forcing removes noise-level conditioning from autoregressive video diffusion, decoupling denoising-field learning from sampling schedule.
  • Also notable: RelArena-α and TabPFN-Rel open relational multi-table learning, and a developmental study finds children, unlike language models, show accelerating returns per unit of linguistic input.
entry.content:
The day's standout result is algorithmic discovery: AlphaEvolve plus modern optimization pushes the matrix multiplication exponent below 2.371177, a verifiable improvement on a headline open problem in theoretical CS.

  • World models and control: Hydra-0 unifies robot policies via action flow (actions as pixel motion), enabling cross-embodiment transfer; a Stanford team (Finn, Sadigh) reframes world models as off-policy Q-learning improvers rather than rollout generators.
  • Agents and harness engineering dominate volume (22 items): ClawGym II trains agents by black-box RL through opaque production harnesses; Write, Execute, Refine shows agent-authored skills hurt tool use by 8-11 points, motivating separate optimizer and executor roles.
  • Safety and security: Fool's Gold inverts open-weight defense by poisoning the payoff of abliteration instead of preventing it; a formal analysis of decomposition attacks shows stateful defenses fail under unlinkable identities.

Evaluation reform is a recurring theme (13 items). The IOL-AI Challenge supplies contamination-resistant linguistic reasoning tasks from unseen IOL 2026 problems with human grading; related work targets OV3D-Bench oracle leakage, TokEval tokenizer metrics, and clinical error-detection validity.

  • Foundations and interpretability: a proposed curse of ambiguity shows high-entropy next-token distributions are systematically harder to learn, with calibration implications; MIT CSAIL reports attribution decay, where scaling training data makes generated images untraceable to sources, carrying direct legal weight.
  • Generative modeling: Equilibrium Forcing removes noise-level conditioning from autoregressive video diffusion, decoupling denoising-field learning from sampling schedule.
  • Also notable: RelArena-α and TabPFN-Rel open relational multi-table learning, and a developmental study finds children, unlike language models, show accelerating returns per unit of linguistic input.

entry.title: The IOL-AI Challenge: An Open Challenge towards Advancing Linguistic Reasoning
