entry.summary: The authors show that training-free AI-generated image detectors based on autoencoder reconstruction error can be broken by imperceptible adversarial perturbations that inflate reconstruction distance, making synthetic images look real. They introduce two attacks specifically exploiting this reconstruction-error mechanism.

entry.title: CytoFormer: A Molecularly Supervised Cell Foundation Model for Histopathology Cell Classification

author.name: Jialu Yao, Songhao Li, Alina Yu, Zhi Huang

entry.summary: CytoFormer trains a cell-level foundation model for histopathology using molecular supervision instead of pathologist annotations, pairing imaging-based spatial transcriptomics with H and E staining of the same physical section. The authors assembled 81 paired Xenium sections across 16 organs and derived per-cell type labels through clustering, marker genes, and expert review.

entry.title: ReForce: Learning Force-aware Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation

author.name: Yuhang Wu, Lingqi Zeng, Changwei Jing, Jianglong Ye, Xiaolong Wang

entry.summary: ReForce makes human-to-robot demonstration retargeting force-aware rather than purely kinematic, predicting a residual on the kinematically retargeted action so the intended contact force is reproduced. A general force tracker trained on large-scale simulated interactions supports both online teleoperation and offline translation of demonstration data.

entry.title: Learn What's Left, Not What's Mastered: Saturation Aware Advantage Reweighting for Multi-Reward Policy Optimization

author.name: Yixuan Wang, Yifei Chen, Haichao Zhang, Haozheng Luo, Xander Wu, Jie Ni, Yun Fu, Nuno Vasconcelos, Yijiang Li

entry.summary: This paper argues that scalarizing multiple rewards before group-relative standardization in RL post-training causes distinct rollouts to receive identical advantages and wastes gradient budget on already-saturated objectives. The proposed saturation-aware advantage reweighting adapts objective weights to remaining headroom, targeting unmastered skills during multi-reward policy optimization.

entry.title: CompoSkill: Compositional Skill Chain Attacks from Individually Scanner-Passing LLM Agent Skills

author.name: Mingxiao Liu, Zhoumian Jiang, Jianan Ma, Jian Zhang, Jialuo Chen, Xinhao Deng, Zhen Wang

entry.summary: CompoSkill shows that agent marketplace skills certified individually by scanners can combine into harmful chains, because composition risk is a path-level rather than node-level property. The framework constructs such chains from individually passing skills and demonstrates that per-package scanning intercepts only a small fraction of them.

entry.title: When State Becomes an Attack Surface: State-Semantic Injection in LLM-Driven Embodied Agents

author.name: Jiawei Liu, Jiacheng Guo, Tian Zhang, Yiwei Xu, Juan Wang, Jinlin Fan, Bowen Xiao, Chi Guo, Keyan Guo, Hongxin Hu

entry.summary: Introduces state-semantic injection, an attack surface in LLM-driven embodied agents where manipulated environment or agent state semantics rather than direct prompts steer high-level planning and robot action selection. The work argues that as language models take over task understanding and behavioral decision-making in robotic stacks, persistent state becomes an exploitable channel.

entry.title: HAF: Adapting Generalist VLAs to Humanoid Whole-Body Loco-manipulation via Hierarchical Action Flow and Spectral Latent RL

author.name: Langzhe Gu, Chengkai Hou, Meng Li, Xinhua Wang, Jiaming Liu, Xinyuan Lv, Bowei Zhang, Shuanghao Bai, Guangrun Li, Jingyang He, Gaole Dai, Ziluo Ding, Zhiyuan Xu, Kuan Cheng, Jian Tang, Zhengping Che, Shanghang Zhang

entry.summary: HAF adapts generalist vision-language-action models to humanoid whole-body loco-manipulation using a hierarchical action flow that separates coordination of locomotion, waist posture, and dual-arm manipulation, plus spectral latent reinforcement learning that refines behavior without fine-tuning the full VLA backbone. The goal is to overcome the suboptimality of offline behavior cloning while avoiding costly and unsafe real-robot tuning of large models.

entry.title: Rethinking Reverse KL as Adaptive Entropy Distillation

author.name: Shizhen Li, Zhiyu Shen, Yuyin Lu, Yunhe Pang, Jielin Song, Yanghui Rao, Fu Lee Wang

entry.summary: Revisits on-policy reverse KL distillation for LLMs by decomposing its objective into a teacher-fitting term and a student-entropy term, showing that the token-level optimal student is a tempered version of the teacher with an adaptive weight controlling imitation strength. The claim is that reverse KL already provides the mechanism usually sought by mixing forward and reverse KL branches.

entry.title: CoM$^3$eT: A foundation model for medical image analysis through federated, multidimensional context integration

author.name: J. Raphael Sch\"afer, Kai Geissler, Till Nicke, Chiara Tappermann, Karoline Heber, Eike Petersen, Habib Mergan, Lars Ole Schwen, Nick Weiss, Annika Gerken, Jan Hendrik Moltz, Tom Bisson, Isil Dogan O, Tim-Rasmus Kiehl, Norman Zerbe, Sefer Elezkurtaj, Robin S. Mayer, Nadine Flinner, Peter Wild, Isabel Dahm, Felix Peisen, Heinrich von Busch, Robert Grimm, Sebastian Arndt, Lisa Siegler, Matthias Stefan May, Antje Prasse, Natalia Artysh, Fabian Kiessling, Johannes Lotz

entry.summary: CoM3eT is a medical vision foundation model trained in a federated setting that unifies pathology and radiology, sparse classification and dense segmentation outputs, and two- plus higher-dimensional inputs through multidimensional context attention. It reportedly outperformed other medical foundation models across twelve datasets in an open competition.

entry.title: The Working Set of a Coding Agent: Coherence Debt in Repository-Scale Tasks

author.name: Bardia Mohammadi, Lars Klein, Aman Chadha, Akhil Arora, Laurent Bindschaedler

entry.summary: Models repository-scale coding as reconstructing a coupled-fact graph and defines coherence debt as the facts covered by neither the context window nor parametric memory. By systematically supplying, withholding, and corrupting each channel across seven models and five agent harnesses, it shows that no model succeeds on unseen APIs with both channels empty, that in-prompt facts restore success, and that all models fail identically when a rename contradicts memorized library knowledge.

entry.title: Regime-Conditional Verification: Correctness Estimation for Adapting and Monitoring Safety Classifiers

author.name: Thiago Sandoval, Ufuk Topcu

entry.summary: A lightweight wrapper that adapts an off-the-shelf safety classifier to a deployer's own policy without retraining, by estimating from internal representations the probability that a prediction disagrees with the desired policy and selectively correcting it. The same estimates double as a label-free distribution-shift detector for ongoing monitoring.

entry.title: Braided Vision Transformer for Stroke Detection in Multi-view Retinal Fundus Imaging

author.name: Aysen Degerli, Mika Hilvo

entry.summary: A benchmark that reframes video understanding as multi-turn, tool-augmented agentic interaction, motivated by leading models already reaching roughly 90 percent on saturated single-turn video QA leaderboards. Models must iteratively perceive, call tools, and gather evidence to answer.

entry.title: PixRestore: Unified Image Restoration via Pixel Diffusion Transformer

author.name: Lingchen Sun, Rongyuan Wu, Xiangtao Kong, Jixin Zhao, Qiaosi Yi, Yujing Sun, Shuaizheng Liu, Zhengqiang Zhang, Lei Zhang

entry.summary: PixRestore is a VAE-free pixel-space diffusion transformer for unified image restoration, trained from scratch with flow matching on patchified pixels instead of adapting a latent text-to-image model. This avoids the detail loss from latent autoencoders and the content-inconsistent artifacts introduced by open-ended synthesis priors.

entry.title: Imagining Recovery: Inference-Time Counterfactual Realignment for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Yanyan Zhang, Disheng Liu, Kai Ye, Chaoda Song, Xinpeng Li, Mohsen Hariri, Vikash Singh, Yu Yin, Vipin Chaudhary

entry.summary: CoRe recovers a frozen vision-language-action policy at inference time after disruptions such as goal, scene, or robot-state changes, without failure data or retraining. On detecting deviation it imagines how the policy would proceed from a recent viable state using synthesized observations, then minimally realigns the robot rather than physically retrying.

entry.title: StructRL: Structured Action-Space Exploration for Flow-Based VLAs

author.name: Jiarui Yang, Bin Zhu, Jingjing Chen, Na Zou, Yanwei Fu, Jianggang Zhu, Yu-Gang Jiang

entry.summary: StructRL argues that online reinforcement learning for flow-based vision-language-action policies needs temporally smooth, group-scaled exploration noise rather than isotropic noise, and identifies structured noise dilution where noise injected mid-denoising is washed out by remaining steps. It proposes a way to preserve structured exploration through to executed actions.

entry.title: Contact Modes Are Strata: What Geometric Structure Buys in Discrete-Continuous Planning

author.name: Phone Thiha Kyaw, Jonathan Kelly

entry.summary: This work observes that contact modes in manipulation literally are strata of configuration space, so planning becomes a walk over strata with geodesic segments within each. On pushing a T-block around obstacles and in-hand cube reorientation, the planner returns solutions in seconds without prescribed mode or contact sequences.

entry.title: Tactile Sim2Real without Tactile Simulation via Bottlenecked Latent Reconstruction

author.name: Fan Yang, Youngsun Wi, Jinhao Yu, Nima Fazeli, Dmitry Berenson

entry.summary: SBLR trains manipulation policies on a generic simulator-native oracle tactile signal (point cloud plus fingertip forces) and then aligns real tactile sensor embeddings to that oracle latent space at deployment, avoiding the need to simulate any specific tactile sensor. This sidesteps a major bottleneck given how fast and how diverse tactile hardware designs are.

entry.title: SurgVIL: Scaling Surgical Robot Imitation Learning with Open-source Surgical Videos

author.name: Xinhao Chen, JuoTung Chen, Nigel Nelson, Antony Goldenberg, Jesse Haworth, Sean D. Huver, Axel Krieger

entry.summary: SurgVIL scales surgical robot imitation learning by mixing kinematically labeled phantom demonstrations with unlabeled open-source and web surgical videos, estimating approximate action labels for the latter. This targets the severe scarcity of paired video-action data in realistic tissue settings.

entry.title: Discovering High-Quality Chess Puzzles with Offline Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Allen Nie, Anirudhan Badrinath, Nicholas Tomlin, Timothy Dai, Carissa Yip, Rose E Wang, Emma Brunskill, Chris Piech

entry.summary: Uses offline reinforcement learning to discover high-quality chess puzzles that balance tactical motifs and required look-ahead depth, addressing the difficulty of producing pedagogically useful practice material at scale. The team includes machine learning researchers, education researchers, and a chess grandmaster-level player for expert judgment.

entry.title: Measuring Reward Hacking and Reasoning-Answer Decoupling Under Position-Confounded Optimization

author.name: Suyash Maniyar, Armaan Sandhu, Abhishek Mishra

entry.summary: Trains language models with GRPO on multiple-choice math where the correct answer is always the same option, then evaluates on unbiased positions to measure how much a benchmark score reflects task skill versus exploitation of a confounded but technically correct reward. Across Qwen, Llama and Gemma models, biased training frequently produces reasoning that is decoupled from the emitted answer.

entry.title: The Value of a Prompt: An LLM-Relative Kolmogorov-Complexity Approach

author.name: Rafael Pass

entry.summary: This paper proposes measuring the economic value of a prompt, hint, or partial solution via a Levin-Kolmogorov style complexity relative to a fixed LLM: an input is valuable to the extent that it raises the sampling probability of the target artifact or reduces the thinking time needed to find it. It gives a computational definition rather than a heuristic score. The framing matters for attributing credit and value in human-plus-model production.

entry.title: JailbreakSkill: Scaling Automated Red-Teaming with Reusable and Ever-Evolving Skills

author.name: Xiaoyu Wen, Jiajia Li, Zhida He, Peng Yu, Chenxu Wang, Han Qi, Ziyuan Zhou, Cheng Jin, Ying Wen, Xingcheng Xu, Shuyue Hu, Tianhang Zheng, Chaochao Lu, Qiaosheng Zhang

entry.summary: JailbreakSkill packages known jailbreak strategies as modular, agent-selectable skills and closes the loop by using attack experience to refine, combine, and discover new skills that are added to a growing library. The goal is scalable automated red-teaming that accumulates capability instead of scattering one-off prompts. It also raises dual-use concerns since the library keeps improving.

entry.title: Reconstruction: A Blind Benchmark for Recovering Research Ideas from Pre-Publication Bibliographies

author.name: Shaolong Chen, Yanlin Fei, Nazhou Liu, Xinmiao Yu, Lei Li, Rahul Thapa, Madalina Ciobanu, Qingqing Mao, Ritankar Das

entry.summary: Reconstruction asks models to recover a published paper's core research idea given only its pre-publication bibliography, with strict anti-leakage controls including temporal citation cutoffs and anonymized reference identifiers, judged by an independent model against the held-out ground truth. Across six domains and 643 papers, seven frontier models match the real idea only roughly 3 to 15 percent of the time. It provides a contamination-resistant measure of scientific ideation.

entry.title: Stop Indexing at Full Precision: Revisiting Clustering for Vector Embeddings

author.name: Leonardo Kuffo, Peter Boncz

entry.summary: Shows that vector-search indexing pipelines do not need full-precision vectors for the clustering step: applying dimensionality reduction, quantization, and dimension pruning before clustering yields centroids within about 1 percent of ideal quality even with 1-bit codes. Reported gains include roughly 60x storage reduction plus faster clustering, with open-sourced code.

entry.title: Workspace Topology as an Attack Vector in Agentic Coding Assistants

author.name: Alexandre G. R. Day, Pradeep Yadlapalli, Sriram Venkatapathy, Thomas Paniagua, Nick Raines, Sahil Wadhwa, Himanshu Kumar, Andy Luo, Sudeep Panyam, Rikhiya Ghosh, Pranab Mohanty, Giri Iyengar

entry.summary: Introduces workspace topology as an attack surface for agentic coding assistants, showing that directory depth, codebase modularity, in-file injection position, and context framing all measurably change indirect prompt injection success. The empirical study covers open-source repositories across ten languages and six engineering domains.

entry.title: From LLM Inference to Agentic Workloads: Characterization and Implications for Serving Systems

author.name: Chaokun Chang, Yukun Zhou, Kaihua Fu, Dakai An, Tianyu Feng, Hanfeng Lu, Sheng Yao, Pu Guo, Yinghao Yu, Yizhou Shan, Bo Li, Binhang Yuan, Wei Wang

entry.summary: AgentSysBench characterizes how agentic workloads differ from conventional LLM serving, using ten representative applications with unified systems instrumentation across controlled deployments and production traces. It identifies six distinguishing properties, including heavyweight stateful execution where non-LLM components dominate latency, with implications for how serving systems should be designed.

entry.title: No Task Fails Every Time: Why One-Shot Audits Are Structurally Blind to Agent Damage

author.name: Shiven Khurdi

entry.summary: Presents an environment-agnostic reliability benchmark that measures severity-weighted damage from agent actions using database state differences rather than model-based judging, run across thousands of trials and nine models. The headline finding is that damaging behavior on irreversible actions is stochastic, so single-run audits systematically miss harms that repeated runs reveal.

entry.title: PertMind: Eliciting Emergent Biological Reasoning in LLM via Reinforcement Learning on Cellular Perturbation Data

author.name: Zhenchao Tang, Xiaogang Xu, Tianxu Lv, Jiahui Guan, Jiale Zhou, Haohuai He, Zhi Song, Hanbo Huang, Jiehui Huang, Jiafei Wu, Zhe Liu

entry.summary: PertMind turns cellular perturbation atlases into reinforcement learning environments, using measured gene responses as computable rewards for biological reasoning after a trusted-trajectory supervised warm start. Trained only on forward perturbation-response prediction, it transferred without task-specific tuning to reverse perturbation identification and combinatorial settings while retaining general language ability.

entry.title: Neurosymbolic Embodied Agents

author.name: Mohammad Albinhassan, Yuming Feng, Alessandra Russo, Pranava Madhyastha

entry.summary: Presents a neurosymbolic embodied agent that splits long-horizon household tasks into VLM-driven exploration that grounds symbolic predicates, followed by constrained symbolic planning where a PDDL transition model restricts token decoding to applicable actions and MCTS scores executable continuations. The design targets the executability gap where language-model plans violate environment dynamics or misground objects.

entry.title: DUET: Dual-Teacher On-Policy Distillation via Same-Weight Disagreement for Prohibition Compliance

author.name: Zihan Li, Feifei Li, Wenhui Que

entry.summary: DUET performs token-selective on-policy distillation for compliance with runtime-injected prohibitions by pairing a teacher that sees the prohibition with an identical-weight teacher that does not, so their per-token disagreement isolates the causal effect of the constraint. This gives a supervision signal that avoids the label dilution of SFT and the sequence-level mismatch of DPO for token-localized violations.

entry.title: Learning reshapes power-law anisotropy in internal representations

author.name: Asahi Nakamuta, Jun-nosuke Teramae

entry.summary: Exactly solves the learning dynamics of a wide two-layer linear network in a teacher-student setup with power-law input and teacher spectra to explain how the power-law anisotropy observed in both language model representations and cortical activity emerges. In the feature-learning regime the local exponent of the internal representation spectrum is reshaped by task structure rather than inherited from the input.

entry.title: Do Language Models Consistently Encode the Current Year?

author.name: Suze van Adrichem, Aditi Bhaskar, Diyi Yang, Christopher Potts, Jing Huang

entry.summary: Introduces two probes of how language models represent the present time, an associative task inferring the current year from verb tense and a declarative task querying it directly, and finds both land within a year of the post-training cutoff for instruction-tuned models. For base models the associative task predicts the pretraining cutoff within about ten months on average across thirteen models, yet mechanistic analysis shows the two tasks engage divergent internal circuitry.

entry.title: Crystal-structure design by agentic AI in a language of motifs

author.name: Dinh-Khiet Le, Minh-Quyet Ha, Hong-Phuc Vu-Dinh, Takashi Miyake, Hiori Kino, Hieu-Chi Dam

entry.summary: MatEvolve is an agentic AI system that designs crystal structures by reasoning in an interpretable vocabulary of recurring geometric motifs, editing a motif profile and rebuilding candidate crystals from it. Promising candidates are validated with first-principles calculations, targeting rare-earth-lean magnetic materials.

entry.title: Think in Latent, Explain in Language: Self-Explainable Latent Reasoning

author.name: Dayuan Zhao, Shengcao Cao, Yu-Xiong Wang, Liang-Yan Gui

entry.summary: Proposes a framework where a model reasons in compressed latent embeddings but can explain those latent steps in language within the same model, avoiding both opaque latent reasoning and separate post-hoc decoders. Aims to keep the efficiency of latent chain-of-thought while restoring human-readable traces tied to the actual computation.

entry.title: Agentic Transaction: Towards ACID-Compliant Agent Systems

author.name: Zhaoyan Sun, Xiaoxiao Wang, Guoliang Li

entry.summary: Proposes reinterpreting database ACID guarantees for LLM agents operating over persistent environments, defining semantic atomicity, consistency, isolation, and durability for multi-step agent workflows. It offers a framework for reliable rollback, safe concurrency, and durable state in agentic systems.

entry.title: Anchor-Regularized Adaptation for Generalizable AI-Generated Image Detection with DINOv3

author.name: Hyeongjun Choi, Juhun Lee, Davide Cozzolino, Luisa Verdoliva, Simon S. Woo

entry.summary: Analyzes why linear probes on frozen DINOv3 features generalize well for AI-generated image detection even with misaligned training data, and shows the final layer underuses subtle pixel-artifact cues. The proposed anchor-regularized adaptation preserves the frozen model's authentic-image representation while adding artifact sensitivity.

entry.title: Unlocking the Potential of Image Editing via Concept Scaling and Dense Supervision

author.name: Long Cui, Xiaoqian Liu, Qi Qin, Yi Xin, Tao Lin, Jianguo Li, Linfeng Zhang

entry.summary: This paper argues image editing suffers from coarse edit-concept granularity and sparse supervision, and responds with a taxonomy of over 1,000 fine-grained edit concepts, a 12-million-pair synthetic dataset, and a dense supervision objective. The library-driven synthesis is designed to prevent distribution collapse in generated training data.

entry.title: Degenerate in Whose Frame? An Equivariance Condition for Degeneracy Detection in LiDAR Registration

author.name: Yujie Zhang, Chunlei Zhao, Yuzong Lin, Yuxuan Guo, Xiaohui Jia, Jinyue Liu

entry.summary: This paper shows that common per-axis degeneracy labels in LiDAR registration are not intrinsic scene properties, because the point-to-plane information matrix transforms by congruence rather than similarity under body-frame changes. It derives an equivariance condition under which a generalized eigenvalue criterion becomes frame-independent, and demonstrates that shifting the origin one metre changes which degrees of freedom are flagged.

entry.title: RoboStriker: Latent-Space Strategic Games for Autonomous Humanoid Boxing

author.name: Kangning Yin, Kaige Liu, Zhe Cao, Wentao Dong, Weishuai Zeng, Tianyi Zhang, Qiang Zhang, Jingbo Wang, Jiangmiao Pang, Yang Li, Ming Zhou, Weinan Zhang

entry.summary: RoboStriker formulates humanoid boxing as a two-player zero-sum Markov game played in a learned latent action space rather than raw joint space, with theory arguing the latent formulation preserves equilibrium structure while preventing physical collapse. It targets contact-rich, adversarial full-body agility.

entry.title: You Can't Iterate to Trustworthy AI Code Without Understanding

author.name: ronbodkin

entry.summary: An argument that iterating on outcomes of AI-generated code without human understanding of that code is insufficient for trustworthy automation, especially for safety research where undetected flaws could produce misleading safety cases. It pushes back on framing coding as a crisp, easily verified task and draws implications for how fast recursive self-improvement can safely proceed.

entry.title: Import AI 469: Science AI; RSI simulator; and Zuck's technological pessimism

author.name: Jack Clark

entry.summary: An issue of Jack Clark's newsletter covering DiG-bench, a suite of 70 hidden-rule games that test whether models can discover the laws and goals of an environment through interaction rather than being told them, alongside items on recursive self-improvement simulation and technological pessimism commentary. Existing frontier models including Anthropic's Fable line are discussed as evaluation subjects.

entry.title: HiPHI: A Large-Scale Benchmark for High-Precision Human Motion and Object-Interaction

author.name: Jiahao Ji, Ji Ma, Runhan Zhang, Runyi Yu, Wenjia Wang, Weiheng Chi, Qianqian Peng, Weichao Yan, Yongfei Gu, Ye Tian, Ting Wu, Longwei Li, Chun Yuan, Ruoli Dai, Lei Han

entry.summary: HiPHI is a 600-plus hour optical motion-capture dataset of whole-body human motion and object interactions, structured using a FrameNet-inspired taxonomy of human primitives to maximize coverage of the behavior manifold. It aims to fill the gap between imprecise internet video and narrow lab datasets for humanoid policy learning.

entry.title: UniDot: A Unified Network for Sequence Modeling and Feature Interaction in Large-scale Recommendation

author.name: Rongcheng Lin, Yan Sun, Jamey Zhang, Guanglei Xiong, Ivan Ji, Xianjie Chen, Shujian Bu

entry.summary: UniDot unifies feature-interaction and sequential-behavior modeling for industrial conversion prediction by observing that the embedding inner product in factorization machines is the same primitive as attention query-key scoring, allowing one dot-product tokenized network to serve both roles. It tokenizes non-sequential fields and multi-domain behavior histories in a single architecture for large-scale recommendation.

entry.title: Whose Gold? Annotator-Pool Disagreement Is Large at the Item Level, and Hidden by Small Leaderboards

author.name: Anik Jha

entry.summary: Measures how much the identity of annotator pools changes preference labels, finding that expert and crowd pools disagree on a fifth to a third of items where each pool is internally unanimous, yet the resulting model leaderboards are identical. Argues this rank invariance is much weaker evidence of robustness than it appears because small model panels hide large item-level disagreement.

entry.title: Wrong but Useful: Trajectory Value Beyond Answer Correctness in Multi-Agent Messages

author.name: Chih-Hsuan Yang, Anjir Ahmed Chowdhury, Cheng-Hau Yang, Weijian Zheng, Fernando Llorente, Xiaolong Ma, Xinyang Li, Eliu A. Huerta, Ian T. Foster, Rajeev Thakur

entry.summary: Measures the downstream value of individual messages in multi-agent reasoning by replaying the same solver with each message shown or hidden, decoupling message correctness from usefulness. It finds that wrong messages can still carry decompositions and constraints that improve final answers, undermining correctness-based filtering.

entry.title: Zetta $\zeta$: An Efficient Closed-Loop Embodied Harness for Self-Evolving Physical Intelligence

author.name: Xin Ding, Liang Mi, Mingzhe Huang, Zixuan Wang, Chao Zhang, Zixu Hao, Fu Chen, Xiangyu Li, Yikai Zheng, Yaoyu Guo, Weijun Wang, Kun Li, Hao Wu, Yunxin Liu, Ting Cao

entry.summary: Zetta is an agent harness that keeps a base robot policy frozen while online-evolving code-based runtime critics and recovery skills across three loops operating at different timescales, so that failures are caught during execution rather than only after an episode ends. It targets the open-loop limitation of current embodied agent scaffolds.

entry.title: Divergent-Convergent Reasoning: Scaling Test-Time Compute through Structured Solution Synthesis

author.name: Bo Wen, Yuhao Chen, Erhan Bilal, Carla Agurto Rios, Chen Wang, Junchen Jiang

entry.summary: Studies a two-phase test-time compute primitive that first generates diverse candidate solutions and then reconciles them, showing a single reconciliation step can recover correct answers that are in the minority where majority voting fails. It also introduces a recursive variant that iteratively analyzes disagreements among candidates.

entry.title: Whose doctor does the AI recommend? An algorithm audit of reputation and demographic signals in large language model-assisted physician choice

author.name: Syeda Anshrah Gillani, Mirza Samad Ahmed Baig

entry.summary: A prespecified randomized audit of how seven models choose among synthetic physician profiles, varying reputation signals plus gender and ethnicity cues across more than 40,000 scored responses. It quantifies what actually drives model recommendations when assistants act as intermediaries in real-world choices.

entry.title: PersonaShot: Benchmarking Person-Centric Narrative Continuity in Multi-Shot Video Generation

author.name: Yuji Wang, Yuheng Chen, Teng Hu, Ran Yi, Yijia Hong, Han Feng, Weijian Cao, Chengjie Wang, Lizhuang Ma, Jiangning Zhang

entry.summary: PersonaShot is a benchmark of about 1,000 multi-shot video segments with 16 metrics for evaluating whether a human character stays physically and emotionally coherent across shot cuts. It provides criterion-specific evaluation for physical continuity, facial dynamics, and cinematic relations rather than a single aggregate score.

entry.title: VicEdit: Learning to Edit Videos from Visual In-Context Examples

author.name: Yuji Wang, Teng Hu, Yuheng Chen, Ran Yi, Han Feng, Weijian Cao, Chengjie Wang, Lizhuang Ma, Jiangning Zhang

entry.summary: VicEdit proposes visual in-context video editing, replacing text-only instructions with multimodal guidance from a single image, an image pair, or a video pair, and releases VicEdit-400K covering ten task types. A unified model is trained on this automatically generated and filtered dataset.

entry.title: A Control-Theoretic Formulation of Global Workspace Theory

author.name: Ryota Kanai

entry.summary: This paper gives a control-theoretic formalization of global workspace theory, proposing that a global workspace is a mediating subnetwork identifiable via reachability, observability, and internal transformation modes. The Global Mediation Workspace criterion is intended to supply a formal test for which subnetwork actually enables conscious access.

entry.title: MISTac: A Vision-Based Tactile Sensor for Minimally Invasive Surgery

author.name: Robin Koch, Annabella Mascot, Rayan Younis, Martin Wagner, Stefanie Speidel, Mark Cutkosky, Ingo Sieber, Roberto Calandra

entry.summary: MISTac is a high-resolution vision-based tactile sensor with an 8 mm replaceable tip that fits through surgical trocars, restoring palpation feedback lost in minimally invasive and robot-assisted surgery. Its modular 3D-printed housing allows off-the-shelf illumination and imaging hardware, achieving optical resolution near 177 micrometres.

entry.title: ViTaR: Visuo-Tactile Residual Adaptation for Foundation VLA Manipulation

author.name: Yi Wang, Renjun Wu, Jinyan Liu, Xuesong Li

entry.summary: ViTaR adds tactile feedback to frozen foundation vision-language-action policies not as a perceptual input that generates actions but as an execution modulator that selects and scales bounded residual corrections. The design avoids modifying VLA internals, which risks catastrophic forgetting, and avoids online reinforcement under near-failure contact.

entry.title: Learning Agent Execution for KV-Cache Management in Agentic Serving

author.name: Rui Zhang, Chaeeun Kim, Shaoting Feng, Kuntai Du, Yuhan Liu, Yi Zhong, Cheng-Wei Ching, Junchen Jiang, Liting Hu

entry.summary: CacheScout is an agent-aware KV-cache runtime for multi-agent LLM serving that exploits the fact that each agent repeatedly replays a fixed context of system prompts, tool definitions, and few-shot examples. Instead of reactive prefix caching with recency eviction, it predicts future reuse from agent execution structure to keep the right contexts resident.

entry.title: Auditing an AI-Generated Mathematical Proof: A Correction to a Greedy Conditioning Lemma in Quantum Parallel Repetition

author.name: Miko{\l}aj Sienicki, Krzysztof Sienicki

entry.summary: Audits a chapter of an OpenAI-published compilation on AI-assisted mathematical advances that claims an exponential parallel-repetition theorem for entangled two-player games. The authors find a polarity error in the greedy conditioning lemma proof, where a test stated in terms of average success does not deliver the needed high conditional failure probability, and supply a correction.

entry.title: Evo-Harness: Context-to-Harness Skill Compilation for Self-Evolving Agents

author.name: Tianxin Wei, Zhan Shi, Minhua Lin, Bing He, Zewen Liu, Yisi Sang, Yuanchen Bei, Xuying Ning, Jiaru Zou, Ting-Wei Li, Xiao Lin, Yanjun Zhao, Chi Wang, Benoit Dumoulin, Dakuo Wang, Jingrui He, Hanqing Lu

entry.summary: Evo-Harness formulates online harness learning, where a frozen agent improves by continually updating a structured harness compiled from noisy one-shot execution contexts rather than by updating weights. The work emphasizes separating broadly useful lessons from task-specific artifacts and validating on complex realistic tasks, which prior experience-learning methods often skip.

entry.title: VibeWorlding: Can Multimodal Agents Construct 3D Open Worlds End-to-End?

author.name: Yansong Ning, Jingwen Ye, Zhongkai Wu, Yang Sun, Yiqin Zhu, Xingyi Li, Weidong Zhang, Hao Liu

entry.summary: VibeWorlding benchmarks and trains multimodal agents that build interactive 3D open worlds from realistic user queries, requiring intent inference, layout planning, 3D tool use and reflection on visual feedback. It ships a benchmark of thousands of assets and hundreds of human-annotated seed worlds plus a training pipeline.

entry.title: Does the Proof Prove It That Way? Faithful Formalization of Elements Proofs

author.name: Tadd Mao, Tianjun Zhong, Dhruva Arekar, Yuming Feng, One An, Jiani Huang, Xujie Si, Ziyang Li

entry.summary: Defines five necessary conditions for a formal proof to faithfully reflect the reasoning of a natural-language argument, rather than merely compiling to the same conclusion, and applies them to formalizing Euclid-style geometry proofs. Faithful formalization would let systems check the reasoning in human or AI-written arguments.

entry.title: TRACE: Trajectory Aware Reasoning for Multi-Turn Adversarial Conversation Evaluation

author.name: Md Messal Monem Miah, Adrita Anika, Zhiyuan Yu, Ruihong Huang

entry.summary: TRACE defends against multi-turn jailbreaks by having the model reason over the whole conversation trajectory before each reply, identifying manipulation cues, weighing benign and adversarial readings of intent, scoring jailbreak likelihood and choosing to allow, caution or decline. It is trained on thousands of curated multi-turn adversarial conversations to reduce over-refusal on benign sensitive topics.

entry.title: Governance at the Boundary: How Agent Decomposition Degrades Policy Compliance

author.name: Bowen Li, Guojun Wang

entry.summary: Fiducia-bench evaluates whether financial agents act within policy (escalating, abstaining, and leaving audit trails) rather than merely completing tasks, across KYC and anti-money-laundering scenarios. The central result is that decomposing an agent into multiple components degrades governance because policy-relevant facts discovered by one component are lost or weakened at handoff boundaries. This identifies a concrete architectural mechanism for compliance failure in multi-agent deployments.

entry.title: BaT: Towards Self-Evolving Medical Research Agent with Stage Rubrics

author.name: Junqi Liu, Yufan He, Yexiao He, Pengfei Guo, Dong Yang, Andriy Myronenko, Can Zhao, Hanrong Ye, Tianhao Qi, Yuyin Zhou, Daguang Xu, Yucheng Tang

entry.summary: Benchmark-as-Teacher turns stage-level benchmark diagnostics into training signal for a self-improving medical imaging research agent, pairing an asynchronous data pipeline that synthesizes content-isolated training states with a bilevel curriculum reinforcement learning method. The motivation is that standard post-training throws away the fine-grained failure localization that structured benchmarks provide. It targets long-horizon, data-sensitive scientific workflows.

entry.title: Plausible but Not Valid: A Psychometric Audit of LLMs as Synthetic Survey Respondents

author.name: Mantas Lukauskas, Viktorija \v{S}arkauskait\.e

entry.summary: This psychometric audit asks not whether synthetic survey answers look plausible but whether 37 models across proprietary and open-weight families reproduce the joint distribution, latent factor structure, reliability, mediation pathways, and demographic effects of a real organizational psychology dataset. Personas are disclosed at five levels with presentation, reasoning-effort, and counterfactual ablations. The headline is that outputs are plausible but psychometrically invalid.

entry.title: DumpsterCluster: From Dumpster Diving to Serving LLaMA-70B on $60 GPUs

author.name: Zeyu Cao, Xuan Guo, Cheng Zhang, Cheuk Hang Lau, Ilia Shumailov, Yiren Zhao

entry.summary: The authors physically built a 128-GPU cluster entirely from retired second-hand accelerators and ran it for a year, reporting that pipeline-parallel optimizations let older-generation cards deliver competitive throughput for serving a 70-billion-parameter model at roughly one thirtieth the capital cost of a current-generation eight-GPU system. They also examine when such repurposing is environmentally sensible. It challenges assumptions that retired accelerators are useless for modern inference.

entry.title: Automatic or Controlled? Repetition Priming Reveals Divergent Processing in Base LLMs, Instruct LLMs, and Humans

author.name: Jinglei Ren, Yuyue Wang

entry.summary: Uses the classic repetition priming paradigm across 15 models from five families plus matched human experiments to ask whether models reactivate prior word representations or re-evaluate them. Base models show automatic, lag-stable facilitation correlated with attention to earlier occurrences, while instruction-tuned models show controlled, decaying processing more like a deliberate strategy.

entry.title: Evaluating Agentic Code Repair Capabilities in Distributed Systems

author.name: Yibo Yan, Huijuan Wang, Junzhou He, Yizhuo Liang, Shaoyu Wang, Huanchen Sun, Seo Jin Park

entry.summary: DDBench is a code-repair benchmark of 60 historical bugs mined from 13 open-source distributed systems, where root causes span processes, nodes, and protocol interactions and are rarely visible in source alone. It also runs a controlled study of how much externally supplied debugging context, such as traces and logs, changes agent success rates.

entry.title: MAPLE: MoE Adaptive Plug-and-play Layer-wise Expert allocation

author.name: Lie Li, Wen Li, Junxiao Shen, Gusheng Hu

entry.summary: Shows that sparse mixture-of-experts models waste capacity by using the same routed-expert count at every layer, and derives a closed-form, sensitivity-guided reallocation of the expert budget across layers. The method is training-free and can be applied to pretrained MoE language models without touching weights.

entry.title: OceanLight: Efficient Global Ocean Forecasting via Geometry-Adaptive Unstructured Mesh Representation

author.name: Wei Wu, Xiang Wang, Hongze Leng, Qingye Min, Junxing Zhu, Junqiang Song

entry.summary: OceanLight is a global ocean forecasting model that replaces uniform structured grids with a geometry-adaptive unstructured mesh tokenization plus a graph neural network backbone, avoiding wasted computation on land cells and allocating resolution where flow is complex. The authors report pointwise accuracy and kinetic-energy spectral fidelity competitive with or better than existing baselines at lower cost.

entry.title: Step-Level On-Policy Distillation: Interpolating Between On-Policy Distillation and Supervised Fine-Tuning

author.name: Changhui Sun, Lanbo Liu, Hang Lei, Tong Ling, Jiahang Xie, Zhiyong Zheng, Yujia Wang, Hao Liu, Feng Xiao, Lu Liu, Yanlong Du, Zifeng Cheng, Ziwei Jiang, Qing Gu

entry.summary: Step-Level On-Policy Distillation supervises complete student-generated trajectories at step granularity, positioning itself as an interpolation between token-level on-policy distillation and supervised fine-tuning. The claim is that token-level corrections only patch fragments of a wrong trajectory while step-level supervision can unfold a full repair path.

entry.title: Semantic Bandits: In-Context Exploration-Exploitation is Biased by Semantic Priors

author.name: David Eric Austin, Kaheer Suleman, Jackie Chi Kit Cheung

entry.summary: The paper introduces the semantic bandit, a multi-armed bandit variant where actions carry textual labels with no formal role in the task structure, and shows that LLM agents' exploration is systematically biased by semantic priors learned in pretraining. This helps explain inconsistent findings about how LLMs balance exploration and exploitation.

entry.title: Historical Backtesting for Scientific Question Discovery: A Protocol and Astronomy Pilot

author.name: Hui Mao

entry.summary: Formalizes historical backtesting as a falsifiable evaluation protocol for systems that generate scientific research questions: questions are produced from a corpus frozen at a past cutoff, then a temporally isolated later corpus judges whether each question was answered, partially addressed, independently posed, or ignored, plus whether its premise held. The author releases reproducible astronomy instances and treats the protocol as model-agnostic.

entry.title: AutoSR: Automatic Symbolic Regression by Searching Research States

author.name: Kejia Zhang, Youran Sun, Xinyu Ren, Chugang Yi, Haizhao Yang

entry.summary: AutoSR reframes symbolic regression as a search over persistent research states rather than isolated equations, retaining motivations, probes, and prior findings so subsequent candidate expressions are informed by an accumulated scientific record. The motivation is that numerical fit and syntactic simplicity fail to distinguish expressions that extrapolate very differently outside the observed regime.

entry.title: Diagnosing and Mitigating Perception-Decision Misalignment in Omni-LLMs via Modality Subspace Activation

author.name: Hongbo Jiang, Jie Li, Yunhang Shen, Tianyu Xie, Pingyang Dai

entry.summary: Diagnoses perceptual-decision misalignment in omni-modal LLMs, where answers stay unfaithful to non-text perception, using a dual-lens framework of answer retention rate at the behavioral level and logit angular discrepancy at the distributional level, plus a curated benchmark that isolates language priors. Popular omni models show near-zero sensitivity even when key modality content is altered, and mitigation is attempted through modality subspace activation.

entry.title: Iterative Refinement Diffusion for Super-Resolved Data Assimilation of Multiscale Physical Systems

author.name: Mrigank Dhingra, Ramchandran Muthukumar, Rebecca Willett, Omer San

entry.summary: Iterative Refinement combines generative super-resolution with classical forecast-analysis data assimilation by decomposing state recovery into resolution-wise cycles rather than a single coarse-to-fine mapping, so temporal constraints from past states are exploited without repeated expensive high-resolution forecasts. It targets multiscale physical systems observed sparsely at low resolution.

entry.title: Every Expert Counts: ExactMoE for Memory-Efficient W4A16 Inference

author.name: Amjad Saab

entry.summary: ExactMoE quantizes only routed experts to symmetric group-128 four-bit weights stored in kernel-native MARLIN format in pinned host memory, streaming them through a GPU-resident slot cache with fused grouped MoE kernels while keeping router, attention, embeddings, norms, and the LM head in BF16. It preserves complete expert availability and unmodified top-k routing so no expert is pruned or substituted.

entry.title: Large Discovery Models: Empirically-grounded Model-Based Open-Ended Search

author.name: Zhongwei Yu, Yan Song, Xue Yan, Anjie Liu, Xingyu Lu, Yihang Chen, Huichi Zhou, Siyuan Guo, Luoyang Sun, Sihan Chen, Xiangning Yu, Jun Wang

entry.summary: Large Discovery Models couple a generative proposer (LLM-style prior over molecules, sequences, or programs) with a Bayesian nonparametric reward surrogate in a recurrent loop, so that calibrated uncertainty rather than model likelihood guides open-ended search. Targets expensive-to-evaluate scientific design objectives.

entry.title: Toward Optimal Second-Order Path-Length Guarantee for Adversarial Multi-Armed Bandits

author.name: Mengxiao Zhang

entry.summary: Resolves an open question of Bubeck et al. by proving that their existing adversarial bandit algorithm already achieves regret scaling with the square root of the second-order path length, not just the first-order one, via a more involved analysis. Provides bounds both with known and unknown path-length quantities.

entry.title: GEO-Flag: Detecting and Measuring GEO-Optimized Web Content

author.name: Junjie Chu, Ye Leng, Mingjie Li, Yun Shen, Xinyue Shen, Yang Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces GEOFlagBench, a benchmark of 3,200 webpages across 400 queries, plus detection methods for content that has been rewritten to be preferentially cited by generative search engines. Highlights that such optimization can give weak or false claims disproportionate visibility since answer synthesis hides source provenance.

entry.title: Belayer: Efficient Fault Tolerance for LLM Agentic RL Training

author.name: Jiecheng Zhou, Qinghao Hu, Peng Sun, Xingcheng Zhang, Weiming Zhang

entry.summary: Belayer is a fault-tolerance system for reinforcement learning on LLM agents, where long-horizon rollouts couple GPU inference engines with stateful sandbox containers whose side effects such as file edits and installed dependencies cannot be trivially replayed. It provides recovery mechanisms that keep completed trajectory work and avoid resuming into environment states inconsistent with the model context.

entry.title: Beyond Natural-Image Foundation Models: Benchmarking Satellite Pretraining for Ophthalmic Image Analysis

author.name: Lovre Antonio Budimir, Mingya Alexa Gong, Alyssa Foong Quinney, Ivana Matovinovi\'{c}, Yukun Zhou, Pearse A. Keane, Sven Lon\v{c}ari\'{c}, Marinko V. \v{S}aruni\'{c}

entry.summary: Tests the unusual idea of pretraining medical vision foundation models on satellite imagery instead of natural images, on the argument that texture and structure statistics may transfer better to ophthalmic scans than photographs of everyday scenes. It benchmarks this alternative pretraining domain for retinal image analysis.

entry.title: Spatially-Grounded Flow Matching: Structured Source Distributions for Image Generation

author.name: Arman Zarei, Mahdi M. Kalayeh

entry.summary: StructFlow argues that i.i.d. Gaussian source noise in flow matching fights the local-correlation inductive bias of images, letting models lean on less-noisy neighboring pixels instead of learning true local structure. It builds spatial locality directly into the source distribution and shows this changes what the model must learn during training.

entry.title: Concept-based explanation of gene expression prediction from H&E images

author.name: Amos Muench, Jonathan Thielmann, Reduan Achtibat, Maximilian Dreyer, Philip Bischoff, Caroline Forsythe, Hamidreza Parand, Thomas Walter, David Horst, Sebastian Lapuschkin, Wojciech Samek, Teresa Gabriela Krieger

entry.summary: This paper predicts spatial transcriptomics from routine H and E slides with a Vision Transformer and then explains it by combining layer-wise relevance propagation with sparse autoencoder concept discovery. The result links morphological concepts to transcriptional programs both locally and globally rather than only producing heatmaps.

entry.title: Underwater Color Restoration with Vanishing Uncertainty

author.name: Grigory Solomatov, Derya Akkaynak

entry.summary: This paper argues that underwater color restoration is currently validated only empirically and is mathematically ill-posed in full generality, so it examines which additional constraints actually pin the solution down to a finite uncertainty interval. The goal is restoration with quantifiable scientific confidence rather than benchmark-only credibility.

entry.title: PACE: Phase-Progress-Aware Credit for Long-Horizon Embodied Manipulation

author.name: Chengye Song, Jiawei Zhang, Rui Song, Shengqi Wang, Xiangrong Zhang, Ziyi Wang, Huanbin Zhou, Hongzhou Wang

entry.summary: PACE provides step-level credit assignment for post-training vision-language-action policies on long-horizon manipulation, where success is only revealed after hundreds of steps. Its phase-progress-aware critic combines global and local value correction using visual and motion-difference features to distinguish progress from stalling or regression.

entry.title: Vision-Based Tactile Intelligence for Robotics: Sensing, Learning, and Embodied Manipulation

author.name: Peng Zhou, Jun Hu, Sihan Chen, Zeqing Zhang, Haofei Ma, Zhenyu Lu, Sichao Liu, Xueqian Wang, Pai Zheng, Xiang Li, Shan Luo, Jia Pan, David Navarro-Alarcon, Chenguang Yang, Michael Yu Wang

entry.summary: A broad review of vision-based tactile sensors that treats hardware, learning methods, simulation, and datasets as one integrated system, organizing sensors into a taxonomy by deformable elastomer design. It is co-authored by a large group of established tactile and manipulation researchers.

entry.title: Making two action heads agree: coordination mechanisms and a runtime collapse certificate for flow-matching policies

author.name: Jinhui Sun, Wei Zhou, Bowen Yang, Xinliang Xiao, Li Yang

entry.summary: This paper studies dual-representation flow-matching policies that decode motion into both joint and end-effector space, where the residual between the two decodings gives an interpretable runtime health signal but produces false alarms when branches pick different valid modes. The authors categorize coordination mechanisms and prove that an auxiliary shared latent outside the flow construction is erased at the population optimum, while sharing source noise can help.

entry.title: Cyclops: LiDAR as a Camera That Dreams in Color

author.name: Wei Gao, Jian Shu, Mingle Zhao, Maani Ghaffari, David Kong, Chengzhong Xu, Hui Kong

entry.summary: Cyclops translates sparse non-repetitive-scanning LiDAR intensity returns into colorized RGB-like video so that standard RGB-pretrained vision models can run camera-free in darkness or extreme dynamic range. It effectively bridges the modality gap between LiDAR intensity and pretrained visual encoders.

entry.title: Exposing the Long-tail in Embodied Urban Navigation via Scalable Learning from In-the-Wild Videos

author.name: Bingyi Xia, Han Bao, Zhewei Chen, Hanjing Ye, Jingwen Yu, Yuhan Pang, Wenjun Xu, Jiankun Wang

entry.summary: Builds a pipeline that automatically annotates uncurated web egocentric videos with metric trajectories and navigation semantics, then trains a vision-language-action policy for point-goal urban navigation. The paper additionally characterizes the resulting long tail of rare, safety-critical scenarios and uses reflection-based analysis to interpret failures.

entry.title: Security of Foundation-Model-Powered Embodied Agents: Attack Surfaces, Attacks, Defenses, and Evaluation

author.name: Jiawei Liu, Jiacheng Guo, Tian Zhang, Yiwei Xu, Juan Wang, Jinlin Fan, Bowen Xiao

entry.summary: A survey of security risks in embodied agents driven by foundation models, organized by which trust boundary an adversary first crosses rather than by attack mechanism, spanning five system layers and twelve attack surfaces from the model supply chain to physical actuation. It also reviews defenses and evaluation practices.

entry.title: Fork Around and Find Out Part 3: Interpreting the knight auditor

author.name: dl27

entry.summary: The final installment of a mechanistic interpretability series on a single attention head in a chess transformer, reporting that earlier causal evidence supported a spurious reading of the head as a knight-fork detector. Purpose-built probes show it functions more as an auditor of knight moves that mainly suppresses pointless quiet knight moves.

entry.title: Bit-Flip Attacks on Vision-Language-Action Models: Action-Decoding Architecture Shapes the Vulnerability

author.name: Yudong Gao, Linghan Chen, Wenhan Wu, Mia Zhou, Jiyao Wang, Kaiyan Ji, Mingyu Guo, Honglong Chen

entry.summary: Demonstrates the first bit-flip attacks against quantized vision-language-action robot policies, showing that a handful of gradient-selected flips in weight memory can drive closed-loop task success to zero while random flips are harmless. The attack budget depends strongly on the action-decoding head, with flow-matching policies far more resistant than direct regression or token policies.

entry.title: Seeing Red, Thinking Bad: Color Bias in Vision Language Models

author.name: Kohsuke Ide, Ryousuke Yamada, Yoshihiro Fukuhara, Hirokatsu Kataoka, Yutaka Satoh

entry.summary: Introduces stealth visual prompts that change only the color and contrast styling of text rendered as an image, showing that vision-language models shift their judgments based on styling despite identical semantic content. The work also traces the effect into vision encoder representations.

entry.title: Registration-Free Hyperspectral Reconstruction from RGB via a Permutation-Invariant Gram-Matrix Principle

author.name: Jiangsan Zhao, Masayuki Hirafuji, Seishi Ninomiya, Jakob Geipel, Wei Guo

entry.summary: Learns hyperspectral reconstruction from RGB without requiring precise spatial registration or a known camera response function, by supervising on permutation-invariant Gram matrices of unmixed abundance maps. A prior state-of-the-art fusion method collapses under pixel permutation while this approach remains stable.

entry.title: Accelerating Mixed Discrete-Continuous Motion Planning via Neural Graphs of Convex Sets

author.name: Ananya Trivedi, Sarvesh Prajapati, Mohamed Khalid M Jaffar, Zhexin Xu, David Rosen, Taskin Padir

entry.summary: This paper accelerates Graphs of Convex Sets motion planning by replacing the expensive convex relaxation with a single forward pass of a graph attention network. The aim is to keep the framework's ability to couple discrete decisions with continuous trajectories while making online replanning tractable.

entry.title: GAINS: Leveraging Inconsistent Human Intervention Signals in Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Xinyi Zhang, Yinuo Zhao, Pei Ren, Lechun Jiang, Huiqian Jin, Lei Sun, Dapeng Wu, Zhengping Che, Chi Harold Liu, Jian Tang

entry.summary: GAINS makes reinforcement learning from human corrections robust to imperfect intervention timing, not just imperfect actions, since at high control frequencies human signals arrive late and inconsistently. It uses distributional RL with quantile Q-networks to model the return variability induced by sparse rewards and noisy intervention timing.

entry.title: MatchingPolicy: Correspondence-Aware Policy Enables Cross-Object In-Context Learning

author.name: Qijin She, Hanyang Yu, Zeming Li, Ping Tan

entry.summary: MatchingPolicy separates demonstration-to-scene correspondence estimation from action learning, conditioning a diffusion policy on dense semantic correspondences derived from vision foundation models with a two-stage matching algorithm. The decoupling is argued to enable in-context imitation that transfers to unseen objects.

entry.title: Position: AI Agents in Scientific Teams Should Be Studied as Human-Agent Systems

author.name: Patrick Emami, Sameera Horawalavithana, Truc Nguyen, Gihan Panapitiya, Bruno Jacob, Siddhisanket Raskar, Saumya Sinha, Jared D. Willard, Andrew Glaws, Nithin Somasekharan, Ling Yue, Brian Lu, Shaowu Pan, Jason Eisner

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that autonomous AI scientist systems should be studied as human-agent systems, with the human-agent pair as the unit of analysis, rather than purely as autonomous capabilities. Using literature review and case studies, the authors highlight near-term risks such as reduced diversity of scientific inquiry when agent deployment ignores team dynamics.

entry.title: Beyond Pass@k: Measuring Reliability and Security of Agentic Code Generation

author.name: Jiajun Jiang, Sharon Zheng, Natan Vidra, Spurthi Setty

entry.summary: Shows that popular coding-agent benchmarks misapply the standard pass at k estimator by setting the sample count to the number of unit tests in a single submission rather than the number of independent rollouts. The authors prove the error by counterexample, propose reliability at k with correct rollout-level accounting, and demonstrate that the mistake can inflate reported scores by very large margins in synthetic settings.

entry.title: Individual Disempowerment through an Advice Channel: Control Loss when Influence is Endogenous

author.name: Adam M. Oberman

entry.summary: Formalizes the classic AI boxing intuition by making the fraction of human behavior that follows AI advice a state in a Markov decision process that the advisor itself influences. The analysis shows that greater reliance weakly reduces every monotone measure of human power, and that an oracle optimizing per-round approval will cultivate dependence beyond a computable patience threshold.

entry.title: Funnel of Thoughts: Efficient Test-Time Scaling via Early Voting and Rollout Pruning

author.name: Chanhee Park, Sungbin Han, Jeongho Yoon, Seongtae Hong, Heuiseok Lim

entry.summary: Funnel of Thoughts reduces the cost of majority voting over many reasoning rollouts by pruning trajectories early, exploiting the observation across many recorded reasoning traces that unproductive paths reveal themselves through repeated hesitation markers. The method reportedly preserves the accuracy of 32-sample voting while roughly halving attention compute.

entry.title: Translating finite-domain integer constraint models to CP/SMT/ILP/PB/SAT solvers with CPMpy

author.name: Tias Guns, Ignace Bleukx, Hendrik Bierlee, Jo Devriendt, Emilio Gamba, Orestis Lomis, Wout Piessens, Thomas Sergeys, Dimos Tsouros, Wout Vanroose, H\'el\`ene Verhaeghe

entry.summary: Describes how the CPMpy modeling library translates high-level finite-domain integer constraint models into many lower-level solver formalisms including CP, SMT linear integer arithmetic, ILP, pseudo-Boolean and MaxSAT. This lets practitioners compare solving technologies on the same declarative model without rewriting it.

entry.title: $D^{2}R^{2}$: Discrete Diffusion with Regulation Reinforcement for Single-Cell Perturbation Prediction

author.name: Ninghan Fan, Qi Liu, Xunuo Zhu, Yukai Sun, Luyuan Chen, Xuheng Zhou, Yuetian Du, Ming Kong, Xiaojun Zhu, Jie Liu, Zhan Zhou, Qiang Zhu

entry.summary: Reformulates single-cell perturbation response prediction as gene-wise progressive generation using a masked discrete diffusion model over ordinal expression tokens, with a regulation-based reinforcement signal guiding generation order. Later gene predictions condition on earlier ones rather than emitting an entire profile at once.

entry.title: A survey of AI-generated voices and their detection

author.name: Chengzhe Sun, Tianle Yang, Siwei Lyu

entry.summary: A comprehensive survey of AI voice generation and synthetic-voice detection, covering technical foundations, current state of the art detectors, datasets and the specific difficulties of audio deepfakes relative to images and video. Motivated by real voice-cloning fraud and impersonation incidents.

entry.title: ATLAS: Scaffold-Free Algorithm Synthesis by LLMs via Embedding-Guided Quality-Diversity Search

author.name: Danial Yazdani, Mohammad Nabi Omidvar, Yuan Sun, Maksud Ibrahimov, Xiaodong Li

entry.summary: ATLAS lets an LLM synthesize entire optimization algorithms rather than filling a component slot in a human-designed scaffold, using embedding-guided quality-diversity search to keep the population of designs varied. It separately detects execution, interface and feasibility failures and applies targeted error handling to cope with the enlarged, riskier search space.

entry.title: THESIS-MoE: Trainable Hierarchical Extraction and SteerIng of Sycophancy in Mixture-of-Experts

author.name: Kareem Hassani, Chaymaa Abbas, Lama Mawlawi, Mariette Awad

entry.summary: Introduces conditional sycophancy steering for Mixture-of-Experts models, building a shared contrastive direction from prompts with and without a stated user belief and intervening within expert computations only when sycophantic behavior is detected. This avoids the knowledge degradation caused by uniform unconditional steering.

entry.title: KV-Rescue: Recovering Reasoning Language Model KV Eviction Loss via Stepwise Interleaving

author.name: Minsoo Cheong, Woosang Lim, Vincent-Daniel Yun, Sungjoo Yoo

entry.summary: Diagnoses accuracy loss from KV-cache eviction in reasoning models as an information gap rather than a capability gap, noting that an evicted large model and a full-context small model make complementary errors. KV-Rescue exploits this with a training-free interleaving of stepwise decoding between the two to recover much of the lost accuracy and avoid runaway degeneration.

entry.title: Dear Algo: A Precision-First Agentic Intent Layer for Unified Search and Recommendation

author.name: Rui Wang, Jiazhou Wang, Zheng Wei, Chenglin Lu, Fangcheng Sun, Ivy Sun, Jin Sun, Hui Geng, Lillian Zhang, Chao Yang, Lei Chen, Shahin Sefati, Reem Helou, Joe Zhou, Babak Shakibi, Yiyi Pan, Bi Xue, Hong Yan, Shujian Bu

entry.summary: Describes a deployed product feature on Threads where open-ended natural-language requests steer subsequent feed recommendations, via an agentic intent layer that compiles explicit, inferred, negative and compound intent into an executable retrieval plan. Evaluation uses a precision-first objective with a blinded audit of hundreds of requests.

entry.title: TRCA: Transition-wise Rubric Credit Assignment for Long-horizon LLM Agents

author.name: Huan Zhang, Mingju Chen, Dongxu Zhou, Can Lv, Heng Chang, Sen Cui, Faguo Wu, Shiji Zhou

entry.summary: TRCA derives step-level training signal for long-horizon LLM agents directly from action-induced state transitions, scoring each transition with evidence, execution, and invalidity rubrics rather than relying on learned process reward models or rare successful trajectories. This addresses the cold-start problem where anchor-based credit assignment fails because early RL produces almost no successes. It is a cheap alternative to process reward modeling.

entry.title: Forward Pass Domain Adaptation (Without Cross-Layer Backpropagation)

author.name: Rivaan Patil, Simon Dennis, Hao Guo, Kevin Shabahang

entry.summary: Forward-Pass-Only training adapts language models without backpropagating through the model body, relying on the empirical observation that at late layers the output-layer prediction error approximates the true gradient with cosine similarity around 0.5. The authors report roughly three times the throughput of standard fine-tuning at about forty percent less peak memory, with off-domain benchmarks staying within seed noise, plus a quick per-layer diagnostic for when the approximation holds. It is a cheap domain-adaptation recipe.

entry.title: HarmProfile: Characterizing Harmful Distributions in Frontier LLMs

author.name: Zhouyuan Ma, Yutao Wu, Hanxun Huang, Xiang Zheng, Xiao Liu, Yixin Cao, Zuxuan Wu, Xingjun Ma, Yu-Gang Jiang

entry.summary: HarmProfile treats harmful generation as an object of study rather than merely an attack success signal, assembling a content-centric dataset of frontier model misbehavior across harm categories and model families to define a model-level harmful-output risk profile. The premise is that a model's risk can be characterized from the content it produces when it fails. This shifts safety evaluation from binary jailbreak rates toward distributional harm profiling.

entry.title: Mitigating Rubric Interference in LLM Judges via On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: Dingyao Yu, Tong Zhang, Yutao Mou, Yunxiao Zhang, Wei Ye, Shikun Zhang

entry.summary: Documents rubric interference in LLM judges: when multiple checklist criteria are graded in a single pass, the verdict on one rubric shifts depending on which others are present, with only about a third of samples fully consistent. The authors build a probing framework using expansion, subsetting, reordering, and noise injection, and mitigate the effect with on-policy self-distillation.

entry.title: Which Question Is Your Attention Metric Answering? Attention Rows as Compositional Data

author.name: Marios Papamichalis, Regina Ruane

entry.summary: Points out that attention rows are compositional data dominated by a sink token, so comparisons using cosine similarity, JS divergence, or entropy depend on whether the sink is kept or dropped and renormalized. Across ten pretrained models, between 17 and 47 percent of head-similarity verdicts flip with this unreported convention, and a well-known BERT head-clustering result is shown to be an artifact.

entry.title: Left-Branching Transformers Excel at Right-Branching Languages: Data Shapes Word Order Preferences in Language Models

author.name: Varvara Arzt, Allan Hanbury, Terra Blevins

entry.summary: Compares word order preferences of decoder-only language models across 192 artificial languages plus typologically diverse natural languages. Models prefer left-branching structures in artificial settings, contradicting both human learning biases and natural-language universals, while on real languages an SVO advantage emerges with scale that tracks resource level and data quality rather than word order itself.

entry.title: Ventor-QTest: Threat-Model-Driven Verification of Vendor-Hosted LLM APIs

author.name: Xiangfan Wu, Zonghao Ying, Huiyu Wu, Xing Zheng, Huangsheng Cheng, Xiaorong Shi, Jing Guo

entry.summary: Ventor-QTest formalizes vendor-hosted model serving as a stochastic routing process and provides a black-box audit that needs no logprobs: it repeatedly queries frozen constrained contexts, reconstructs output distributions from text counts, and reports a bias-corrected average fidelity loss, complemented by a long-sequence component. The goal is verifying whether third-party APIs actually serve the advertised open-weight model at claimed quality.

entry.title: Palmyra x6 Technical Report: An Agentic, Tool-Use Model Post-Trained via Anchored Supervised Fine-Tuning

author.name: Peng Du, Kiran Kamble, Rakshith Vasudev, Zhizhuo Yang, Rohith Nadimpally, Arjun Krishna, Waseem Alshikh, Daniel M. Bikel

entry.summary: The Palmyra x6 technical report describes post-training a mixture-of-experts base into an enterprise agentic tool-use model using anchored supervised fine-tuning on just 626 verified synthetic tool-use trajectories, one epoch, low learning rate, and a KL anchor to the frozen base, optimized with a Muon and Adam hybrid. It reports the top BFCL Core score in its comparison cohort and the highest six-benchmark mean.

entry.title: Diagnosing Dense Same-Class Attribute Misbinding in Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yuanzhi Xu, Qian Gao, Jun Fan, Guohui Ding, Zhenyu Yang, Yuteng Xiao, Sixue Lin

entry.summary: Formalizes dense same-class attribute misbinding, where a vision-language model correctly sees objects and attributes in a crowded scene but attaches an attribute to the wrong instance of the same class, and introduces InstaBind-Lite, a controlled benchmark of 524 images with curated same-class groups and multi-level questions. Standard VQA accuracy and hallucination metrics both miss this transfer error.

entry.title: Don't Drop the BATON: Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation via Agentic Subtask Exploration and Transition-aware Memory

author.name: Bingxin Xu, Yuzhang Shang, Emilio Ferrara

entry.summary: BATON targets long-horizon manipulation where an LLM agent orchestrates a frozen vision-language-action policy, arguing that whole-task test-time exploration costs scale multiplicatively with the number of stages. It proposes agentic per-subtask exploration plus a transition-aware memory so that adaptation learned in one stage accounts for how it constrains the next.

entry.title: Training and Evaluating Ethical Reinforcement Learning Agents on Per-Episode Distributions

author.name: Prabhjyot Singh, Majid Ghasemi, Mark Crowley

entry.summary: Compares four ways of instilling ethical behavior in RL agents on the Craftax survival benchmark, including scalar penalties with termination, multi-objective weight sweeps, an adaptive Lagrangian constraint, and a non-compensatory per-episode utility under expected scalarized returns. The central point is that averaging hides concentrated harm, since an agent can look ethical on average while committing severe violations in a few episodes.

entry.title: When Does the Best Sampling Temperature Rise with the Budget? Sufficient Conditions for Pass@k

author.name: Changsu Jeong (Independent Researcher)

entry.summary: Gives a population-level sufficient condition explaining why the temperature maximizing pass@k tends to be low at small sampling budgets and higher at large budgets, even though for any single fixed task the optimal temperature is budget-independent. The condition concerns monotonicity of a conditional log-success response across a task difficulty distribution.

entry.title: Online Convex Optimization with Dueling Feedback

author.name: Yiyang Lu, Hareshkumar Jadav, Mohammad Pedramfar, Ranveer Singh, Vaneet Aggarwal

entry.summary: Studies adversarial online convex optimization when the learner sees only a binary preference between two queried points, giving a reduction that converts dueling comparisons into approximate gradients so standard first-order methods apply. This yields first-of-kind static, adaptive, and dynamic regret bounds of order T to the three-quarters, improved under smoothness and strong convexity.

entry.title: MiNO: Cotangent-bundle propagator learning for PDEs

author.name: Gnankan Landry Regis N'guessan, Bum Jun Kim

entry.summary: MiNO learns the PDE propagator itself as a phase and amplitude in phase space, using the eikonal equation for phase and the transport equation for amplitude and recovering solutions by an oscillatory integral, rather than learning solution fields or solution maps. The motivation is a regularity gap: transported discontinuities are nonsmooth while the rule that moves them can be smooth, so sharp fronts and caustics become learnable.

entry.title: SchurQuant: Groupwise Discrete Optimization for Layer-Wise LLM Quantization

author.name: Gunjun Lee, Sehwan Son, Younjoo Lee, Byungjun Kim, Jung Ho Ahn

entry.summary: SchurQuant is a backprop-free post-training quantization method that analytically accounts for how the remaining unquantized weights can absorb error, using Schur-complement curvature, and jointly refits scales and integer codes. It reports accuracy gains over GPTQ-style baselines in the difficult 2-bit regime.

entry.title: The Limits of Binding in Dual Encoders

author.name: Kin Ian Lo

entry.summary: Gives a mathematical account of why CLIP-style dual encoders fail at attribute binding, proving that the relevant idealized axioms are satisfiable so any impossibility requires extra hypotheses, then establishing three concrete obstructions including an exact exponential decay of swap margin with role-nesting depth. Clarifies which binding failures are necessary versus contingent.

entry.title: Learning to Price with Persuasion

author.name: Maria-Florina Balcan, Tejas Pagare, Karan Singh

entry.summary: Studies the sample complexity of jointly designing a menu of quality-price pairs and an information signaling scheme when the seller does not know buyers' prior beliefs about taste distributions. Covers both batch data settings and provides learning-theoretic guarantees for revenue-maximizing joint mechanism and information design.

entry.title: SimpleOPD: Simple Tokenizer-Agnostic On-Policy Distillation for Long-Context Reasoning

author.name: Haonan He, Haodi Lei, Yun Luo, Haoran Zhang, Shunkai Zhang, Yizhuo Li, Shengji Tang, Zhilin Wang, Runzhe Zhan, Lei Bai, Ganqu Cui, Fangchen Yu, Yafu Li, Peng Ye, Ning Ding, Yu Cheng

entry.summary: SimpleOPD makes on-policy distillation work across mismatched tokenizers by aligning only tokens spanning identical text and operating in a shared text space, while addressing response-length explosion, distribution mismatch, and training instability when transferring from a long-context reasoning teacher to short-context students. Demonstrated on proof-reasoning transfer.

entry.title: Reading Between The Lines: Modeling and Evaluating Behavioral Realism in Legal Simulation

author.name: Divya Vetticaden, Arya Gupta, Julian Nyarko, Megan Ma

entry.summary: Presents a deposition simulator driven by controllable witness personas plus an evaluation framework that separates behavioral realism from pedagogical usefulness, tested with adversarial probes and blinded attorney judgments. Attorneys could not systematically distinguish simulated from real testimony.

entry.title: OvDSGG: End-to-End Open-Vocabulary Dynamic Scene Graph Generation

author.name: John Helsby, Yi Yang, Bodo Rosenhahn, Michael Ying Yang

entry.summary: Introduces an end-to-end framework for open-vocabulary dynamic scene graph generation, recognizing subject-predicate-object triplets in video beyond a fixed training vocabulary without the multi-stage LLM pipelines used by prior open-vocabulary methods. It targets long-tailed rare concepts at lower inference cost.

entry.title: UC-VLM: Consistency-Driven Learning for AI-Generated Image Detection with Vision-Language Large Models

author.name: Lei Tan, Shuwei Li, Mohan Kankanhalli, Robby T. Tan

entry.summary: A multi-stage framework that trains vision-language models for AI-generated image detection using only binary labels, automatically selecting effective instruction variants and adding a visual discrimination objective for low-level forensic cues. It avoids reliance on hand-crafted prompts and human-written rationales.

entry.title: Revisiting Classifier-Free Guidance Methods in Latent Diffusion Models

author.name: Artem Sergievskii, Artyom Turevich, Sergey Kastryulin

entry.summary: The authors re-evaluate eight training-free guidance techniques derived from classifier-free guidance on two modern open-weight rectified-flow transformers, using compositional alignment benchmarks rather than image-quality metrics alone. They report that no method consistently beats plain classifier-free guidance under a fixed protocol.

entry.title: MM-BEV: Enhancing Timeliness by Computing Where and When it Matters

author.name: Liangkai Liu, Kang G. Shin

entry.summary: MM-BEV makes multimodal bird's-eye-view perception real-time by allocating compute according to safety relevance, doing mandatory full processing only for objects within braking distance or short time-to-collision. It also exploits input sparsity and cross-modal timing misalignment rather than uniformly compressing detectors.

entry.title: ReRef-3D: A Benchmark for Spatial Referring Expression-Guided 3D Scene Rearrangement

author.name: Mary Lynn Martin, Yifei Zhang, Martha Palmer, Maria Leonor Pacheco

entry.summary: ReRef-3D is a benchmark of nearly 34,000 language instructions over about 1,000 synthetic scenes that requires resolving spatial referring expressions, including one-hop and two-hop references, into valid object placements. Evaluation inserts the predicted placement, recomputes relations, and tests both relation satisfaction and physical validity, and fine-tuned 3D language models solve only 22 to 68 percent.

entry.title: What gives you away: how LLMs form opinions of you

author.name: Cat McGee

entry.summary: Follows up on findings that linear probes can extract user attributes such as age, gender, education, and socioeconomic status from model activations after a single message, and that intervening on those representations changes model behavior. The author investigates which subtle stylistic cues, such as casing, emoji use, slang, and syntactic complexity, drive the model's inferred user profile.

entry.title: Teaching Everyone to Fish for Tokens

author.name: Nathan Lambert

entry.summary: An essay distinguishing truly open-source language models, which ship full training recipes, data, and code, from open-weight releases that provide only weights and inference code, and comparing the ecosystem dynamics to open-source operating systems. It argues weights are transient while recipes are the durable public good, drawing on the author's experience building fully open models.

entry.title: Local and Global Regimes of Geometric Complexity in Language Model Representations

author.name: Arwa Osman, Marco Baroni, Iuri Macocco

entry.summary: Shows that intrinsic dimensionality estimates of language model representations depend systematically on how many unique final tokens a probing dataset contains, with the ordering between low- and high-diversity conditions reversing at a predictable scale. Derives an exact parameter-free formula for the reversal point, implying many published ID comparisons may reflect dataset construction rather than linguistic structure.

entry.title: AnchorBench: A Multi-Pathway Benchmark for the Anchoring Effect in LLMs

author.name: Yiderigun Borjigin, Alexander Hermann, Christian Cyron, Roland Aydin

entry.summary: A benchmark for anchoring bias in LLMs that varies the pathway through which the anchor is presented and explicitly distinguishes irrelevant from plausible anchors, tested across fourteen open-weight and frontier models. It finds anchoring effects are strong and depend systematically on pathway and relevance.

entry.title: Risk-Adaptive Edge--Cloud Visual Reasoning for Communication-Efficient Autonomous Driving

author.name: Meng Ma, Shuyang Li, Naigang Wang, Ruimin Ke

entry.summary: Proposes a risk-adaptive split between an onboard vision-language model and a cloud VLM for autonomous driving, invoking cloud reasoning only when local hazard assessment warrants it while keeping control and emergency braking local. CARLA experiments report matching periodic cloud access on success rate with far less communication.

entry.title: FLEET: Token-Based Feature Extraction for Event Camera-based Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Tristan Gottwald, Maximilian Schier, Melanie Schaller, Bodo Rosenhahn

entry.summary: FLEET is a tokenization-based feature extractor for event camera streams intended for reinforcement learning control policies, avoiding the CNN practice of aggregating asynchronous events into dense grids. It decouples compute from sensor resolution and does not require pretraining on trajectory data, better preserving temporal precision.

entry.title: GenRouter: Unified Workflow Routing for Agentic Image Generation

author.name: Harold Haodong Chen, Zhiyu Hou, Wen-Jie Shu, Weilin Ruan, Yingjie Xu, Litao Guo, Ying-Cong Chen

entry.summary: GenRouter introduces workflow routing for agentic image generation, standardizing diverse pipelines into a shared canvas formulation and then routing each user request to an appropriately sized workflow. The motivation is compute mismatch, where simple prompts are otherwise pushed through heavy retrieval and reasoning pipelines.

entry.title: SplatGuide: Geometric Priors from 3D Gaussians for Pose-Free Novel View Synthesis

author.name: Yejun Zhang, Zihan Wang, Xu Ji, Yihao Wang, Yuxin Hou, Junyuan Fang, Juho-Matti Kilpel\"ainen, Arno Solin, Hamed Rezazadegan Tavakoli, Esa Rahtu, Juho Kannala
